Here's something you should know about Jet Set Radio. It's old. You can tell it's old. It's blatantly obvious that this game is from an older era of gaming. The controls, whether you use a gamepad or keyboard and mouse, are clunky. It's like trying to drive a tank that someone put on roller blade and it's certainly not helped by the camera's insane decisions with how it wants to move and track you.
But, despite the control issues, it is a very fun game. Because of how hard it is to actually do what you want to do, completing a level is quite satisfying. The main appeal of this game, however, is its style. This game is utterly unique in its presentation and art design. It's cell shading manages to keep such an old game looking rather fresh, sort of like an indie made game, actually. It won't amaze you in graphical impressiveness, but it certainly won't offend either. It's style, in regards to the world it creates and the individual levels, is off the charts. You can feel like this game is trying to win you over in sheer style, if anything.
The last thing to mention: The soundtrack. I hate to have a different opinion here, but I did not find the soundtrack that great. Now, I did find it satisfactory. It was varied and interesting enough to keep me from begrudging any particular track, but none of them managed to stand out for me and leave any real impression.
Conclusion: I don't regret buying this game. It's cheap at full price. On sale, this game can do you no real wrong. If you'd like something funky to break the mold from just about anything else in your Steam library, this might just be the game for you

Chivalry is first or third person medieval combat simulator...or so it is advertised. You have four different classes that duel it out together on various game modes: Team Objective, Free-for-All, Team Deathmatch, Duel, etc. The four classes are Archer, who uses bows, crossbows, or javelins to attack from a distance; Men-at-Arms who have light armor and simple melee weapons, but utilizes a special dodge to avoid incoming swings; Vanguard who uses pole-arms to poke at the enemy from a relatively safe distance; and the Knight who uses heavy armor and large shields to bash through enemy lines. The game is setup beautifully, in which class diversity and support can equal strong team plays and wins. The only problem is that the developers of this game discovered a secret fighting technique from the Dark Ages, called the broken back. Players have abused this system to the point that the game is really just a joke, and the developers have done nothing to stop it. Players run around jumping in heavy armor, and then breaking their backs by aiming up at the sky in a ridiculous manner to avoid enemy swings. This is goes completely against what the game is advertised to do, which is to "...seeks to capture the experience of truly being on a medieval battlefield." Yeah, that sentence can be found on the store page, is a full on lie. The game is broken, lag rules the battlefield, and the dumber the technique and less skilled looking you look, the better you will do...guaranteed.
-Can offer some funny, random moments.
-When playing at low levels you get a better feel for true medieval combat.
-Can be incredibly fun with friends.
-Broken gameplay and fighting system.
-The community is terrible, as you'll find more d.icks online than for Harambe.
-Lag wins battles, not the player.
I give this game 2 mugs of ale out of 5. The game in practice is fun, and could be something to rival the Mount and Blade series. However, by not fixing the issue it takes the skill and fun of medieval fighting out of the game. To the developers, I suggest removing the crouch feature, and possibly even jumping, or at the very least make it much more clunky and slow. Until these issues get fixed, I suggest buying Mount and Blade instead of this game.

Vangaurd = Uses long polearms and greatswords and dons mail armour he also has a special charge ability (front line force good for dealing high damage)
Man At Arms = Uses one handed maces, swords, daggers, and axes and dons leather armour he has a special dodge ability (good for harrasing the enemy and trolling)
Archer = wields ranged bows, crossbows, and sling to throw projectiles and insults from afar he has a special backstab bonus (good ranged class and best insults).
The game's main mode is an objective based map where there is an attacking and defending team. The objectives can range from battering down a castle gate to♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥and pillaging a village but it also has last team standing, TDM, and FFA. The game have big design issues:

It's not terrible and I can see the reasons why someone could like or even love this game, It's a British attempt to make an jRPG-style game, published a year before the Bioware's Jade Empire. Both these games threw away the infamous turn-based combat system and are basically action jRPGs. Both were published for Xbox and have some gameplay similarities, like autospawning enemies and grinding. I have to admit that Sudeki's magic system is more interesting than JEmpire's and graphics are fine for 2004, but, unfortunately, in other aspects the game is much worse. At first I was charmed, but after 10+ hours (half of the game) I got bored and annoyed.
Music - unlike JE, Sudeki has very boring and generic music with no distinguishing style. Not a single track is worth recommending and they do little to nothing for the overall atmosphere.
Voice acting - while most of the sound effects are decent, voice acting is laughably terrible.
Walking simulator - most RPGs have some annoying walking simulator elements, but this game made it something unique. I think I spend more than 15% of this game pointlessly walking from one point to another while doing "bring me X" quests or getting to a specific merchant or altar. And since most of these areas were already known and additionally I had to face randomly spawning enemies - it was exhausting.
Portals - the worst portal systems I've ever met. Sure, most non-sandbox RPGs don't even allow you to go back to previous areas after finishing a plot chapter and it's awesome, that you can do that in Sudeki, but using a portal always takes a minute of boring cutscenes and is almost pointless, since the portals are always in the middle of nowhere and are very far away from most important areas (another walking simulator element).
Battles in the 2nd half of the game take too long - most of the midgame-lategame battles are very long, don't show anything specially new and exciting and are just annoying, especially since enemies are showing up in waves what makes the AOE spells less effective. Some fighting scenes took 5-10 minutes of repeating one decently tactic. And since you mostly can't avoid the randomly spawning enemies in certain areas, most of the fighting scenes brought nothing to the game's plot.
Overall plot is boringly cliche - while a lot of jRPGs (and even American Jade Empire) can do a great job entwining generic threads and some unique ideas and Sudeki avoids some of the most obvious concepts (for example: no fake-ending, no burning the family village, main villain has no "real form"), there is literally not a single original idea in the entire game, especially since...
Boring fantasy setting - ...the entire game's world is just Another Fantasy World with no main theme beside "good vs evil". It kinda feels like an RPG Maker game made by a 18yo who decided to ignore plot by reducing it to minimum and focus only on graphics, cool mechanics or useless cutscenes or animations (like climbing on a high wall aka Pressing One Button or Portals) and walking to make the game longer. And also...
Game takes away your PCs - The plot for whatever reason mostly does not allow the player to control all his or her party members. Instead the game constantly takes away some of the Player Characters and forces us to walk solo or with two characters, especially when fighting with bosses. It even teases us showing us areas, which the characters we control can't enter, but gives us clues, that other PCs can go there. This tease means to encourage us to return to the same area 1-2-3 hours later to finally see, what was this previously unavailable secret...
I think I'm done with this review but I'll end with a quick reminder - it's not a terrible game, it's not even bad, however even though I spent 20+ hours playing it and I bought it in a bundle for like 0.40$ it is true I was enjoying myself while playing this for maybe 8-10 hours. The rest of it was either boring, repetitive or just poorly executed. I don't mind playing a game 8 hours long, but if I have to force myself to endure another 10 hours, to get this 8 hours of decent gameplay - I don't think it's worth it.
EDIT: Also, the camera in some locations is just terrible, and the game does not know what to do when an enemy pushes our PC to a wall - we can't see  the enemy at all and we have to defend blindly.

Unfortunately, that's about the only good thing about it.  Here are just a few of the issues I've noted with this game.
1.) The story is confusing.
2.) The combat is unfair in a number of ways.
A.) You have 4 characters.  Two of them are melee fighters and control exactly the same. You have a combo meter, and can pull of combos through a series of heavy and light attacks.  To successfully make a combo, you must press your next button when the next circle in the meter is lit up.  Miss it, and your subsequent attacks are slow and clunky.  But sometimes, the circle lights up for a very short time, or not at all.  Your other two characters are ranged attackers and, again, control the same...i.e. HORRIBLY!  Even though the view is of a third person perspective in normal gameplay, during which your characters movement is perfectly natural and fine, when entering combat, you are forced into a first person view, and suddenly your character turns like a damn tank!
B.) There are no invincibility frames, so if enemies gang up on one of your characters and corner you, you'll probably lose health pretty damn fast.
C.) Enemies respawn too damn often.  Specifically, if enemies spawn in one portion of a particular area, and you defeat them, explore another portion of the same area, then return to the first portion, the enemies will respawn!  I can understand them doing this if you went to an entirely different area and came back, but not while you're in the same damn area!
3.) Even putting my love for Doctor Who aside, the voice acting by anyone in this game not named Tom Baker is dry at best, but for the most part grating.
4.) The camera can zoom in and out and adjust horizontally, but not vertically.
5.) Your characters can not use magic abilities if you're not in combat, particularly annoying as one of your characters is a healer.
6.) Speaking of healing, there's a 4-slot Quickslot system in the game.  You're supposed to be able to go into the menu, go to the item section, and highlight an item and assign it to a slot by pressing the corresponding button.  The only trouble is half the time it doesn't work properly, and it's easier to just press Y (on an XBox controller) during combat to find an item you want that way.
If you're a fan of Doctor Who or of Tom Baker in general, this game might be worth looking at just to hear him in it, but other than that, I can find no redeeming features about this game.

Poor planning, poor execution, poor communication, poor problem solving after the fact. For those of you that say "go play on private servers" that isn't a solution, it's a band-aid.

With servers finally accessible, within an hour multiple bugs are present and the community provides feedback. One of the issues is extreme building lag when placing objects. Friday: devs put out a hotfix before leaving for the weekend to attempt to correct the building lag. What actually happened? Building lag was unfixed, but in their attempt to fix it the building/snapping system was completely broken. No one could build stairs or snap foundations or walls together all weekend. Tons of meme posts popped up for work arounds like stacking boxes or attaching shelves to the walls in order to get to various parts of their base. The super high jumping spear exploit was inadvertently readded into the game, being able to fly up a cliff into anyone's base while they can't build or replace their doors makes for interesting events.

This game is all about ambiance and exploration.  It's a relaxing boat ride through a world that's empty but alive.

I personally liked the game very much - the art was pretty solid, the music was appropriate to make you feel alone. The area you are in is manageable and to be honest it doesn't feel too big (except near the end when you are trying to track down those last few pesky secrets.
The cons are that its short, the building textures aren't amazing up close, the models are smooth but the graphics are nothing to write home about.  My biggest complaint, though, is the climbing.  It's very tedious especially after the first few buildings.  It just feels unecessarily slow.
Overall a good game to get lost on if you have time to kill or want to relax with a story/ exploration game.

Overall, Submerged is a decent game. Here are some thoughts:
Many of the reviews refer to this game as a platformer. This is absolutely not a platformer. You don't do any traditional jumping in this game. You simply direct the main character from ledge to ledge with no timing or danger involved.
The game appears more beautiful in screenshots and trailers than it actually is. In reality, you will spend the majority of game time hugging a wall that is simply a repeated texture of windows and concrete.
I beat the game in 2 hours. There were more collectibles available for me to find, but I didn't feel compelled in the slightest to find them. Simply finding the main items of the game tells the minimal story. I applaud the developers for making a game that doesn't force itself to continue going for the sake of padding game time. The two hours I had was fun, but if it dragged much longer I would have ended up hating the experience.
I would not pay $20 for this game. I purchased it on sale ($7.49) an I am happy with it at that price point.

I do enjoy this game but as I'm using an AMD CPU I'm afflicted by a serious issue present in the UE4 engine. Fixes exist both from Epic and from other development studios on getting over the issue in UE4 for AMD but unfortunately Funcom seem either unwilling or unable to fix this problem. I've tried to get the game working properly with sound, I've even helped others get their game at least halfway functional but it's all for nought. Honestly give this game a miss if you're on an AMD CPU, there's a good chance you'll be affected by the problems and they don't seem willing to fix them despite still advertising the product as being AMD compatible.
Issues AMD CPU users face;
- Freezing on inventory and crafting screens.
- Continuous unavoidable stuttering movement and freezes while travelling, fighting, harvesting or even simply standing still, effectively rendering the game unplayable.
- Crashing when minimising or alt-tabbing.
The only way to resolve these issues is to completely and utterly disable all sounds in the game by editing the settings ini files, deleting a DLL and setting all volume sliders to 0 or purchasing a soundcard instead of using onboard sound (which you shouldn't have to do for a single game). If you're deaf and using AMD this is the game for you, if you're not deaf and you don't care about sound then yeah this game is pretty great, if you're like the rest (that is the majority) of us that actually like or need sound in a SURVIVAL game, so you don't you know, get eaten by the local wildlife or trolled by other players, then skip this and go with something else.
If funcom correct the AMD problems, I may change my recommendation but as of the time of posting this review they still haven't fixed them so I really cannot recommend the game.

Definitely recommended if you like driving related games.  This is one of those simple games that has a very addictive playstyle.  So what do you do in ATS?  Do you race?  Drift through mud and smoke your tires?  Run over pedestrians?  No.  You transport cargo from point A to B and earn a profit.  Sounds boring, right?  Somehow, it's not.  If you want to get into more of the business side of trucking, then you can start your own company, hire drivers, buy more rigs, upgrade them, and earn a profit.
The driving is more on the realistic side of playing, but not so much that casual players would be intimidated by it.  Don't want to shift gears?  Fine, go with an automatic transmission and worry only about accelerating and braking.  Want to spice it up?  Do a manual transmission, 18 speed gearbox and try to stop on a hill, then get it going again without stalling out.  Turn on speed limits so traffic tickets pile up on you, or, turn them off when they get annoying.
Graphics....well, the foliage needs work - I think everyone agrees that is a little dated, but everything else looks good.  And the sky....oh wow, the sky - it's fantastic.  It actually feels refreshing to gaze at the sky when the sun is just peaking over the horizon from an all night drive.  The cities are well-built and feel alive.  I could go on and on, but you get my drift...buy it; buy it now.
Rated 9.5/10.
P.S. This game caused me to shell out $350+ for a steering wheel + shifter.  I had zero intentions of ever buying one before this game...especially one that expensive.  That has to mean something.

I already wrote a review for the first game of the trilogy, so here I will just say how it has evolved.
- The lore is still the same so as great as the first one. The exploration system was greatly improved.
- The storyline is a little bit into pieces - the main story is not very visible, the whole game comes up as a succession of anecdotes. However, these "anecdotes" are great if considered alone. I cried.
- Gameplay makes your playing style more strategic due to limitation of resources.
- More characters than in ME1 and all with deep, unique personalities. Very good point for this game.
- More diversity for the secondary missions, though there are less than in the first one.
- The game goes on even after the main story has ended, which is interesting - for example you can talk to your crew and have some feedback on your last actions.
- More romance choices than in ME1. A lot more. And I support that.
Overall, I would recommend ME2 to anyone who tried ME1. It's worth it!

Besides lots of bugs which I reported, the main issue with this game is that they use a third-party UI called "Coherent UI" which seems to have lots of issues. In fact, the devs of Overworld insist that you have a crazy-high graphics score of 1,500 at this benchmark site
or the Overworld devs simply won't take any responsibility for the game lag, mouse lag, and general heavy scripts that weight down this game. The real problem here is that when I go to a completely BLACK SCREEN (fog of war on the map) on an area of the map where there are NO GRAPHICS the game is choking and has serious lag in multiple ways. This means it's not a GPU problem; it's a coding issue with scripts and how heavy they are. I have 16 GB of RAM on this machine and play lots of RTS like AOE, Sins Of A Solar Empire, LOTR, Galactic Empires, and others all without any problem. Overworld has the worst performance out of all RTS games I have every played in the last 20 years, and that is a criticism I don't give lightly.
The real issue is the attitude of the devs on the forums when these type of complaints are leveled. They use comments like "we will optimize later" and "we can't do anything about that" and "it's your graphics card" and instead they should be looking at how to lighten scripts for off-screen activity, and make their own UI instead of trusting an outside "Coherent UI" which they have no control over.
The cursor is important for selecting many things, but the lag makes it impossible to do many things, including the fact that some information about minions is impossible to see unless you're hovering directly on them (while they are running around LoL). Add to that heavy scripts for everything OFF SCREEN. Even when you go to a black screen (fog of war) part of the map, the game is still choking, and trying to use the UI in general is slow and chokes.
Then there are real bugs, even in 2017 after the game has supposedly been "stable" for a while. I get weary of bogus warnings from the narrator, who keeps saying that a minion can't find food or its lair, but this minion is invisible, and there are pigs all over the dungeon, and plenty of lairs. The narrator keeps saying a beastmaster is mad because it can't be paid, and I can actually see this minion, so I drop it on gold and it keeps running around angry, because the game AI is choking and the beastmaster somehow forgot how to get his gold for years, and will never work again, because the AI is broken and thinks that minion never got paid, even with 80,000 gold in my dungeon laying around for him.
Then there are gameplay issues that were not well-thought-out. For example, there is a payday every cycle, where the intelligent minions get paid. Every payday all of the intelligent minions leave their posts, stop working and go get gold. Why do they have to leave their posts? Well, unlike most other RTS games, there is no "automatic deposit" and your intelligent minions will wander around to some place where you have some gold, even if it is all the way on the other side of your dungeon. But there is no way to put gold on a specific place on the map, it's all randomly placed and you have no real control over where your gold is, even with vaults strategically placed, because every time you place gold it's randomly allocated, and when you spend gold, it zaps it randomly from all vaults. This "randomness" is nice in a way because you don't have to micromanage it. But it's terrible at payday because all your intelligent minions will wander around to the farthest parts of the dungeon to get paid. So this issue is that if you have intelligent minions far from the random place gold might be, they have to walk to the gold that exists. So you could have a ton of gold, but no way to pay intelligent minions that are far from the core. If you try to set up a sub base that is far from the core, you can do everything right, but the minions will still try to walk to the core to get paid (unless you have your gold maxed out and a vault right by them, which is hard to keep current). For example, if your workers find some gold and place it locally on the edge of your dungeon, that's where your intelligent minions have to walk to get paid, or if you spend money, it randomly pulls it from wherever, so there's no way to keep your intelligent minions working at payday, especially if you spread your dungeon out or try to create a sub base.
There is no way to automate things like Averice gold spells, so you'll find yourself having to pass multiple gold spells all the time and not actually be able to play the game.
The graphics are lovely and there are some clever parts of the game. But the lack of testing at the developer, and the lack of proper UI diligence is unforgivable, and makes the game unusable. For the devs to have such lame excuses really disrespects all the people with decent computers who buy this game and have problems, and simply don't want to keep complaining after the devs dismiss their issues.
Archon will show fully healed and then suddenly in two seconds he dies, all 20,000 hitpoints zapped. This is because the health bars do not always correctly display a minion's health.
The lack of a pause feature is blamed on coding issues (even though other RTS games have them) but this really would solve some problems because at least the game could catch up with itself, and the player could do some diligent work in the RTS due to the crap issues in the game. At least IF there was a pause, you could actually look at the stats of individual minions instead of trying to chase them with a mouseover while they are running.
If you have a few "0" gold instances at payday, some minions never go back to work, even if paid for years later and they become happy again. This is a serious bug. The archivists, for example, will simply stop working for the rest of the game, and you never get any more "sins" (the "sins" are the tech tree equivalent in this game).
I could go on but I won't. I paid $30 for this crap game. Ha ha. Good effort perhaps by the devs but Steam should not allow these kind of buggy amateur efforts. This game is no longer on Early Access so at some point let's get real about the quality. I can't believe this game is so highly rated but I cannot recommend it, compared to all othe RTS games I'e ever played, Overworld is the worst performing, even though the graphics are beautiful.
Major FAIL as devs. Good job on being artists but I bought a game, not an art book.

in short for the casual players:
from a party game point of view where you'd play with your friends casualy local or online it's realy good, especially when everyone is equally unskilled at the game. i like to think of it as a sidescroll mario kart with a higher skill ceiling, losing/winning a very close match can be very infuriating but also very rewarding/satisfying.
while it can be played casually the gameplay can become very fast (as the title indicates), challenging and addicting. controlls are pretty responsive and good too. there are also new avatars/runners and colors/skins that can be unlocked once you gained enough exp. they give a nice little extra incentive to keep playing.
there are still some game crashes to desktop and strange bugs but those only occured maybe 2-4 times within those 50+ hours i got on record at the time of this review. the developers still patch and maintain this game so i don't see to big of a issue there.
overall very recommended for casual play but can get pretty frustrating from a competitive point of view.
more detailed thoughts on the competitive side of the game:
- competitive online ranked play can become quite frustrating.
thats due to how the +/-points get distributed after matches especially when running vs higher ranked players. you sometimes still get +points towards your rank level even tho you got clearely outperformed. those points slowely add up resulting in rank ups and even stronger competition although your skill didn't increase.
i think it would be better if the points would get distributed depending on how fast you ran during the match, for how long you could maintain that speed and which routes you choose. (there are plenty of shortcuts on each level some easy to reach others only with alot of practice).
- also it should be mentioned that ranked matches have a significant smurf issue (players with very high skill/rank which downranked on purpose by leaving matches or loosing on purpose cause they get some kind of satisfaction when they can crush people who are relatively new to the game).
- another problem is the netcode which sometimes does ok and other times doesn't at all which results in players beeing in slightly or completely different positions on your screen then they realy are. this makes it alot harder or impossible to judge the right timing to use your items or dodge the enemys (grappling hooks, boxes, rockets... kind of like the green/red shells in mario kart). this shifts the gameplay more towards the luck based side of things which is not desirable in a competitive environment.
same goes for sliding which can be used to trip nearby runners.
in its current state the advantages of playing with laggy connection are so high that some maybe choose to gimp there connection on purpose to get the edge (tendency also seems higher ranks have very frequently jumpy or continuous high pings... coincidence?).

It's surprising how well this game has aged, especially since it was originally a console game. The keyboard controls are nowhere near as bad as people say they are, they take a bit of getting used to, and they do feel clunky at times, but they're still manageable and it's incredibly fun to skate on walls and rails successfully, and thankfully it never feels awkward pulling off these fun stunts. However the graffiti mechanic is downright BROKEN on PC, i have never pulled off a successful graffiti prompt without failing. The prompts are meant for analog sticks, not keyboard. For example: sometimes you have to make a quarter circle motion, easy with a controller, impossible on keyboard. It's hard to explain, but that's the biggest problem with this game keyboard wise.
The gameplay is incredible, it's a mix of platforming and vandalizing the city's property with your art. The grinding is incredibly fun, and as I stated before, the graffiti mechanic doesn't work properly. But the fun is supposed to come from the joy of skating, jumping and grinding. The game has a time limit, which can be a bit frustrating since finding the last spot you need to tag can be infuriating in some levels, the game could have benefited from a mini map. The government is against graffiti, as in they'll launch missiles and tear gas at anyone who dares to express themselves (i.e vandalize). The police were are a great addition, as they add more challenge, but are easily outmaneuvered and I never died because of them. The game is challenging but incredibly fun, if the controls were ironed out a bit more and if they added a mini map it would have been even better.
Graphically, the game shows it's age, but the cel shading, vibrant colors and unique character designs really make this game pop, and the HD makes it look even better. It is a bit rough around the edges (literally) but this game looks better than most generic games that come out today. It just goes to show that solid art direction is more important than putting life-like realistic military gear on a dog.
And then there's the soundtrack, oh boy the soundtrack. The soundtrack for this game is fantastic, I don't know what genre it is, but it gets you pumped and it really fits with the game's art and gameplay. Even the character selection screen has a catchy tune. Music isn't exactly my forte, so just look up some gameplay online and you'll see what i mean, it fits greatly.
Don't believe the reviews that tell you this game has aged badly, because that just isn't the case. And keep in mind, I didn't grow up with this game, so i'm not blinded by nostalgia at all, I have played this game on Ios previously but that's about it (the Ios port is awful, so don't buy it). The controls hold up well even on keyboard, the game looks incredible, especially now that it's in HD, and the soundtrack kicks♥♥♥♥♥ At the time i'm writing this review this came costs 0,99€. That's a steal for a game like this, and the regular price is 3,99€, which is also a great deal. Now all we need is the superior sequel (Jet Set Radio Future) re-released in HD. DO IT SEGA

I was hoping that they'd improve a lot on original Tanki, since that game is pretty much crap. They have improved on a few things, I'll give them that, but there is way more that they should fix.
I suppose I should state the improvements. Garage supplies (drugs) have been nerfed, which is awesome, since they were always overpowered in Flash Tanki. Instead, you have abilities that are on cooldowns and you aren't charged crystals for single uses. Also, you can chat without having to play the game for 20 hours to reach the eighth rank. That's about it. On to the problems.
Firstly, the gameplay is very slow, even than the original game's. I don't know how the dev team managed to make a game about exploding futuristic tanks absolutely mind-numbing, but I found myself nodding off to this game after only playing an hour. It seems like the developers spent so much time working on the visuals of the game that they completely forgot to make it fun.
Secondly, the visuals. There's a lot to complain about here. I'll admit, Tanki looks pretty sharp in a coat of fresh paint, but there a load of problems with the new scheme. In Flash Tanki, you could immediately distinguish hulls by their distinct shapes, but in the new game, it's hard to tell what chassis the enemy is using at range. It's also extremely difficult to tell if they have supply boxes activated, since the changes to its appearances are absolutely minimal and there's no popup display. A tank with 2x damage, 2x armor, and 40% speed looks physically the same as a tank with none of those perks, and that's a huge problem.
And don't even get me started on the ranking system. Ranking up takes absolutely forever, and when rank directly influences gameplay (mastery, upgrades, and unlocks) that's a big problem. Additionally, all of the easily-recognizable stripes, bars, diamonds and stars have been replaced with pathetic little shields, each with slightly different designs and colors. And that wouldn't be so bad if there wasn't any way to check which shield emblem outranks which other shield emblem.  Ingame, you're basically supposed to guess who's more powerful based on who has the fancier shield.
Additionally, there's absolutely no tutorial, no help screens or menus, and no effort put into teaching the player about the game. No insight on deeper topics, no moderators or helpers to get information from, and you can't ask experienced players about the game since there's no lobby. All you get is a screen that shows you the controls for 3 seconds, and once it's gone, you can't look at it again. It's quite disgusting how little effort went into this part of the game.
There's also quite a few gripes I have that aren't huge issues, just issues for me. For one, controlling the tank feels more cumbersome and clunky than I'm used to, which is bad for a Smoky player since your survival is dependent on your aim and driving. The "ghost" or "phase" time after respawning is incredibly short as well, and sometimes I can't even tell when I've respawned since my camera is shoved into a wall. Turret recoil seems to also have been decreased, so good luck to all you parkour enthusiasts.
I think this game could be great if a lot of these were changed. Help menus should be added, and possibly a funcitonal tutorial for people who haven't played any Tanki game. Popup displays showing supply box usage should also gome back, since it's crucial to know which fights you can take and which you can't. And while you're at it, make sure to add something to help newer players rank up (like the 3x experience pass in Flash Tanki), so that you don't instantly turn off newbies with the game's slow progression rate.
I realize the game is early access right now, and is probably going to change, but in its current form, I can't recommend this to anyone.

With a few technical hitches first opening the game, that took three days over a lengthy email discussion with the support team on how to fix it, I had low hopes at first. I used to play Tanki Online back in the day and sunk at least 1,000 hours into it, so I jumped right on Tanki X the minute I saw it, so to see it not working for three days after downloading was very disappointing. However, with the problem solved, I'm quite happy to say that this met my initial expectations of a "Tanki Online 3", and has brought me back to simpler times of blowing other tanks up.
The gameplay is a lot of fun. I would have liked simple music in battles as an option, but this feature was not in the original Tanki Online so it's not a massive deal. I would have liked a proper pause menu in missions, with options, garage, and other options right there for you so you don't have to unnecessarily leave a mission just to swap out a hull.
The graphics are stunning and perform well. I have a medium-power GPU (GTX 950M) and I play on Maximum graphics at about 60 FPS on average. In intense battles this can dip down to about 40 but this is still manageable. I enjoy the inclusion of advanced or basic graphics settings to suit anyone of any computing expertise or performance, this is a step in the right direction from TO.
Overall, despite severe technical difficulties at first that resulted in me nearly losing hope on this game, I recommend this game to anyone looking for a game to waste time with. The support team is incredibly fast and often respond to emails within the hour, and the game itself is a moon jump ahead of its previous iterations of the franchise. 7/10.

Despite being released in 2011, Gemini Rue is without a doubt, a timeless game. Anyone who claims to be a fan of story-driven games, or indie games, or pixel art, or just generally ♥♥♥♥ing good games should definitely play this. Excellent voice acting and a complex story are the backbone of Gemini Rue, and they more than make up for the retrospectively-accurate graphic style, which I personally love, but doesn't have the pretty lighting effects that more modern "8-Bits" like Sword & Sworcery, for instance, utilise.
The gameplay incorporates a very nice little shortcut that other point-and-clicks I've played are sadly missing, and that's to allow fast-forwarding of long walks through environments when it doesn't interfere with the mood of the sequence you are playing through. The effect that it had on the overall gameplay was that I couldn't stop playing, I was able to somewhat control the tempo of the story so that I was constantly engaged and able to maintain a sense of urgency - something that I often find lacking in adventure games and point-and-clicks in general, since rarely do they inculde the ability to run.
The story is absolutely fantastic and is backed up by great sound and well-produced music. If I was to make any critiscism of Gemini Rue at all, it's that I think they could have pushed it even harder with the music to really hammer home the urgency in a couple of the big scenes or to add some real unease and suspense to some of the smaller ones, simply because Nathan Allen Pinard is so obviously capable of doing it. Having what I would call a more subdued soundtrack however, did allow the voice acting to really shine. It's second-to-none as far as indie games go for me. The only game I can think of off the top of my head that comes close is Firewatch, and that is soley on the back of Cissy Jones who isn't even the protagonist of that game. Everyone is Gemini Rue nails it, and considering the size of the cast, that's pretty impressive to me.
This game is deserving of Cult Classic status to me, and it's no wonder that so many of my indie-loving friends recommended it.

So just to start off, I used to be a huge fan of Lugaru and when I was finally able to run Overgrowth on my new PC, I bought it straight away. I enjoyed it a lot, but was quite disappointed with the lack of content, even though the physics, combat system, movement and graphics were absolutely awesome.
At the time it was 2015, and I wrote a review against buying Overgrowth because at the time, in my opinion as well as many others, it just wasn't worth buying. This was because the game still after 7 years had no story mode. My review received a fair amount of hate from big Overgrowth fans, some not understanding that I loved the game but just couldn't recommend it due to a lack of content. But now I have given the game another try since it hit Beta and I am really impressed.
The Lugaru story mode was added earlier this year. This added the old Lugaru story mode into Overgrowth to allow new players who never played Lugaru to understand the story. Then very recently they added the Overgrowth campaign. This took quite a bit of time but when playing some of the levels, one can easily see why. Levels are much more detailed, with huge buildings, more enemies, more dialogue and a sort of target or goal you need to reach to get to the next level. Different enemies such as dogs, cats and rats are now seen throughout the game (as well as wolves and rabbits which were already seen in the Lugaru Story Mode). Level sizes are much greater and you are able to approach levels from a stealthy or straight on violent run and kill type of style. There are now 3 difficulties that you can choose from, Casual, Hardcore and Expert. Each difficulty can be changed at anytime by just pausing and selecting it. Another cool feature is being able to adjust the speed of the game between 50% speed and 100% speed. This helps a lot if you are struggling during combat or parkour.
After the long wait, I think the game is finally worth it, also leaving early access very soon.
The game now has a story mode for Lugaru (the game before Overgrowth) and a new Overgrowth story mode. The game has improved a lot since it entered beta and is soon going to be leaving early access. Apart from the story modes, there is also a lot of workshop content/mods that you can download. After the wait I can definitely recommend this game to anyone interested in buying it. If you wanting to give it a go, buy it.

I never really owned or even played an original Xbox, so that's why this game flew under the radar for me. It wasn't till much later that I actually got the chance to play it. I have to say though if they had released this on the Playstation 2, I would have been all over it.
Sudeki is a unique RPG in that it doesn't follow your typical JRPG formula. Being a British based company, Climax Studios brought something new and different to the US during it's initial release. While at it's core it still feels like a role playing game, Sudeki also contains elements of third-person, action, adventure, shooter, and even first-person shooter games. The voice acting can be a little campy at times, but sadly most games during that generation had the same problem, fortunately it is tolerable. I do have to admit, the graphics and shaders still look really good, unlike other games that do not age so well. I'm pretty sure they were able to add a lot more to the PC version(because, you know, PC MASTER RACE), because it shows, and it has aged well.
At least until we get to the point where we blur the lines between reality and virtual reality, where our brains won't be able to tell the difference... Then you can run a Sudeki emulator to play it, and wonder how we used to play these types of games. Until then, give this one a shot. Buy it, Play it, Love it.

Submerged is a moving experience, but a boring game. Here's the low down as far as I could deduce:
Pros:
+ Beautiful world and sound design
+ Ambient, compelling story (like Brothers: Tale of Two Sons), particularly liked the fragments of caveman-like imagery
+ Great feeling physics (fo' real)
+ Short (yes, I'd put this as a positive, it sticks around just long enough to make its point and for you to explore the world)
+ Good for completionists who like collecting fragments of story.
Cons:
- Very mundane gameplay
You just climb the outside of buildings 'til you get to the top, press interact with a crate, respawn and do it again. It reminds me of Grow Home (objective-wise) crossed with a disappointing Assassin's Creed (movement-wise).
- Some minor immersion-breaking things - randomly floating grass and tree entities (palm trees also do not just grow out of straight concrete!), and
- Could use more depth, I'd love to explore some of the inside of the buildings, or even underwater.
Overall, if you're the kind of person who favours experience over mechanic, I'd recommend it.

I just completed Submerged a couple of minutes ago, and I can honestly say that I enjoyed every moment I played the game. Even though I had missed a secret (due to my blindness), I didn't mind trying to find it.
The graphics are extremely beautiful, and the effects are amazing. The water looks and moves realisticly, and it is neat to ride the wake from a nearby whale that has jumped from the water. The trees swaying in the wind, the flowers moving back and forth, the butterflies flitting from place to place. All highly realistic, and a joy to look at.
There are also really good weather effects, such as rain, thunder/lightning, and fog. The sunlight and moonlight glisten off the water almost magically, as if they had a secret to tell, but couldn't.
Discovering the various landmarks and other unique buildings and signs added to the mystique. This takes place on Earth, but is it
Earth in the future or an Earth from an alternate universe. There is enough to make it familiar, yet alien at the same time.
I have grown quite fond of Miku, and would love to have more adventures with both her and her brother, Taku.
I did not suffer one crash or any graphical glitches, and it ran smooth as silk even with all the settings at max. You can use mouse/keyboard, but I used a controller and I am glad that I did. It makes use of the rumble feature (you can turn this on or off in Options), and controlling the boat was quite easy to do.
This game has absolutely NO combat in it whatsover, nor are you racing against a timer to prevent failure. You can explore at your leisure, and you don't have to worry about doing things out of order. You can explore any of the climbable locations in any order, no matter how close or far. I like having that freedom, and not being boxed in to "go here first".
I cannot recommend this game enough. An absolute joy, and I would purchase a sequel (if they ever make one) in a heartbeat.

I love a good point and click game because I'm all about a great narrative and interactive story. While Hotel may have soothed my craving for a good PNC, by no means did it satisfy me.
Pros:
1.) Graphics are pretty decent (which you love to see in a good PNC).
2.) There are a few unexpected twists.
Cons:
1.) The puzzles are so easy that you don't have to think very much, or at all, to pass them.
2.) The story goes from "weird" to "wtf" really quickly. Plus, the character development is very weak and predictable.
3.) This game is SO short. I completed this game is 2 hours and that's with me taking my time. Look at the other reviews, no one takes very long to complete this game.
As a rule, I think that PNC games tend to only be worth as much as: (1.) Hours put into the game, (2.) Strength of the storyline. Since this game's story really falls flat, I'd recommend not spending more than $2.00 to play this game because it will not take you more than 2 hours to finish it.

Hotel - Collector's Edition (Cateia Games, 2010)
While playing I planned on writing a recommendation for this game.  Now that I've finished it I realise the thing as a whole has little merit and, aside from recommending it to long time adventure gamers, I honestly can't give a thumbsup to what I've experienced here.
Why recommend it to long time adventure gamers?  Because we'll play anything that is an adventure game, and so if you are one and you havn't yet played Hotel you may as well go and get it over with.
The odd thing is that I really love the core concept:  you have a fancy hotel somewhere in France, an accident has resulted in a young woman's death.  You're a police inspector and your boss believes it was murder.  Will you find out the truth?  And what's with the weird occult symbology all over the place?  And that's how the game starts;  for about an hour you feel like you're building up to something interesting, then it all quickly falls apart as the developers, who clearly had no idea where to take the story, slather on layer upon layer of hoodoo and fantasy that ill-suits the tone of what has gone before.  In other words, they quickly ruin a good murder mystery with what can only be called nonsense, in the process grasping at various mainstream clichés as regards the supernatural.
Note, the game is short.  I logged a bit more than two hours, and that includes exploring the collector's edition extras.  Regarding those extras, they aren't worth buying the game for, for the simple reason that Hotel takes up less than 300 megabytes, making for an extremely compressed package.  That means everything that counts as art assets including audio is incredibly downgraded to fit the meagre file size.  This, I presume, was done to make the game better fit portable devices (there's also a version for smartphones and tablets).  On PC however, you end up suffering because of the low quality assets being run through much better speakers and a much bigger screen than you're likely to find with your mobile device.
In terms of puzzles Hotel is fairly easy.  There isn't much to interact with.  And oddly enough this creates a nice flow through the game, and I became quite engaged early on, despite the game not really taxing my grey matter.  Of course, then the hoodoo starts.
SCORES
Graphics:  35%
Extremely compressed pre-rendered 2D backgrounds.  3D models lack detail.  Character designs are fairly generic and lack outstanding features.  The game starts off with one of the worst pre-rendered FMV sequences I've ever seen.  I mean, straight out of 1992.  It really is that terrible.
Sound:  45%
Not much in terms of atmospheric sound effects.  Only one particularly catchy tune.  No voice acting outside of the horrible introduction and ending FMV sequences.
Execution:  35%
As an adventure game, the mediocre first half manages to improve on Cateia's Kaptain Brawe;  the second half throws all that away.
Addictiveness:  40%
First hour, I wanted to see what happens next.
Second hour, I wanted to get it over with.
Overall:  34%
Like I wrote before, if you're an adventure gamer you either already own this game or you were planning on buying it anyway.  (Which is how I ended up with it.)  For others, forget about it, there are much better adventure games out there if you're only interested in dipping your toes in the adventure game pool.  Buy the likes of Culpa Innata, Perry Rhodan (sadly not on Steam), Jack Keane, Lost Horizon, etc. instead.
Heck, now I feel like making a list of the best adventure games.

First off I would have to say that this is an extremely satisfying game.This game is, much like many Wadjet Eye games (particularly Technobabylon) a mixture of superb story telling retro graphics and puzzles.
However, this comes with a caveat. The puzzles are a mixed bag. Some are quite clever with interesting solutions, while others compel you to look for the walkthrough online.
It is the writing that will keep you going. It should be noted that it starts off slow which may turn off some people. But the story continues to evolve from a mildly interesting tale improving to a fabulous crescendo of exquisite storytelling (I  know that sounds excessive, but it really is a great story).
This is not to say that some of the themes were dealt with, with as much skill as they ought to have been. The nature vs nurture debate and the  discussions about free-will and determinism was not dealt with the degree of nuance one might hope. Further, some of the dialogue making explicit what was already apparent by what was occurring in the plot made some of the lines feel redundant. Despite this it was a fantastic tale, with several surprises (genuine ones) and considerable depth of storytelling.
Overall I would encourage anyone with a taste for good story telling to give this a look.

In short, it's a great game, but a wasted opportunity.
The game has a killer soundtrack, a charming art style, and a superb premise. The port is one of the best that I've seen, no bugs or crashes or anything.
My main complaint is the controls. They simply aren't very tight. I find it difficult to go where I want in this game, and it's gotten to the point where the only antagonist seems to be the analog stick. Mouse controls are in here but they just don't feel fleshed out.
It feels like a wasted opportunity, too. Many titles have come up with ways to get around the inherent inaccuracy that comes from using a controller. The Sly Cooper series is a great example, as the games share many mechanics. The difference is, in sly you had the circle button to automatically snap to things like grind rails. Hell, the B button doesn't seem to do anything, they could have bound it to the same function as the circle button in Sly!
Hell, even Sonic games seem to get automatic snapping better than this game. It's like you need space shuttle precision just to grind a rail! I mean, I'm slowly getting better at it but it's very frustrating when you can't... just... go... there, when the mechanics to do so have been around for more than a decade.

This game fails to capture what made the original dungeon keeper games fun, mostly due to design issues, but also because the attempts at humor fall flat.  Calling out specific design issues, the levels are poorly designed, the way monsters behave and level up is poorly designed, and a lot of the rooms seem barely functional.
The level design is probably the biggest issue.  Timed objectives don't really work in a game with such a low level of control over your units.  Many levels are overly large for such slow units, and even the game's engine stutter has to be agreeing with me there.  For some reason, enemy units always spawn at very high levels, and you get guys at level 1 that take too long to get strong enough to be relevant.
Monsters and their behaviours are pretty terrible, too.  Monsters will not get stronger by doing their default tasks, and won't go train unless you force them to.  The AI isn't smart enough to know if it's hitting or not, and is content to spend a lot of time trying to hit a unit or door and hitting a wall instead.  Additionally, the game will not spawn monsters for you past 2-3 of each, regardless of what you build; your best bet to get an actual army is stealing enemy units with the prison.  I ended up beating the game by chaining together "defensive" turrets because monsters are so painful to actually work with.
Each room has some functionality in that you have to build it to bring in a type of monster, but most of them are otherwise worthless.  So it doesn't matter how efficient they are or big they are, once they've attracted that 2-3 unit maximum they're done.

Although a good game in its core it isn't executed well. Here is some of my critique:
- Poor optimization ( system well over recommended still can't get above 30 fps in certain missions)
- No ''real'' strategy being used in campaign missions ( you can basicly rush most of the missions down easily), this is being solved in multiplayer however.
- During the beginning each missions implements a new aspect ( like new unit etc. missions build around it) , although this is a nice way to let players learn it is certainly boring ( especially the necromancer mission, it was way too long and repetitive).
- Workers being idle while things have been assigned to them need to be resummoned to trigger , they are not efficient.
- I expected a dungeon keeper not a dungeon invader, not enough ambush missions in the main campaign.
- Workers/Units getting stuck in narrow paths when grouped up together.
- No unit strategy, your units basicly attack every enemy near them but can't focus all together on one enemy when multiple enamies are around.
-AI of other dungeon keepers has the same simple strategy ( build and expand and then attack when everything has been build), would be nice to see more variety ( this excludes the mission where traps are being introduced)
-In multiplayer, my blueprints would show up not completed while they would at a friend's/ enemy.
-Spawn times are unclear.
-Is there a cap on the number of units you can have? It does not get explained well.
-Damage numbers?
Aside from all of this War for the Overworld is an addicting game that can keep you entertained for hours and I surely see it as a succesor of the originals, however for me it got boring quite fast, making the main campaign more of a ''how fast can I complete this mission'' campaign,multiplayer is much more entertaining though. It is also great to see regular updates and the developers spending enough attention to the community.

This is one of those cases when you wish the Steam review system didn't have just thumbs up or down, but to answer the question: would I recommend War for the Overworld? I would have to say no. It's not a bad game, but not that great either. It is very similar to the original Dungeon Keeper games, at least based on my recollections, but I don't think the Dungeon Keepers were that great either. They were good, not great.
First of all the plot is mostly pointless, and I still don't know really much about the world after completing the basic campaign. I suppose it's a fairly standard fantasy world with a dose of evil. Overall though, the story left me feeling like I missed the first episode or season of a TV series and never understood why the characters were fighting in the first place. Yet none of that matters really, since the best part about it was that it didn't interrupt the game too much with pointless cut-scenes and exposition. The narrator voice was great though, although the character was a bit annoying since once again I didn't know my motivation story wise to follow him.
The gameplay is fun when you get to destroy stuff, corrupting enemies to work for you is fun, but the main problem I have is that you don't have that much control over your units. War for the Overworld is an RTS, after all, but you can only set up a rally flag and your troops will eventually lumber towards it. Using complicated tactics is almost impossible, since the troops don't really listen to you. It's really annoying when you tell your minions to go to a place, and there's two routes to it: the safe one and the unsafe one. Naturally some of them will take the unsafe one and die for nothing. But it doesn't really matter since the computer AI is crap too.
You might say that War for the Overworld is a game about controlling chaotic monsters to destroy civilization, you're not supposed to be able to control them properly. In theory I might agree, but mostly it comes down to bad AI and lazy game design. The AI is bad, both for your units and enemies as well. Mostly the fights are such cluster♥♥♥♥s you can't tell what's going on, but every now and then I paid attention to specific characters and what they were doing. I remember once when an enemy priestess had her back turned and was walking away veeeeery slowly as my minions were hitting her. She wasn't trying to get away, it was just a case of dumb AI lacking any basic self-preservation instincts. So the basic idea is the AI is bad, you cannot win by using smart tactics with your units, so you just have to have a bigger army, hope enemies come to your traps and then shoot lightning bolts at them. It's not challenging or anything.
I remember back in the day when Dungeon Keeper was still in development, and a games magazine said something like Dungeon Keeper will be like Dungeon Master, but you get to play as the bad guys. I don't know if this claim was made by the games magazine or the developers, but ever since Dungeon Keeper was released I've felt a bit disappointed by it, since it wasn't like playing as the bad guys in Dungeon Master. Thematically it might be, but gameplay wise it is just another RTS. Sure, it's a bit more unique than Command and Conquer or Warcraft -games, but it's still just an RTS. This disappointment has naturally carried over to War for the Overworld as well.
Overall I found the lack of control in the combat system annoying at times, but overall I didn't hate playing it. I guess I just wanted something more. Gameplay wise it isn't great as you have little control over things. The interface isn't very good either. The game doesn't always announce clearly when something important is happening, like an attack, or when it said I had to feed a vampire. I thought I have to give him food like a baby, but it just means he has to be able to go to the prison to drink blood from someone. Sometimes the monsters whine they are sleepy or didn't get paid salary, but the only reason they didn't is because they did not go to sleep themselves or pick up the money. Another AI issue probably. Even the mouse cursor shape, the evil hand, makes clicking on things a bit awkward at times since the cursor feels it's to the side, not on center. So I don't know what the hook in the game is, well, except nostalgia.

Space Epic Untitled is a 3D space shooter with a slight twist: with your phones or tablets, you can easily add 2 extra players to your ship. Jolly cooperation! Great concept, but the game is very unpolished and has practically no player base at the moment.
- Audio is possibly the most polished aspect of this game. The sounds and voice acting are decent, and the music is actually quite nice.
- This game is centred around playing with friends. The mobile app add on is interesting and works surprisingly well (I experienced no connection issues). With one pc and 2 phones/tablets you can form a three-man crew, all operating on the same ship. I think this concept is great and has a lot of potential. However, it is a shame that ads play on the app, even when you are in the middle of a game. I understand that free games/apps need to resort to ads for revenue, but it should not distract the player from the game.
- It’s nice that you have the option to name your ship and choose up to 3 different weapons. It would be nice if they allowed you to customize the appearance of the ship too.
- No one is really playing this. Online multiplayer doesn’t work without other players. I can’t really fault the game itself for this, but the current player base is far too low.
- The app can be improved. No sound comes from the app. This isn’t an issue if you’re all playing the game in the same room. This wasn’t the case for me and my brother, so it would be nice if sounds were introduced. It should also be considered that players who don’t use the app will be at a disadvantage. I think it’s very important that the developers address this issue, because it will become a large issue if the community grows.
- Honestly I have little experience with spaceship/flight games, so I’m not very good at piloting ships. The controls are responsive, but feel quite sensitive, so any small movement can lead you to your demise. Maybe that is just my lack of experience.
- Asteroids will kill you in one hit. Even if you nick just the tip of your ship, BOOM, you’re dead. Lasers from enemy ships, on the other hand, will damage your health accordingly.
- You are expected to mine ores from asteroids. This can be done by shooting the asteroid and driving into the ore. I encountered a glitch where I could not pick up the floating ore. I drove into it 3 times but the game would not register. Furthermore, there is little indication that your shots are doing anything. It takes many shots before the asteroid starts to crack so I often felt that my shots weren’t doing anything.
- The images/graphics used in this game are clearly of low quality.
- Difficult to exit the game. I had to resort to alt+f4.
Space Epic Untitled surprised me. Considering the mediocre title, cover image, and game graphics, I was expecting the worst, but It's not all bad. The music, for example, is great. Although I cannot recommend this game in its current state, I believe it has a lot of potential. I am very intrigued by the inclusion of a mobile app and surprised by how well it works. Yes, the app idea is fantastic, but the core game is lacking. I think the developers should focus on creating a fulfilling experience without focusing too heavily on the app. There's a lot of work to be done to improve this game.

Making games as an independent developer is difficult. But it's even more difficult to make games of the genre's FTP - it is necessary to entertain players, draw in the game and provide donate, which does not affect the game balance.
The first thing I liked was the gameplay. An exсelent idea of control the whole ship with one whole team - Engineer, Weaponsmith, and Captain. Two additional players on the ship are connected using phone devices or emulator on PC. The Engineer manages the shields, the distribution of energy, the repair drones. The Weaponsmith controls additional turrets and battle dron. When you correctly cooperate, the gameplay will start to be transformed - this is a total fun and an interesting gaming experience, even though of the FTP component.
But here starts are only disadvantages. No matter how I try, I can not love the game, which is based on only one gameplay (exception PlayerUnknown'sBattlegrounds). Physics is not worked out. If the action of the game takes place in space, then it is not necessary to abolish the basic laws of physics and the trajectory of motion. Ships are not felt as something big, whole, but as a small box with engines and guns on which the textures were pulled.The history of the world and the characters do not cause sympathy (But im loves that video between missions :D ) The current game mode is monotonous to the point, after two or three games the desire to play is lost.
A simple formula of a typical game session in Space Epic Untitled: start - dig - collect - kill - return to base. That is all.
Add a couple of game modes, diversify the game universe (use background story, further extension), give more freedom to the players, or vice versa, send them to restricted but interesting frames of the game engine.
The game named Space Epic Untitled -
. Now it's worth trying it, but it's nothing better than "flying-shoot".
I sincerely hope that the developers will correct their disadvatages and make the right sequel, because the original idea is simply amazing.

I would like to give this game a positve rating, I really would, but with how often the Devs drop the ball I simply can't. If it was based soley off of the game the Overall reviews would be very different but because of how many mistakes have happened in the short few weeks of this game being out, it remains as Mixed and will most likely drop.
So, lets get some specific problems out in the open while understanding that the game is in early access.
1. The game is fun for the first week of a fresh server and after it turns into a nonstop grind for levels, material, and food.

1A: Yes the game is meant to be a survival game and all survival games are grinds. Conan Exiles however is different in that the grind is imbalanced so far. Getting to the max level in this game requires hours and hours of nonstop killing. But this also requires costly repairs(repairing costs the same as making a new item), and the food/water for a character depletes substantially quicker than any other survival game I have played and the food spoils faster. Unless you have a dedicated clan to providing materials for 1-2 players in order for them to level up, you will be left behind in terms of PvP.
1B: The game gets stagnant at the end game because raiding is near impossible currently(yes, I know they mentioned siege weapons). Explosive Jars take far too many materials and have very little effect when trying to raid large bases. Gods are near impossible to spawn on some servers because the Priests needed to summon them have been blocked. Even with gods, there are some places gods can't reach and with enough doors the amount of explosives needed to break in outweigh the reward in both time and loot.
2. The devs have some serious work to do, both in the game and internally as a company.
2A: Exploits hurt any game like Conan Exiles, but they have been going on since the release of the game and with no end in sight. Fix one Explosive Jar exploit? Another shows up the same day. Super Jumping into bases, flying up walls, using a spear to climb cliffs, super speed using thralls, admin password vulnerability, etc. All these caused imbalances on the Official servers because people used them very early on to raid and hoard resources from people they would wipe. Nothing was done about this by the Devs except fixes to some exploits while others remain.
2B: Another big problem with this game is the unapologetic tone of the Devs when something happens that hurts the players. For instance, just recently there was the Decay system being accidentally implemented and caused players to lose anywhere from nothing to weeks worth of work. The Devs merely gave a solution for Unofficial servers but the Official servers must deal with the loss. The same happened when the Official servers went down for a week, Devs apologized but just told players to move to Unofficial servers instead.
3. Official vs. Unofficial servers seems to be a hotly contested topic for this game and some would argue the best way to play is via Unofficial because of admins actually shepharding the server which the Devs do not do for the Official Servers.
3A: Whenever something bad happens to the Official servers, the Devs are quick to direct people to the Unofficial servers. This is a cause of concern because it should not have to be up to Third Party admins to make the game better for the players but instead the Devs themselves. Instead of fixing the problems, they seem to want to shove the players off onto Unofficial servers where other people will be responsible.
TL;DR: I really enjoyed my initial experience with Conan Exiles but with problem after problem, I will have to put the game down and wait for both the game and the devs to be fixed.

American Truck Simulator is a game where you get into a truck and drive across the United States (just a bit of the South West and California for now unless you get map mods). It may not sound fun but it is because you can go to real places that you may not be able to see in the real world, there are a lot of goals such as;
- Get your own truck
- Pay off a loan
- Fully upgrade a garage
- Travel to every city
and so on. Someone commented here on Steam that it gets boring when you complete those ones but you can make more goals like be a major carrier with 1,000+ trucks and having all of your garages fully upgraded. Some cons are;
- Steering wheel and brakes are too sensitive
- You cannot own trailers
- You cannot put your company logo and/or name on the trucks
- You cannot put a truck number on the truck which is more realistic when you have a fleet
- There are no beacons for the trucks at first but you can get mods
- Almost nothing in the cab to customize
- Road signs do not reflect light when they are in the distance which does happen in real life
- Low beams do not have a large enough beam at night
- No walking mode (however that would be the same as GTAV with it's trucking mods)
However, some great things are;
- Having realistic hazardous placards but they are missing the UN number for the hazmat loads
- The parking brake makes a sound when applied or released
- Unlike SCS's 18 Wheels Of Steel series ATS supports MP3 format audio which is more common it seams
- You can listen to real radio station's online player through the game
- Customizable licence plates if you have a World Of Trucks account
- Varied delivery points and skilled backing
Somethings I would want to be added is;
- Overtime the truck gets dirty epically from driving in the desert and construction sites so you should go to a truck stop for a wash (if your truck is dirty then you are more likely to get inspected at the scales in real life), also the air filters needing to be changed once and a while. Plus, being able to spray your windshield with washer fluid and that running out over time
- Emergency vehicles going to a call sometimes, occasional AI traffic crashes and other emergency calls and seeing the vehicles on the side of the road.
- Building and road construction will progress slightly each time you revisit the area (more if it has been a while). Eventually it is done and some very old buildings get demolished then a new one is built.
- Having a choice of Km/h or MPH on the outside of the speedometer
- Hitchhikers and have some of them reference films, shows, songs or something. However, to talk to them then SCS would need to get several voice actors so the player can choose a voice for their character so the character can talk to them.
- Several fictional game stations for different areas that will comment on the weather, traffic in that station's area and turn to static and eventually another station if the player drives far enough.
Overall, I give this game 8.5/10

They made a lot of changes that make this game better than Mass Effect 1.  They also made a number of changes that are inferior to Mass Effect 1.  Overall, I enjoyed this game a lot and recommend it.
Pros
+The graphics are way better than Mass Effect 1
+The Mass Effect sci-fi universe is great
+The story is intersting
+The combat is MUCH improved (you can actually snipe now)
+Most of the companions are very interesting, particularly the aliens
+I really cared about most of the companions
+The story missions are varied and overall interesting
+The loyalty side missions are varied and overall interesting
+The voice actor for female Shepard is very good
+Most of the cutscense are skippable (unlike the first game)
Cons (most of these are minor)
-The human companions are horribly uninteresting (just like Mass Effect 1)
-You get some of the companions late in the game, which gives you less time to interact with them
-Wrex isn't a companion (my favorite from Mass Effect 1)
-The non-story side missions are mostly a joke.  You get one from a person, walk across the room, and then speak with someone else to resolve it
-The hubs feels even smaller than Mass Effect 1
-You basically have no options to customize your gear (a huge problem in an RPG).  For example, Mass Effect 1 had dozens of different sniper rifles.  Mass Effect 2 has 3 sniper rifles to choose from.
-There are way fewer level-up options
-The load times are pretty long, even with an SSD

Hello, I am Jadiwan from Let's Play Online.
I have played about 45 min of the game with several deaths. I have found the developers have a good concept for the game. Everyone needs to remember, this is an early access game and there are always bugs and content planned for a game that has not been implimented. This being said, I have a few isssues with the game, that are game stoppers for me "even early access"
1: No save function for the game on release. (Note: Developers say this will be added in the next update}. This is an issue because playing a game for 30 minutes or so and then having to restart the game the next time makes the game no fun.
2: As with all survival games, gathering resources is part of the game and expected. Having the tools to do this is a must. Having the resources needed to make the basic tools needed to gather resources is also a must and if not available in the game it becomes a game stopper. I found that the first tool you are given is a stone axe "basic survival tool". The stone axe has durabiliity and will weat out " expected in a survival game". However; to make a new stone axe, it requires stone, branches and cloth. No cloth to be found. I was able to get resources from one tree, on boulder of clay and boulder of stone. Axe is almost wore out. Wandered the map for over 20 minutes and found no source of cloth. Game over for me as I can not gather more wood, stone or clay to make any of the items in the crafting menue.
3: Food and liquid intake is part of survial games. When you start the game you are provided berries for liquid intake. The amount provided lasted the 40 minutes or so of game play and I still had some left. However; while wandering the map[, I found no source of berries to resupply my liquid intake and will eventually die of thirst. Game over in maybe an hour or two.
With the above comments in concideration, If the deveopers make regular updates to the game and address the above issues in the next update I whole heartly give the game a thumbs up. This being said. if the devolpers do not fix the abouve issues, the game is not worth the money you pay for a game that will only give you about an hour or two of continuous playing and game over "restart".

I've put the tl;dr section below this one.
I've played only about half of an hour and I don't really get any idea of why this game is trying to accomplish. For one, it looks like the game has very little of a playerbase since the majority of things I was fighting, from what I could see, were bots. The controls feel stiff and floaty. Whenever I accelerate, I go very fast, but this may cause early players to die almost instantly from the meteor belt. It caught me off guard a few times. When I decelerate, however; I expected not to grind to a complete halt and it seems as though it does it even if you press tab. It isn't a bad thing, but I was trying to learn the controls and it wasn't helpful to know that I was getting shot at from invisible forces. The graphics themselves aren't terrible, but they do leave room for desire. For example, the asteroids look like they come from space, but I can't tell the difference between those you can mine and those you can't. You can't even destroy the other ones, so why have a weapon that can, to put it bluntly, hit just about anything? I think the game could of used a bit of fine-tuning to help it out.
Pros:
-The game accurately depicts at least the ability to be in space. There are planets, spaceships, asteroids, etc to make you feel like you are in it.
-Hardly any bugs as I can figure out.
Cons:
-Controls feel very awkward to control. For example, trying to move the mouse around quickly is a bad idea and instead you are kind of forced to make it more slowly in order to be able to hit anything or move around.
-The episodic nature of the game felt weird. I didn't really get why the game had to be in episodes as it could of done fine being something similar to that of Kerbal Space Program or Spore as examples. I couldn't for the life of me figure out why this game needed to be episodic.
-One of the controls that should be able to bring up something doesn't at all for me. My tilda key never brought up the scoreboard even though it should have by all means. I don't know if this is the game's fault, but if it is, then that should be addressed.
-The live broadcasts didn't really help it out. From what I could tell, they were prerecorded and not at all what I expected.
Overall Score:
I'd give it a 2/10 or a 3/10.
Comments: It's not terrible, but it isn't good either. The overall game feels rushed. I couldn't move very well, and some players could easily shoot at me, but I couldn't even hit them. The controls definitely needed some fine tuning along with the map in general. I played both episodes to see if there was any difference between the two, but as far as I can tell, all that happens differently is that you aren't mining ore and instead you are trying to kill the big base. You can still mine for ore to get power ups, but the instructions weren't very clear on what parts you had to kill. For example, I could try shooting at one of the turrets and then try another, but the only true way I figured out how to get something is to have a reticle. That unfortunately is not always the greatest case because if you are trying to fire at something, you may forget to stop and instead crash head first into it. I can blame some of this for being my fault, as I'm not the best at these kind of games, but I feel as though the whole game had me interested just because it was a space thing. I'd recommend it to those who can deal with these kind of controls, but otherwise steer clear of this. It's not the best thing in the universe.

Cons:
