Been playing Conan for the past month and have to say i have a good opinion.
1. This is my first survival game so i don't base it on any other in its field. I don't believe in compaison of games in the first place, for making reviews.
2. I am an avid gamer who spends 4-8 hours a day over the past 16 years. I have open beta tested several games many people never heard of.
I would currently give the game 8 out of 10. It is lacking in some current content, and if it is released i would up the game to a 9.
The game has a good dev team that work hard on informing the players of what they plan, as well as listening to them to make game balancing choices.
The game runs smoothly on my now 3 year old gaming PC. I have on high settings and get s solid 30FPS. I also have 100mb download net with 10 up. They have fixed the rubber banding and worked extensively on optomizing the basic server structure.
Now onto game play.
The game lacks a bit of pvp balancing. In its current state, there is no reason to make bows and use shields. Bows travel speed make it hard to hit anyone, and once someone is close to you a sword does more DPS. A bit of zig zag and bows are useless. Shields are useless at the moment. Its better to swing wildly than trying to block as shields will break and you sill take damage from swings.  There is dual wielding with dagger, but there is no combo system yet and dual wielding does nothing, as you are better to use main hand weapon for damage on swings.
The skill system is not completely balanced either. Its heading in the right direction but not complete. The only rewarding skill i ever invested in is vitality. All the others are iffy. With grit being the other decent one and str and agility following into 3rd priority.
Currently there is no reason to raid. By the time you get to raiding you can build everything on your own and investing that much resources in raiding hardly yields anything. 9/10 times i have been raided while offline and lost everything. Players have spent 120 jars to get a handfull of resources. This is a serious issue with the game. Pvp sucks.
Beside all that i still give it 8 out of 10 due to the amount of fun i have had. The building system, though a bit annoying is very rewarding indeed. Being able to find a few players running around and fighting them to death just for fun of taking their stuff is very rewarding. While i totally understand, why this game is so much loved by the players, i sadly have to admit, that at least i cant recommend the game. But when i see, that only around 50% of the people (even now, where the game still cost around 50 bucks) finished the first act, i think that i am maybe not the only one who disliked at least some aspects of the game. So to give you besides all the praising reviews also an neutral review from the side of a player who sadly didnt enjoyed the game as much as many others, i hope that my review, together with the many reviews that love the game, can help you in deciding, if you are the targeted audiance of the game, and if you would enjoy the game.
Because everyone has a different taste, and maybe you will love the game like many others, but maybe the things that i will adress are also very importand for you too. And if this is the case, then maybe this game, while having a very high quality, will just not suit you as a player.
Let us begin with the positive aspects, and their are many of them:
The graphics are just awesome! The graphics allone are already very atmospherical, (like in the mysterious swamp, the view is turning slithly green, a strom on the sea looks dark and dangerous, a sunny day on the beach looks very harmonious etc.) it will be even surpassed by the elemental graphics in the battles: When your fire spells turn the oil into fire, explosions overcome the whole area, your enemys bleeding to death from the necomancer spells, thunders crashing into the water and shocking everyone in it: The battles look very chaotic and awesome in so many ways, and just staring at the battle effects bring me much joy. Everything looks so good in this game, and while it is true, that graphics are not everything, i wanted to give them the praises they deserve, because they are all so perfectly done.
The world is very interesting indeed. Besides the lore of the world that bringes some interesting new aspects into the "clischee" fantasy world, like cannibal elfs  or the possibility to speak to animals as if they would be normal persons etc. makes the world even in such an often used genre like the fantasy genre, a very individual touch. The story is interesting(at least the parts that i have seen so far) and you are always curious how the story will continue. While i was never totally "lost" in the story, and it never gets me very emotionally, it still fullfilles its purpose to keep the player interested. Just when you are a player who really needs a totally deep innovative, and unforseeable story, then you maybe will not be happy from it.
Even better then the already good story is the overall world: The locations you visit look very "real", the citys are full of interesting and different people. Everyone has something to say and i never felt like their are just a few "maincharacters" and a bunch of empy npcs to fill the location. As to the story, you shouldnt expect to much, every character is "just" a very good scripted character so they dont develop the depth of a major Mass Effect Charakter, but also they dont feel like hollows witout any personality.
The gameplay is maybe the best i have ever seen in an classic RPG. The fights (at least in the higher difficulties) really need you to think about your moves, and can be very hard sometimes. Every Quest can be solved in many ways and in generall you have a very high freedom to play the game as you like. You can play (most of the time) as a pacificst, avoiding every battle with your good conversations talents and your stealth mechanics, or as a psychopath who killes everythink that just slithly provokes him. The lonewolf who only fights for his own, or the classical hero who tries to safe the whole word.
But with this freedom comes a very huge problem: The lack of connection between the "worldparts"
Since you are free to do what you want, the game never can forsee how your next movement will be. In one situation you can be the hero who showes mercy to the enemy because you understand his motive and forgive him, and in the next battle you kill everythink that moves. You can first rescue a member of the resistance against the cruel regime, and in the next moment when you are in the outpost of the resistance you can kill everyone inside to get the loot. Their is no "wrong" way to play the game. But this leads to the huge problem that almost nothing of the single aspects of the game is connected.
Let me make an example since just talking around the topic is confusing if you dont exacltly understand what i mean. *minor spoilers ahead*
In the first real act you are trapt on an island where sources mages like yourself are forced to wear a collar that surpresses their power. And also they are trappt in a ghetto, unable to leave the castle and the island. In a certain quest one of the prisoners helped me to destroy the collar so that my source powers are free ones more. But this leads to the situation that now every magister (the guardians of the castle) will see that you have not the collar anymore and will imprison you once more, to force you to wear it again,or attack you if you show resistance. I showed resistance...and in the result every magister in the whole castle did attack me on sight. So i have started a revolution against our surpressers, overcome them, killed them next to the other scared prisoners, opened the closed gates, let the people to freedom....only that they didnt care. Since the daily routine of the prisoners is not connected to the life of the magisters, they will just continue their life as normal. That means complain how hard their life is under the surpression of the magisters, and that they so greatly want to escape but cant, because the guards are so many and the gates are closed...while in reality every guard is dead and the gates are open.
And this problem is in every aspect of the whole game. On a sinking ship i did calmed a few of the shipkeepers so that i didnt have to fight them...but when i found a lifeboat to escape i could safe everyone but them...because they could be already be dead if i just fight them before, and so their life is not connected to the lifeboat so that their is no way to safe these fellas even if you try. Or a leader of the resistance (who cried how many of his good man died in the fight against the supressing magisters) doesnt even say a word after everyone(!) of his camerads died in a big battle, since their was also a possibility that they would be already dead, before the battle starts. And so he just talkes totally normally like nothing has happend while in reality all his friends with which he has fought for many years, just died a few minutes ago.
And this, at least for me, totally killes every bit of immersion that the game would normally develop from such an awesome world. Since you realise more and more, how scripted everything is, and that certain NPCs just react to this quest that they give you, and dont interact with anything else at all (as long you dont attack or try to steal from them) you never develop the feeling that you are "inside" this world and that the world is living around you. But more and more it feels like everything just exists to give you a quest, and stay silent after they have fulfilled their purpose (like maybe a person from an MMORPG, that gives you one quest and then just stands their without any purpose) and since the world and the mainplot are so great and fascinating, it have lead to great frustration to me.
I know that this is not a fault of the game itself since its techically awesome in any sense it wants to be, but i think i just realised in this game, since the experience i get from this game becomes more and more "empty" i think that i am just the wrong audience for this type of very open RPGs. Because for me, the huge amound of freedom just destroys the illustion to be in a real world. And for me this is more importand then 10 options in every quest.

Fantastic game, feels very true to the Dungeon Keeper spirit as many people will say, but not without adding it's own mechanics and extras of which there appears to be plenty.
There is lots about this game that I like that are part of the original package, not to the major Dlc Mention, though the original stands well on its own.
WotO creates a very immersive experience, with the dark dirges for music, as well as the animated and interesting world that becomes your dungeon.  I found the decor to be very much in line with the original.  It is really nice.  Even the walls are something to be looked at with detail, again, much like the original... There is a level in the My Pet dungeon Dlc which exhibits a maze full composed of these rooms, with their walks and it was quite interesting to see all the different varieties of walls and effects.
However at times, though this certainly was the case with dungeon keeper, combat can be a bit lame when your looking for a challenge.  Though in saying that, the thrill is in making the resources to win combat and not to fight it...   Dungeon keeper was never designed to make combat develop past the initial conflict, it was a game of 'stacks'.
Though do not take that as a negative so that all you need to do is make an army and that is, there are plenty of traps, though I find the mana system for them quite suffocating... Though, this is clearly a good design as a player who uses traps wont use magic (much) so there are counter balances.  This is good.
Despite this, combat (like Dungeon keeper) is quite engaging.  The UI for combat in Dungeon keeper 1 was the best though and I yearn for a window that shows individual instances, this you get an alert button where you need to watch the creature individually else something may die or at least get knocked out.
In saying that the UI is quite good, it doesn't deviate much from the other dungeon keepers, with virtually the same tabs , though there are a couple more added for extra or expanded mechanics.  Rest assured, you can manage your minions almost entirely through the minion information tab(activities and other stats).  They could do with fading the images of the portraits for the creatures though - it can be difficult to read numbers on the creature panel - this is minor.
Research is not a bad edition either, this makes a lot of sense, given the automation of the original research and as much as I can say Supreme Commander 2 made this design grating and dull, WotO made it good.
Some of the creatures and designs were really great.  I wont go into too much detail, but there are are still Horned reapers here, even though its not clear. In-particular the vampire is a time bomb if there is not a good supply of enemies, though suitably powerful themselves.
The voice acting from the original Dungeon Keeper was very good, and yes its worth mentioning.  From the silly  'its past your bed time' statements (which there are many, it's great there is so much variety) to the general narration.  However, though the DLC made the narrator more chilled and pleasant which I enjoyed;  the end of the original scenario made him bickering to the extent that a particular level where you fight a Keeper with an rubix cube for a heart; he sounds sonically aggressive, imposing and quite annoying... I think the devs went too far with this and its something games today need to sort out where the timing of their 'prompts' that are too short as if they appeal to the mental ability capacity of a fish.
There is very little bad to be said about War of the Overworld and is a great game.. I still don't get how to beat crucible, but Really enjoyed this and is more than worth the 20 quid, funny given most Unity games on Steam are often worth < 10p You learn something every day...
These are post multiplayer thoughts  and can be seen as negative - its not really - multiplayer was good - just not that great late game... dont let that put you off!
One issue is the multiplayer - any game larger than 1v1v1 is likely to suffer drastically when each dungeon reaches maturity.  The lag becomes game breaking (could have been me and my frind's set up...) -deciding for some 'clients'  not to build a titan - which is a high handicap - this bug has been sent to the devs by someone.  But generally units become stuck and misbehave when unit numbers reach a certin size - I thought this limit was not much higer than a standard sized dungeon... It is a deep shame, but I suppose Molyneux in the old days had people making their engine(I think?) maybe this shows limits of Unity... or maybe this was an optional feature.
Whats more multiplayer is a -richer gets richer formulae.  There is  - as far as I know - no way for the underdog to win - other than being a MUCH better player than your opponent(i mean 500%) not much way to beat someone who is winning, they have more money, bigger rooms and more numbers - quanity matters.  This is a shame as this limits WFTO's replayability to a casual excursion. :(
In saying that - War For the Overworld.. or Underworld... is still a pleasure to play and I found it a deeply satisfying building my dungeon in the first place - and as mentioned : Dungeon keeper is more about keeping units out of battle until it's right and if not about stacks.

It makes me sad that the Mass Effect franchise is currently going through a bit of a rough spot, one that it may not recover from.  With the trainwreck that is Andromeda suggesting a grim future for the series, it helps to look back at the old games and remember how good they were.  Mass Effect 1, while a great sci-fi RPG in its own right, was not without its flaws.  Awkward combat, unnecessary skills, and tedious planet exploration would all be addressed with its sequels.  Fast forward a bit and we arrive at Mass Effect 3 which had a lot to live up to as we were all waiting with bated breath to see the conclusion to this epic story, or more specifically what the outcome of our choices throughout the story would be.  Needless to say, they dropped the ball on that one leaving a bad taste in all of our mouths (however, if we're being honest, it was a pretty good game up until that point).  Mass Effect 2 on the other hand doesn't seem have too many of these faults; it's just a great game from start to finish.  Two of the main reasons this was achieved was that it had a more fleshed out and satisfying combat system that forced you to react to your enemies defenses, and it had a story that was much more character driven than anything else.  Your squadmates' loyalty missions are so well done that it was difficult not to become emotionally invested in every one of them.  But hey, even if you decide to ditch your teammates' missions, you can still finish the game and get a completely different ending that's just as emotionally engaging.  Even its DLC is good.  Shadow Broker and Overlord are fine examples of what DLC should be - an extra piece of a delicious pie, not a missing piece.  tl;dr, Mass Effect 2 is a damn good game.

As I have said in my ETS2 review driving a virtual truck might not seem like the most exiting of things, but ATS just like ETS2 before it manages to achieve the improbable and actually makes it a very relaxing and fun experience to just start your favourite music on the radio and drive through the expansive roads, cities and small towns of California, Nevada, and Arizona delivering various goods and growing your trucking empire.
Both ETS2 and ATS have something unique to offer. ATS captures the feel of US roads pretty well particularly after the rescale SCS has done to make the map a lot bigger and complete. The diversity of companies and cargo is pretty good in my opinion, and the three states provide plenty of roads to drive, even if not as much as full ETS2. The complexity of cities is also better in ATS than in most parts of ETS2.
ATS definitely has a different feel to ETS2, the landscapes are new as well as road layouts and the overall feel is different to when I am driving in ETS2. You can definitely tell whether you are in Europe or the US and not just because of the truck you are driving.
The only downside of ATS currently is that it has only 2 truck brands with 4 truck models together; and it seems SCS is having a rather hard time getting new truck licenses so the wait for new trucks, if you don’t like using mods, might be rather long.
Overall ATS is a brilliant US truck simulator with a ton of potential when new states and new trucks are added in the future.

BEST MULTIPLAYER SURVIVAL GAME EVER +Your choice of PvP or PvE and RP (by server preference)
Given decent server settings (low gear wear / combat damage taken, and other tweaks) along with a good admin that can work with the database to keep things clean, this is the best survival game in the genre.  Couple that with roleplay and clans, and you have a really rich environment to enjoy.  One issue a poor server / host will have is real estate being taken up by people that are inconsiderate and build profusely, then leave and do not come back.  Areas that have player buildings keep things from spawning and potentially ruin the prospect of gaining thralls or combat in that area.  So it's important the server admin / host manages the real estate / database efficiently.
MODS
A server that hosts mods is also a plus, improving the game measurably.  Such as Increased Item Stack - so you don't have to have multiple iventory or storage box slots dedicated to the same stuff, MapCoords - a grid on the player map to make it easier for players to find each other, and Pickup+ which is super helpful as it allows picking up placed builds instead of only dismantling them.  The game (unless it changes) does not allow moving things around once placed.
BUGS
I have found playing in 4k video res made the game unstable for me.  I do not know if this was representative of the game, or my PC.  I recommend playing in no higher than 1080 HD for stability sake.  Also, a player should refrain from mixing modes - try not to use inventory or build while sitting in a chair, or swimming, as examples.  Mixing placing buildings with inventory actions or equipping / unequipping items can cause issues.  However, in all the crashes I've had on all the servers I have played, the game picked up where it left off without any remnant of the problem.

The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion has been my favorite open-world RPG, let alone my favorite game of all time for quite some time now. Set in fantasy medieval times on a distant, earth-like planet called Nirn, but with a variety of magic spells and creatures, you break out of jail as a tutorial and fend for yourself right outside the sewer exit. An extremely large map surrounds you while you have to scavenge for food, currency, weapons and armor. 250+ quests wait for you. The side-quests are of the plenty and they make your experience unique and amazing. A great level-up system is in place too, as you have to increase your skill levels to increase your overall level. Fantastic voice acting too. The downsides are that this is only a console port, so there are some bugs and a few broken quests in place, that had carried over from the console version as well. Control mapping is completely customizable, and seems well optimized. This game is so large that if I were to tell you everything about it, it could be a pretty thick book, so I'm just going to leave you with the rating and adventure.

War for the Overworld began as okay modern day Dungeon Keeper clone. After the fiasco with the mobile DK it seemed a lot more amazing than it actually was at the time. As people put in the hours and hours of game play it's flaws and shortcomings began to show and remove a bit of the veneer. It was worth picking up for DK fans and was worth a try for base building fans but not really recommended for anyone else.
After a short stint in the spotlight this game should have faded into obscurity but the developers did something odd and rare, they kept developing the game with love and passion and they listened to their fans. Bug fixes, new content, new modes, new mechanics, free and paid expansions, new and expanded lore, graphical improvements, game play tweaks, major quality of life improvements, I could go on and on. Just check out the patch logs. They've been at this for two years and they're STILL going strong.
Today with all the dlc War for the Overworld surpasses it's predecessor in every aspect and is easily a modern day masterpiece. There's something for everyone in this game now (even stealth levels and disco music) and this game can be highly recommended to just about everyone without a hatred for strategy. The evil dungeon building throne is now firmly theirs and it is most certainly well deserved. I look forward to the upcoming dlc that will hopefully provide more background information on our favorite Underlords.

Here's a single session description which will hopefully strike the reader with the joy I experienced. To be honest, it's more like a review for myself than an actual help information but forgive me for being egoistic this time. Not the last time though.
That day I was the ruler of some small territory in Ireland. My name was long so I preferred to call myself Ua which is actually a part of it. I was 47 years old with a wife and a few kids. They all were very talented siblings with good education except for the last one named Dub-da. I decided to experiment a little with him so he ended up not having a guardian and betrothed to a dumb woman. People of my tribe knew me as 'the sloth with good strategic skills". My treasury was almost empty but I decided to invest last coins in some risky business opportunity. Some oversea lord invited us to his country for a business discussion!
It was a question of whether or not we should buy some merchant's ship or hire bandits to capture one. We hired bandits and were readly to sail off. Some priests catched up and asked to join us. 'Sure sure come in feel yourself like in the Heavens'. After a few days of sailing priests declared that they haven't seen the crew which was fully consist of thieves and bandits.
We finally arrived at the castle of our potential business partner. Feeling ourselves a little uncomfortable we realized that we forgot something important - a gift. Thankfully, on our ship we had: a dozen of good breeded horses, some rich cloth and a pouch of herbs. So with a smile on his face, Ua presented the pouch as a gift and it was the moment which started a long friendship.
The oversea lord invited us for a dinner. My brother was a barbarian just like me as you probably figured out already so he was very hungry and ate the food with his bare hands. The lord noticed that and asked me to do something about it because YES it was an issue. I replied 'What?! I'm hungry too!' and with a cavemen cruelty I attacked a nearby roasted rabbit, punching it before eating. It was already dark outside when the atmosphere in the throne room suddenly changed. Excusing  everyone I ran off the room then up the stairs disrobing as I go and finally standing completely naked on a balcony in front of the full moon howling 'aaaAAAAAOOOOOOooooo'. The guards found me soon.
Next day some of my priests started a discussion with the Lord about something important but I just witnessed it from the ground next to them. It was our last day there.
After sailing off to our lands I had a signed trading contract between our nations for two years!! #OOhYEAH! #contracthype
After coming back some events took place such as:
I woke up and noticed that my garden looked wild with tall weeds and fibres everywhere on the walls and statues so you can't pass without a good sharp sword. So i decided to clean it up and to do it myself! That was the moment when people stopped to call me a sloth but instead started to call me a gardener! Who would think that at the age of 48 I'll become a gardener?
One year after I recieved a book of poetry. I digged through it twice or so and discovered a great sympathy to this craft. So here and there I started to white poems and verses. I didn't consider myself a poet and thought that all this was just a fun hobby. BUT WHY anywhere I go I hear people singing and reading MY POETRY??!! Who would believe that at the age of 49 I'll become a poet?
Somebody sent me a bird. It was an eagle-kind and I took it with me for a hunt! The bird was brilliant! We came back to the big house with lots and lots of rabbit corpses! Who would imagine that at the age of 50 I'll become a falconer?
After these events my friend, Koyori, who knows about this game more than I'll ever know was impressed and called me 'Master of Hobbies'.
So it seems like my point is: it's not important to know how to win in this game because just playing it is a lot of fun!

This game is quite simply an insult to fans who loved the original majesty (including me), i loved majesty 1 when my parents got it in the Winter of 2003 (oh so many years ago), it was one of those games that was one of the memories of my childhood. But enough of that, lets get to why this game is atrocious compared to the original Majesty.
Paradoks decided apprantly that instead of developing this game themselves, they outsourced it to 1C, a company in Moscow that i guess have no idea what made the original so good. So what did 1C, (and Paradoks) screw up that made this game inferior to Majesty 1? the list is too long, but i will list the 3 biggest problems with majesty 2 with a paragraph for the first two problems, and a short summary for the third.
First: AI: The AI in Majesty 2 is quite simply put, abysmal compared to majesty 1, your heroes seem to not have any personalities like Majesty 1. (ironic considering the subtitle: Fantasy Kingdom Sims) in majesty 2 heroes seem to have no motivation to do anything outside of Greed by placing reward flags for doing things.
In majesty 1 heroes could be motivated by reward flags, but they did things on their own, warriors would raid monster lairs on their own because it fits their description of a glory seeking WARRIOR, rangers would explored the unexplored areas of your map and reveal on their own, healers would follow other heroes, because it would fit their noble nature and they were a real help for your warriors if they were fighting tough monsters. they also were smart enough (most of the time) to know when facing an enemy that was way above their heads, and would try to flee from unwinnable fights. In majesty 2 your heroes are so stubborn, they will try to fight monsters 15 levels above theirs and will get smashed to paste because they're stupid to run away. Oh but they do run away when they're wounded enough, to bad that when they do they often are literally one hit from death by anything, and they don't get away usually the monster is already in the attack animation and they die. they're also so stupid they will tunnel vision with their actions all the time. i can't tell you how many times a dragon flew right by my one of my warriors, and they don't notice each other, maybe they gave each other a funny look, but they move on.
Heroes in Majesty 1 also had priorities to defend their homes if they were attacked. If your palace was attacked it would send out a call for help, and ALL your heroes (no matter their skill or level) would drop what they were doing and try to save your home because if you fall, then they fall.
In Majesty 2 your palace can literally be ablaze in fire getting attacked by monsters and your heroes will not give a second look. all the AI in Majesty 2 seems to be centered around reward flags, and if you don't give them rewards they will not do anything. I must press on the importance, that with a strategy game where you can't directly control your units, you cannot screw up the AI to the point where they're so robot-like they might as well have made it into a RTS. Making it to where heroes will not do anything unless you give them rewards adds more needless micro-managing, for a game that focuses on macro-managing gameplay.
Second: Quests: more specifically their difficulty, now Majesty 1 had problems with some of the quests rushing waves of enemies before you were ready, but they were few and far between and even then they did not have enemies right at your palace gates before one in-game day had passed.
Having a boss be challenging because he/she is hard to get to is good difficulty because its not facing it before you're ready. Challenging gameplay does not include having bosses join in every so often with the aforemented dumb rushes of monsters to harrass your kingdom to screw up your attempt at setting up a base to get your kingdom up and running.
Majesty 1 also did not have artificial difficulty by having steep learning curves that makes Dark Souls blush, where if you don't know/use the EXACT SAME strategy you will lose no matter what. The tutorial and the second mission is very laid back and a breeze, but when you get to Quest 3 the learning carve goes higher then Mount Everest. You will be attacked by monsters before your peasents even come out of their houses to build your buildings. because your Guards are so useless against any enemy stronger then a rat. have fun watching your peasents die over and over, as they try building your buildings, but they can't because they keep getting waylaided by the monsters that will be swarming your kingdom b4 they're done building.
Third: Bugs: this game suffers from a bunch of bugs, but one bug that really stands out (or doesin't as the link i will provide will explain) is people with powerful PCs that have high FPS ( anything higher then 60 FPS) will suffer from a gamebreaking bug, where your peasents will build buildings slower. If you want more details, heres a link to a guy who found this out:
TL;DR: The first Majesty game had more thought ,more polish, and less bugs then this game. Go buy that if you're looking for a game where you feel like you're running a Sims game in a strategy genre. stay away from this botched attempt at a sequel.

Among the earliest PC RPGs were the dungeon crawlers - the Might & Magics, Dungeon Masters, and the Wizardries.  In the US, dungeon crawlers fell out of fashion around the time that modems and video cards became a thing, and despite the odd throwback like Legend of Grimrock, our RPG development took a different track.  In contrast, Japan fell in love with the Wizardry style of dungeon crawler (even getting some actual Wizardry games we didn't), and have been putting them out for years.  Recently, those Japanese dungeon crawlers have been getting localized for our audiences, largely on portables - your Etrian Odyssies, Dark Spires, etc.  NIS has taken a number of their Vita dungeon crawlers and brought 'em to PC.  Sword City is one such example.
It's pretty good!  You've got some of the standard Wizardry-like tropes - generic characters you create, class changing to build more powerful teams, potential for permadeath (excluding your hero), guess-the-trap style loot chests, unmapped dungeons with environmental hazards and hidden doors, that sort of thing.  You've also got Etrian Odyssey style hunts for "Lineage types", minibosses that can tear you up much like a good FOE would.  There's even a Shin Megami Tensei style Law/Neutral/Chaos split, albeit with less extreme behavior on both sides.
Combine all that with a nice system where you acquire gear by ambushing enemy groups at designated spots and some nicely challenging boss fights, and you could certainly do far worse if you want a relatively story light, dungeon-crawling, monster-bashing way to spend some time.
One caveat; there's a remastered version of Sword City available on Vita, with some extra classes, some balance tweaks, etc.  It may or may not be coming to PC, so if you want the remaster then you'll either want to grab that version or take a wait-and-see approach here.

If you were intrigued by the description, you probably will like this game. The mechanics are a fairly standard visual novel, with a decent balance between events that are within your control to choose and challenging obstacles put forth by other characters.
The plot I would say also strikes a good balance between lighthearted romance and harsh consequences for bad decisions. The society the writers described is an interesting one, where lineages are passed down along matriarichal lines. Consequently, there are some interesting twists on gender roles which are very clearly defined for the characters (though they sometimes follow and sometimes invert traditional gender roles in our world.) It's deep enough to be interesting and provoke thought, but still light enough that it doesn't get bogged down or stray from its core romantic-adventure heart.
If you liked both Fruits Basket (or Hana Yori Dango) and choose your own adventure books you will probably like this.

The worst game in the trilogy, but still a must-play to bridge the gap between ME1 and ME3. (For crying out loud, start this series with mass effect 1. Dont start here. None of these games are that great but as a whole series it made for one of the most excellent gaming experiences I've had.)
Combat hardly improved upon ME1's, and the things that made ME1 combat unique over other games was replaced with a generic combat system seen in pretty much every shooter game. So when I say it hardly improved, I mean it became worse.
The entire game is basically a recruitment mission, only to end up not using any of your acquired squad members properly in the final mission. Sure you get to put some of them to work, but this is just by the press of a button in a menu, and their action will take place off screen, resulting in the least badass team ever. There was no sense of teamwork for me in the final mission at all, making me question why I acquired so many squad members in the first place.
Some of the characters feel like they were designed by interns and tacked onto the game just because. Thane doesn't even have a friggin codex entry for his alien species for crying out loud. (This is why I think ME3 is great, THAT game was able to make me care about all these stupid characters introduced in ME2, something that ME2 itself completely failed to do. (This also applies to ME1 to some extend, but it's not as bad as ME2))
Also this game's plot is completely irrelevant to the overall plot of the entire series. You could completely skip ME2 and you'd miss out on nothing that's relevant to ME1 or ME3. The only reason this is worth not skipping is because of Shepard's personal story; the friends he makes and the personal relationships he builds. (As I said, ME3 was able to make me care about the new characters from ME2, so it's nice to have the backstory)
One last thing: The dialogue system is horrible. Genuinely worse than Fallout 4's. Might I recommend Door Monster's "Dialogue Shrubs" video on YouTube. It describes this game with pinpoint accuracy.
As I said, this is the worst game in the trilogy, but it is a must-play in order to bridge the gap between ME1 (which is ok) and ME3 (which is great, apart from the ending, and only because ME1 and 2 established the universe so it didn't need to.)

I hesitated on whether to give this a thumbs up or down but in the end it has so many ridiculously over-the-top positive reviews that I feel like it's not an accurate picture of the game. So:
Pros:
- Good heroine. She is intelligent, independent and strong with a mind of her own.
- Brilliant grammar and good writing. I only noticed one spelling mistake the whole game and the writer(s) of this game clearly have some skill.
- Touches on some difficult subjects, such as transgenderism and homosexuality.
- Adequate amount of choices.
- I liked how you are given walls of text instead of having to read everything in a dialogue box.
Neutral:
- Music: Good enough but short and repetitive pieces.
- Art: Not bad, not good.
- The story has a few good twists and kept me engaged enough but was essentially very generic and quite samey through all the routes.
Cons:
- Short game, especially for the price.
- Not enough character development. I felt I got to know the heroine well but every other character felt rushed. You also have to choose a route knowing barely anything about these guys and you don't learn much more after.
- EXTREMELY misleading as an otome. Only two of the five routes actually leads to romance - Spoilers:
- The choices are kind of meaningless as, for the most part, the end you get in the game hinges on one or two choices with the vast majority of dialogue options offering absolutely nothing of impact.
So. I really disliked that this game misleads you into acting like more of an otome than it is, that's my biggest grind. As for the rest, the cons were just too big to really mean I could recommend this (especially at full price!) I got this for about £3.50 and felt it was fair enough but I wouldn't recommend spending any more on it and only buy it if you're really stuck for a game.

IMHO, this is one of the best and underrated MMOs I've player on my entire gaming life (20 years of gaming so far).
Why, you might ask me? I'll tell ya.
The background story is amazing and it mixes Fallout series, Mad Max movies and also A Boy and His Dog references (if you ever saw this movie, you, sir, consider yourself lucky). The game has an unique atmosphere aswell. Not only a futurist set, but a post-apocalyptic one, finely made.
The map is HUGE, I mean, HUGE (already tell ya that♥♥♥♥♥♥is huge?!). You could spent like 8-10 hours to cross the sectors on foot, if you make it alive.
Forget everything else about other's game crafting. This is THE♥♥♥♥♥♥
You can craft your own vehicles or train your own animals! Ride a mutant chicken or a horse (you can have many, many different kind of horses) or go in a bad♥♥♥♥♥mode on a bike.
You can craft almost everything, even tents, campsites and stuff like that to get temporary area buffs.
Craft armors, firearms, melee weapon, explosives, medicine, steroids, recipes, foods, drinks, mutagenics... the list is so big that probably I'd spend all the reviews talking about it.
Also, you need to craft ammunition for your weapons and gas, diesel or biodiesel for your vehicles, besides ration for your animals and repair kits for heal equipment damage from fights.
After all, even if it bothers some people, I must say that I LOVE the time required to crafting. Everything you make by crafting need proper time to get done, from just a few secs to hours or even weeks. A single tire for a car requires 8-12 hours.
It's a partial FPS where you need to land your blows and aim to shot manually. No auto-target, which is great for PvP. Headshots cause a lot of extra fatal damage, rewarding you for your skill player.
The game have a lot of customization, meaning your character can max various skills to fulfill different roles on a party or even solo. You could be a mutant DPS or a healer, a gunslinger, a rifleman, sniper, fight with a big axe, two tires, be a sneaking rogue, a buffer/debuffer leader or pretty much anything.
Awesome.
The game is partial-PvP. I mean, it's not a full PvP map, but, instead, we have PvP zones. On these zones, players need to fight over rare resources like petroleum! People can build settlements and siege-like stuff aswell.
The game has 6 factions which the player can join. Each one has it's owns charateristics, RP-related and PvP gear. These factions are at war/alliance relationships with each other.
The game also have a lot of player's guilds and alliances and people Pvping over resource nodes and PvP zones.
- Not just more of the same. It really brings something NEW and FRESH to MMO players looking for something special.
- F2P (doesn't matter to me, but it's nice to try for free if you're not sure about it).
- Buy, craft and dye clothes and use them over your regular armor on cosmetic slots. You can even paint and customize your car, bike, etc.
- Active, nice and helpful GMs; 24/7 on chat.
- A LOT OF DANCE MOVES, including MJ and the awesome Carlton Banks dance (Alfonso to his close friends).
- A LOT of creative skills that you don't see everyday.
- Welcoming and active community (don't let the Steam numbers fool you, cause the most people playing it are using the non-Steam client).
- Deep and beautiful scenarios.
- Scary voiceover (turn it off, man).
- You have a flashlight.
- Immersion feel on every step you take.
- Level up takes a long long time, giving you some sense of importance in the world.
- Awesome PvP.
- You can fight while riding or driving! Man, EVERY SINGLE MMO should have this. Drive fast while unloading a submachinegun clip on a pursuit, why not? Not a Fast & Furious type? You can do the cowboy Texas style aswell and shoot you Colt Anaconda on the horseback.
- You can have a dog! (anyone remember Dogmeat from Fallout 2?)
- Different paces of walking/driving/riding. You can walk, jog or run and drive/ride at speed as you like. Not so fast, no so slow, the way you want.
- One thing I dislike in this game is it's name. Should be called Awesome Earth.
- Performance issues on some PCs.
- "Dated" graphics (I've player UO for 11 years, ask me if I give a dame for graphics?!)
- "Hardcore", even not having a full loot system like Darkfall, Ultima Online and Mortal Online (love them all). What makes this game "hardcore" for some users is the fact that you need build and plan your character very carefully or it could be useless or disapointing at some point.
- Unfriendly interface and learning curve.
This game is AMAZING. If you want to have a unique gaming experience with an AWESOME soundtrack to match get this game. JET SET RADIOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO!

As I have said in my ETS2 review driving a virtual truck might not seem like the most exiting of things, but ATS just like ETS2 before it manages to achieve the improbable and actually makes it a very relaxing and fun experience to just start your favourite music on the radio and drive through the expansive roads, cities and small towns of California, Nevada, and Arizona delivering various goods and growing your trucking empire.
Both ETS2 and ATS have something unique to offer. ATS captures the feel of US roads pretty well particularly after the rescale SCS has done to make the map a lot bigger and complete. The diversity of companies and cargo is pretty good in my opinion, and the three states provide plenty of roads to drive, even if not as much as full ETS2. The complexity of cities is also better in ATS than in most parts of ETS2.
ATS definitely has a different feel to ETS2, the landscapes are new as well as road layouts and the overall feel is different to when I am driving in ETS2. You can definitely tell whether you are in Europe or the US and not just because of the truck you are driving.
The only downside of ATS currently is that it has only 2 truck brands with 4 truck models together; and it seems SCS is having a rather hard time getting new truck licenses so the wait for new trucks, if you don’t like using mods, might be rather long.
Overall ATS is a brilliant US truck simulator with a ton of potential when new states and new trucks are added in the future.

TL,DR : A great VN, overall I was very happy with it - but before you play, know that Callum's route is NOT unlocked until you finish the story once so don't let him be your first love interest.
PROS
Maddie was a great female lead - she had strengths (rational thinking and fighting skill) that made her admirable, but she also had flaws (most notably, her lack of empathy) that made her seem both human and likable.
Varied love interests, who may not be like the "first impression" they portray once you get to know them better.
Speaking of love, it's also nice to see that you have choices about how much of a focus you want to put on it. You can choose a love interest that will be your best friend, sweetly romantic dream, your soulmate, a practical business arrangement - or walk away from all that and choose just friendship.
I felt like my choices really did matter in the story. If you are dismissive or rude to another character, it can come back to haunt you - sometimes even cost you your life!
World-building is very good - I liked how noble women inherit from their mothers, yet must pick a husband to rule their lands as they become his "wisdom".
Music was beautiful and appropriate to the scenes, yet did not distract from the story. Sometimes I turn the game on "jukebox" mode to have the music play in the background, it's that nice.
The artwork was good, and I was pleased to see the varied facial expressions as the story unfolded.
NEUTRAL
The story was good, and the mystery unravels a piece at a time as you explore your connection with the different love interests. However, to make the most amount of sense, the routes really do need to be read in a certain order.
I did enjoy the political aspects of this game, but I also felt a bit unsatisfied there was no clear cut "villain" - there were just fallible humans who made dubious choices. The character who supposedly set this whole situation in motion is only mentioned, and does not appear in the story.
CONS
There is NO in-game notification to tell you Callum's route is not unlocked before you complete one story.
For 2 of 4 characters, if you are not on their route, they seem to fade into the background and not be involved in the story. Did these Princes really just sit around waiting to be chosen by Maddie, and otherwise do nothing?
Only 3 backgrounds? I feel there should be one for each of the main love interests! I was also disappointed the Duke got his own background while NONE of the main love interests did. *sighs* at least the palace BG is nice …
Final Thoughts ...
My first play through I tried everything in my power to get Callum's attention, yet I kept getting pushed toward Oscar, which made me more frustrated because I did not like his character - so I got a bad ending. :(
I was so angry I nearly requested a refund, but then when I looked through the forums it said that 1) Callum's route is locked until you complete one story, and 2) there is an "optimal" play through sequence for the most enjoyment and most sense out of the story.
I was really annoyed the game did not tell you these things, and you are expected to search through forums for the info - apparently before you even start the game! If the game is going to be laid out that way, that information really should be available in a in-game "getting started" file.
I almost walked away from this game because of this - but now I am glad I stuck it out. Overall I was very happy with the game. I would buy another game by Hanako Games, but now I know better to check for info such as optimal play sequence and not expect the story to be more free-flowing.

The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion has been my favorite open-world RPG, let alone my favorite game of all time for quite some time now. Set in fantasy medieval times on a distant, earth-like planet called Nirn, but with a variety of magic spells and creatures, you break out of jail as a tutorial and fend for yourself right outside the sewer exit. An extremely large map surrounds you while you have to scavenge for food, currency, weapons and armor. 250+ quests wait for you. The side-quests are of the plenty and they make your experience unique and amazing. A great level-up system is in place too, as you have to increase your skill levels to increase your overall level. Fantastic voice acting too. The downsides are that this is only a console port, so there are some bugs and a few broken quests in place, that had carried over from the console version as well. Control mapping is completely customizable, and seems well optimized. This game is so large that if I were to tell you everything about it, it could be a pretty thick book, so I'm just going to leave you with the rating and adventure.

This game is pretty good.  I beat the game on Tactition dificulty, and I found it to be a fun but challenging time, expecially early on.  While the previous game had several issues (The story not really picking up, the combat being about chain CCing) they have made efforts to change that.  Now the story picks up and keeps you engaged, and the combat requires you to adapt to the enemies actions combat turn order is a round-robin style.
That is not to say that the game is flawless.  On release, the game had bugs, and the character progression system is simplistic.  While none of the bugs kept me from beating the game there was certainly a few side quests that I couldn't complete or seemed to act strangely (However, I did a blind playthrough so its possible I missed something).  As for character progression, in my opinion, the Str, Fin, Int stats all do the same thing.  It mostly comes down to you putting 90% of your stats in your appropiate damaging stat, with a few in Memory, and finally the rest of your points in Wits (For Initiative/Secret Finding) or Con (For HP).  My main complaint is that what I described here can be a build for most characters, in that its not really a choice.
In my opinion, combat has been improved from the previous game.  No longer are you perma CCing enemies from round 1.  If you are not running many of the same damage types you might not be CCing much at all early on in a fight due to their magical / physical armors preventing it and being quite large.  No longer are you missclicking an enemy because their character's animation caused them to shift.  Nothing was worse in the first game then wasting all your action points moving around the target.  No longer is my friend taking 10 minutes a turn to spend his 20 action points.  The max being 6 means every point is more important.
Overall, I'd highly recomend this game.  Its one of the best CRPG's I've played in years.  The bugs will hopefully be fixed, which would make this game even better.

Here is a personal review of Stranger of Sword City. (from someone who does not know the Anime)
Hopefully I can be of a little help for you to decide on playing this game.
=Long story short=
If you like dungeon-crawling, multi-classing, grinding, and/or farming, get it.
If you like spending hours and hours building your character up, get it.
If you are a Wizardry fan, get it. Period.
=Short story long=
This is what you get.
Portrait - very nice built in portraits, import custom portraits
Age - Age affects times of death (can always heal so no problem here) and bonus roll points for attribute. Younger have more life, older has more bonus points.
Race - Human, Elf, Dward, Migmy (something like a Gnome in D&D), Ney (a cat/fox-human hybrid)
Talents - Fortunate (bonus attribue points), Educated (better identify items), Invincible (no one shot death), Intuition (better identify treasure/traps), Wild Eye (better finding secret doors)
Attributes - Strength, Intellegence, Piety, Vitality, Agility, Luck
Class - Fighter, Knight, Samurai, Ranger, Ninja, Dancer, Cleric, Wizard (no class has attribue requirements)
Character voice - Chose from 36 different voice (some good, some too mechanical). Attack, Damage, and Death voice.
Name and Nickname - (if you cannot chose, just name them the same)
6 equipment slots - Main hand, Off hand, Head, Body, Underwear, Accessory
Think this will cover the basic game system.
Here are my 'personal' pros/cons:
=Pros= (in no order)
Artwork of portrait
Custom portraits, importing custom portraits is just an awesome +
Control is very easy, could use only keyboard or mouse throughout the game (can customize hot-keys)
Interesting story line
Automatic mapping, auto-run to point already explored (this is a great option!)
Class change system (upto 5 times for a total of 6 classes)
Many different equipments (including Unique one-of-a-kind items)
Ambushing (or rather item farming - set up amush at certain map locations to steal chests)
=Cons=
Artwork of portrait (some artwork are mobs lol)
Control - There are no hot-keys for combat options (example [A]ttack, [D]efend, S[K]ill, [S]pell). So you will have to mouse click or navigate with movement keys.
Story line - The English text is very repetitive, don't know about Japanese. The plot giver (NPC) repeates the same thing in different wording many times. (my example: Make sure to give your mom a hug. Hug your mom, okay?. Don't forget to hug your mom before you leave. Huging your mom is showing that you appreciate her.)
Many different equipment (but many becomes obsolete - just trash, the stat difference between some equipment are too great)
One-hit-death, the critical strike (many people will think this as a con just because the mobs have it. But remember, you do also. Besides, there are skills and talent and spells that can protect you from them so not a big deal later on)
Not enough spells nor diversity
=Conclusion=
A little clumsy overall, but that's the attractiveness that keeps me going.
It's fun when you find a Dirty underwear +10 and think about wearing it because you have a Leather Undie +2.
Very very enjoyable game and is highly recommended for it's genre.
PS: don't forget to hug your mom =)

A currently in-Alpha Sandbox,Level-editor,Brawler and Parkour game, where the enviroment is your most effective weapon and the factor that usually determines your survival. (And no I don't mean that the Earth just engulfs your enemies when you're about to die)

Speaking of creating very intense parkour levels and such, The Level editor is great for allowing you to, as I stated above to create interesting and unique levels whether it be a large scale battle with swords and spears or an intense ninja parkour challenge, or both, you are able to create it, and if you are too lazy to build an interesting map or the base game materials aren't enough for you, theres a program created for modding the game known as the SUMLauncher(Supported by the Devs themselves) which instantly downloads and places the files in the correct areas so you can use them with no hassle of moving the files yourself, this program has lots of user created mods that range from maps to characters to props.
However the game is still in Alpha and if you're not the person to purhase early and follow a games progress untill its finished then perhaps wait until the game is finished as it is very worth it already in its current state, and I recommend getting it early and watching it grow and develop.

I have a long history and love affair with dungeon crawlers, starting with Might and Magic 1. I really enjoyed Etrian Odyssey 1-3. I've dabbled in Wizardry (mostly 8) and several of its misbegotten clones on multiple consoles, including the Vita. I think this game is hot garbage.
Yes, the art is cool. Since that's the big draw, the first complaint I have about this game is that the character art is split between the nice art, and woefully derivative anime garbage. This ensures that unless you want to jump through hoops to import your own art, you will actually have a very small selection of stylistically consistent portraits that will suit your race and class choices.
Next, this is a game with boring, been there done that races and classes. If you've played one copy-cat wizardry clone, you've played them all. Nothing to see here folks. The big gimmick for character customization is... a somewhat convoluted multi-class system. Take another boring, ho-hum class and grind extra? OH BOY, CAN I??
I thought Dancer would be cool, but it's actually completely useless at low levels. I've got a level 8 character doing a whopping 3 damage EVERY OTHER TURN (he has to set up, otherwise he does just one damage) in large part because the gear you find is very subject to RNG. Want a new dagger? Well, you can't buy one and you won't find it on a regular monster or in a treasure chest, heck no! Better wander the same labrynths over and over again, treading back to the same designated areas where you can "ambush" the same "unsuspecting" monsters and their bizarre supply trains carrying mostly the same low level crap you don't need to nowhere in particular. Why does this make sense again?
This game's idea of "challenge" is to sometimes throw a monster 10-14 levels higher than normal into a crowd, with the same sprite as a normal mob. Forgetting to check is one of the few ways to actually die in this game that I have found. I did forget to check once. It's not that the monster quickly killed me either - it just wouldn't die and eventually it ground me out through a war of attrition from which I could not successfully flee. Challenging? No. Tedious? Yes.
I'll admit that 10 hours ain't much for a game like this. Heck, I probably spent at least 2 hours of that rolling stats in the character generator (the rolls are very stingy - prepare to roll a lot of zeros!). But in only the second dungeon, somebody thought it would be a fun mechanic to spin the party in a random direction in every intersection while simultaneously turning off your compass in intersection squares. Just... why? Why would you punish your players so? I'm just trying to fill in my map, fight monsters and get loot. Do you think I want to be stopped in my tracks multiple times and be forced to study repetitive wall textures so that I can turn myself back the way I was supposed to be going in the first place? One brilliant 4-way intersection has no distinguishing features no matter which direction you turn, so you just have to guess. Oops, wrong way! Oops wrong way! Serously. I have no patience for games that blatantly waste my time.
Yes, this game looks nice. So go look at the art somewhere, but don't waste your time or your money here. This crap might fly on a dead handheld, but not on glorious PC. There are much better games you could be playing.

SOSC, I have a love-hate relationship with this game honestly. It's one of the most enjoyable and well-constructed JRPG Dungeon Crawlers to come up as of late, yet is is also one of the most brutal ones. I will review only "Normal" difficulty and up, will not review "Easy". Tl;dr; A MUST-PLAY for any JRPG or Dungeon Crawler fan.
Pros:
+ Beautiful artwork.
+ Top-notch soundtrack and SFX
+ Interesting story with enough plot twists.
+ Good amount of classes, each unique on their own.
+ Game mechanics are very refined and work well.
+ Replay value is there, but only for people that want to challenge the game to its maximum.
+ Good tutorials and easy to get into.
+ In-depth character planning and building.
Cons:
+ There is a lot of grinding for gear and levels involved if you want to challenge the game at its highest difficulty.
+ A lot of planning involved in creating character builds long-term.
+ The game is hard, brutal at moments. You can fight lv 10 enemies, next fight you might be against lv 25 ones. Check before you fight. I like this, most people don't.
+ End-game and NG+ bosses are hard, like hard. Without proper builds and gear, higher difficulties will make you struggle, a lot.
+ Bonus stat roll is a horrible system. Use cheat engine to give yourself a reasonable roll if you value your sanity, or you can roll for like 30-40 minutes per character to get a +10 roll (which you need if you want to challenge NG+).
Graphics:
Game is beautiful, artwork feels very unique and J-like. The ground tiles leave something to be desired, but the characters, menus, effects and cut-scenes look amazing. 8/10.
Sound:
The sound is top-notch, character dialogues (that are voiced) feel authentic (at least with Japanese audio) and cut-scene audio feels just about right. You can choose between a lot of character sound sets for your characters. 9/10.
Gameplay:
Very in-depth character building system long-term. You can literally take hours to plan your party's classes, gear and skills. Game features a class-change system, where characters can switch from class to another, keeping skills and stats, but losing spell (for casters). Some classes serve only for their skills, some serve as a main final class. Characters can die, depending on their LP, I mean die-die, permanently, depending on their age. Critical hits kill your characters in this game, but can be prevented in certain ways. 9/10.
Story:
I won't spoil it, but the story is well-written. It gets stale at times, but has a good amount of twists that keep you guessing. Not something out of this world, but it's very unique and interesting in its own right. 8/10
Replay Ability:
8/10 for hardcore fans that want to challenge NG+ (which is, mind you, considerably harder).
3/10 for casual players that just want to experience the game.
Verdict Score:
9/10 for J-RPG or Dungeon Crawler Fans.
6/10 for people not familiar with the JRPG genre or looking for an easy game to go through for the story.

An engaging and immersive cyberpunk point n click adventure game with a great story and likeable characters. The story has interesting themes and is portrayed in an interesting fashion. The voice acting fit the characters well and they were all unique. I also liked how the music was very understated and complimented the scenes nicely. It was definitely satisfying to play through to the end and see how the story unfolded, leaving a very satisfying conclusion.
The graphics are beautifully drawn and make the world feel immersive. Some backgrounds are only seen for a few seconds yet are still richly detailed and almost breathtaking to look at, so I commend the developer for that.
The puzzles hit the right balance between challenging and logical, there weren't any weird and crazy parts of the game's internal logic. Some areas of the game can be a little tricky and annoying to figure out which part of the map to go to next as you backtrack through familiar areas a few times but nothing too egregious.
There is combat through gunplay. Instead of just pressing the use button on gun and clicking on an enemy in a traditional point n click style, there is combat where the player takes cover, aims, and has to time their shots in the minigame. While it isn't very complex, it breaks up the puzzles and provide an interesting way of doing action in a style of game like this. I noticed a couple of glitches such as when a sprite in the background would be placed on the top layer in front of my character in the foreground, but this only happened twice.
Definitely recommended for people who enjoy interesting sci-fi cyberpunk stories with good voice acting and story, especially considering that the majority was drawn, written and programmed by just one student, so props to him for making such an engaging and interesting game. Worth checking out, especially for the really neat easter eggs.

Summary
As a story, Royal Trap isn’t BAD per say. The writing was well done, but it does lack depth. Madeleine is a poor younger sister noble that found her way into service to Prince Oscar. Together, they embark to a neighboring empire in hopes to woo their princess into marriage. After a series of events Madeleine is accused of treason and imprisoned where she must somehow regain her honor and reputation. Do not read spoilers, if you don’t want to know what happens. Unfortunately, some of the biggest flaws were in the story and it was hard to avoid mentioning them.
Plot 2/5
The plot is a bit TOO simple.
Villain 2/5
Who is the real villain?
Romance 2/5
There really isn’t a whole lot of romance. It is not necessarily a bad thing, but it might be for some. One seems like the obvious route and does attempt to spice things up between the two characters.  Two other characters paths just seem to be the result of circumstances, familiarity, and convenience.  Another seems forced by the fact it happens quickly in its intensity, but probably the next best path after the obvious one. I haven’t finished Dolores, yet.
Story Branches 2/5
There is not a huge difference between story paths. It is the same plot, the same conflict, and the same villain. The only difference is how it gets resolved and who Madeleine receives help from.
Madeleine aka Main Character 4/5
Madeleine is pretty much the star character in Royal Trap. The most rounded and complete character. She has a lot of personal thoughts, insights, and reflections. She is also likable.
Other Suitors/Characters 3.5/5
The characters were different and decent. The only thing really holding most of them back was the lack of story depth.
Final thoughts:
I think I am finished writing the review and I suppose I will give it a recommendation based on the fact it had potential and good writing, but the story could have been much better with depth. It JUST passed my recommendation, but barely. I could have lived without it, but I enjoyed the political aspect of ideas. Sigh. What a wasted potential of what it could have been. I would not buy this game at full price. If you are going to give it a try, do it when it is on sale.
I guess I should also add that most of the bad and normal endings were REALLY short. I mean really short. I started getting that feeling again, in some of them, that they might has well put up the "ending" sign with a "you suck" to it.

When at -50% discount or more, it's a refreshing purchase for a fan of otome.
I found the
to be a pleasant and amusing way to pass the time. While I've completed all the routes now, I haven't necessarily read every dialogue choice. I also would not mind playing through again in order to read out to my partner. I would be lying if I said the courtly intrigue attempted comes across as a bit daft. Still, it's quite an intriguing experience if you don't mind a bit of fluffiness. Is there room for improvement? Certainly. But I do think this title has encouraged me in my positive views of Hanako Games.
Contrary to what somebody else stated in a review, I do not find Madeliene to be a "Mary Sue". Depending on your choices, she can be bested in battle, require assistance, find herself baffled, wind up acting like a complete jerk, wandering into traps, and all sorts. She has merits and flaws. Her strengths turn to weaknesses at important points. Why is she a "dual wielding ninja"? Well, that was how she was trained to be. If she were a man, would we be looking at that aspect with as much scrutiny? Perhaps.
Still, it's not accurate to suggest she's the idealised version of somebody else, pushed into a stereotypical role. If she were she'd never need the help of her friends. Simply because characters do tend find her charming and clever does not mean that she's "perfect". And they don't always think of her as such.
As for the other characters, they range from adequate to amusing/sassy/adorable. There is a sinister feel to some of them... up to a point. The
treacherous character is only mentioned, never seen. This is one of the failings of the game, I feel. Either way, the rest of the characters have their flaws--though certainly some are less impactful than others--and who do have more than one dimension to them. I personally would have fleshed out areas more yet I can't find it in me to complain too much.
+ Appealing graphics, both for backgrounds and sprites.
+ Character sprites were not
static.
+ A fairly coherent plot line with some bizarre twists.
+ Further playthroughs often add extra information and even when they don't, you still have different conversations and occurrences.
+ The music is enjoyable (I didn't feel the need to turn it off as I do in many VNs).
+ Humour/humourous sitations which generally manage not to overthrow the story's point.
+ There is at least one Happy, non-romantic ending. You can add your own head-canon to it but that's on you to decide.
+ If you don't complete all the routes you won't necessarily work out everything that is happening.
+ I would also have enjoyed further female romance options and for the one which is available to be more "explicit"; there is a rather controversial aspect to the main plot, that sideline could have been added to.
+ Some of the Happy Endings might be seen as over-the-top?
+ Some additional sound effects would have been nice although there are enough to get by with.
+ I feel the rather "out there" plot aspect was handled maturely, however certain dialogue choices could lead to the main character saying things which might upset certain individuals. Those choices lead to a bad ending but they do give the option of seeing the protagonist voicing an opinion in a way that others may not enjoy but is not intentionally cruel.

+ I would have like to see further expression and movement from the characters.
+ Reading the fight sequences felt rather tiresome.
+ People may not enjoy the cliff-hanger aspect of several endings. I was fine with them but I can see why others would not be.

Conan Exiles is very fun, somewhat addictive survival game with some incrediblely fun perks and some potentially fatal flaws.
I love the game overall, there is so much to do if you like building bases/forts/castles or just a little hut in the oasis.  Grinding levels on mobs, on animals or via crafting is almost a subset of the game,  levels happen as youre fighting to survive and expand your home base.
Speaking from a mostly PVE experience the buildings are enjoyable,  although the shapes are somewhat limited at the moment there is a massive amount of possibilities for the future.  The Day night cycles are exciting and often terrifying at the same time.  I find myself outfitting for a planned expedition 1 or 2 days in advance of leaving my base. Got food?  got water? got weapons and materials for repairs?  ok,  wait for next day to dawn and head out!
All in all one of the best games ive played for 30 dollars,  almost 200 hours of enjoyment on an EARLY access game (key note there) is less than 15 cents an hour of value!!  and it has so many places it can expand.
Now for the horrifying bads,  even as an early access game it had a horrendous start with servers stability and control, although much is fixed now, Ive left a scattered trail of broken attempts at homesteads on a number of servers.
DESPAWNING THRALLS.  this,  In my humble opinion is one of the most dissapointing aspects of the game, people were able to build on areas where limited resources are, causing them to permanently despawn.  On one of my favorite servers, #208 there is literally 1 camp left of any size with thralls in it.  What are Thralls you ask?  well,  slaves in the making!  you basically knock them out,  drag them home and break their will till they are willing to protect, amuse or enarmour you! Making thralls not despawn permanently under any circumstance, AND giving them incredibly potent attacks against player bases would make it a serious hazard to build on or very near to NPC locations.  (heres hoping for a future fix)
Over all Id give this title a solid 4 of 5 stars,  If you enjoy the Conan fantasy, and live survival games, this one is a no brainer for 30 bucks!

I've found eventually a webpage link duried deep in the discussion boards that lists what looks like an hour or two testing and fixing this, that and the next thing, and the excuse given is that some part of the middle-ware seems to not work with some computers...and that's my spare time for a bit of gaming down the pan.
Seems a crock to me. I paid full price for the game, which did work once upon a time, and now it's unplayable. I shouldn't have to be scratching my head and fixing errors. In this state, I can't recommend it. I will say that it has enormous potential and needs the Dev's to fix it.

I've tried to get into Oblivion several times now, and I never seem to end up making it terribly far.  The interface has undergone a huge upgrade since Morrowwind, which is welcome, but the overall gaming experience has taken a HUGE hit.
The year Oblivion was the game of must have been a very slow one - there's NO way this game warrents a perfect score.  The graphics are trying hard to be good, rather than actually BEING good, which makes a huge difference in practice.  Textures are servicable, yet bland, and the facial animations are terrifying.  The lighting is straight up awful, and the voice acting is so bad it's tedious.  The story is just another bland, generic "go kill the big bad" with no sense of urgency or danger, and you end up a second banana to the GM's Pet NPC anyway.
Bethesda falls into the same trap here as Fallout 3 - trying to ape the success of a previous game (in this case Morrowwind) without understanding what made that game good in the first place.

Despite being a massive fan of the original Dungeon Keeper games, I decided to hold off on buying this game at release because of the mixed reviews it was getting, saying that it still wasn't finished etc. but eventually I gave in a bought the game a little while after Heart of Gold was released, and all I can say is that this is definately the spiritual successor to Dungeon Keeper that I have always asked for.
A lot of the the early problems that I saw have been fixed for the most part and there's is now plenty of content that has been added to the game to keep you coming back, and it suits all of the play styles. You have the main campaign which despite being relatively short, is good at introducing the new features of the games such as Sins, Beasts and Potions and such, and there are plenty of side objectives you can go through for repeat playthroughs to keep you going, same goes for the Heart of Gold campaign, which improves in a lot of ways on the original campaign.
There are also the other game modes including Crucible, a survival styled mode where you have to fight against oncoming hoards of enemies. Skirmish for playing online and against AI. Sandbox for just having the freedom of building your dungeon. Also the recently added My Pet Dungeon mode which had taken the elements from the original Dungeon Keeper 2 game, and improved upon it by adding basically a small campaign with multiple maps and objectives to complete at your own time.
Though this wouldn't go without a few faults with the game I feel there still are, though recently improved upon, I still find the possesion to be a little finicky when it comes to attacking enemies. Also there is a little bit of a lack of variety when it comes to creatures for your dungeon, but Crucible did help this by adding new varieties, and you can also convert a lot of the enemy hero units.
Overall I'd say if you were a fan of the original game give this game a go, and even if you're interested in the genre try it out. Though it may not be for everyone I still had a great time and couldn't reccomend it more.
