Easily one of the most enjoyable games I have ever played.
Jet set Radio, originally known as Jet Grind Radio on the dreamcast, is most easily relatable to Tony hawk's pro skater mixed with a grafitti simulator. The gameplay consist of timed challenges that can vary from racing your grafitti crew, to covering all the other gang's grafitti in town. Though sometimes the controls may feel clunky, I found that there were rarely any problems that forced me to restart the level. (I played the entirety of the game with a keyboard and mouse instead of a controller as well.) I did find that after chapter 1, there was a difficulty spike that caught me off guard, that was the only spike in difficulty in the entire game, it stayed steady and fun after that.
The character roster in this game is also pretty big, with characters you unlock throughout the story, as well as secret characters. I did find that some characters had pretty OP stats in comparison to others. YoYo especially, he pretty much has his technique and grafitti maxed. Other than that, character roster is awesome.
This game looks amazing, the colorful, cell shaded style reminds me of wind waker a bit, but with more of a comic book feel to it, which I adore. The texture quality isn't very high, but that's to be expected for a game that origninally came out in the late 90's to early 2000's.
Just a side note, this game runs on pretty much any computer, which is amazing.
I saved the best for last, thought I missed the soundtrack didn't you? No way, this soundtrack is unforgetable. The soundtrack feels like a fantastic mixtape of what someone would actually listen to, with songs that range from hip-hop, to rock, and back again. My personal favorites of the bunch are "Sneakman" and "Rock it on".
If you're on the fence about purchasing this game, I can very simply say, it's worth it.
Now I just have to wait for Sega to make J.S.R.F HD. Haha.

This game is more expansive than you would think.
My experience with interactive novels prior to Tin Star were despicable, to say the least. Now I'm pretty much stalking the company that makes this game.
Tin Star is an interactive novel that can go almost any avenue you can think of. You can name yourself, or choose from a set of names. You can be a man or a woman, and of either gay or straight sexuality. Doctor, lawyer, or I think something else. You can be a good marshal, bad marshal, decent marshal, questionable marshal. it all depends on how you play the game; what sides you take, who you shmooze and who you shoot.
When I played the demo I ended up as a lawyer, froze to death on my way to my job, retried, then ended up friends with a Mormon cowboy who'd just had a calf shot by a prospector. I shmoozed to the head of the town and angered a woman in a saloon who almost shot a guy for touching her leg (though he was apprently after more).
Each character has a story, and you can become close to almost all of them. Your influence and persuasion over them can fluctuate depending on your actions and your influence on them decides what happens in the future (they gonna save you from a shot, or loot your body when your dead?). You don't even have to follow through with the whole plotline; you can say f*ck it all  halfway through and just skip town and stop being a marshal. You can go to Mexico. You can be a womanizer, a sharpshooter, a friend of the Native Americans or a target of everyone who sees you.
Really it's interesting. I will definately play this game through again. The dialoug and otherwise also shifts slightly depending on whether you are a woman marshal or a male marshal; it also shifts, though very slightly, if your relationship is not of the heterosexual sort.
How you act determines whether or not you are remembered. Whether or not you tell people your name or your title as marshal might effect whether or not your deeds have your name stuck on them; the events may be remembered, but will the marshal?
Or you can be a total utter♥♥♥♥♥♥and be remembered because you shot at everyone and gave a middle finger to the Natives, the Sheriff, everyone in town and the damn mountains for all you care. F*ck those mountains. They can kiss your♥♥♥♥♥
You can stand by and do nothing. You could practically not be there; just sit and watch and let the town fall to ruin or blow itself up, long as you get your coffee and your pay.
Some consequences are unexpected, some are funny, some are fair.
All the writing in this is very good as well. Allen Gies put a good effort into presenting the scenes too you simply but thouroughly. You can get a real feel for the geography around you and the town - Preston Springs - that you reside in. He also did well with characters and the dialouge isn't too bad either (though cheesy in some parts, but not like painful cheesy at all).
You can also check your stats on your influence and skill in various areas (I reccomend viewing this in both 'graph' and 'story' mode). There's the occasional spelling/grammar mistake, but they aren't noticeable unless you re-read the scene a million times.
Please, please, please get this game. It really is fun and there is an interaction literally every page but a few interleude ones, and there not that long or frequent. I also personally think that you'll find out a bit about yourself if you just go ahead with your own choices, abide by your morals and what you might do. It's pretty interesting.
Now start your adventure and find out whether your a legend or just a total, unrelenting, feather♥♥♥♥♥♥

I'm not a fan of Westerns all that much. What intrigued me about this title was it's epic length, and that it sounded interesting in that you take on the role of a US Marshall on the Old West frontier. There's not a lot specifically about the story that I can say that will not be full of spoilers, so I will refrain; however, this is one incredibly well-done story, full of far-reaching choices. You can be a dastardly, terribly corrupt lawman, or be a paragon of virtue. The ending Epilogue pretty much shines a light on everything you did during the game, and tells you of the far-reaching consequences as a result.
The only thing I didn't like is the numerous typos ("their" instead of "they're," "peaked" instead of "piqued," and several others); this was especially the case in the latter half of the game. Maybe it's not that big a deal, but if a game is going to be presented in a written medium, it really should be super-tight when it comes to editing and proofreading. Still, a commendable effort if several were caught in the making, as the author thanks numerous people for doing so. I would have loved to have helped proofread this to catch the dozens that I did see while going through it.
Still, none of that is a big deal. I felt an emotional bond to the character, felt some stirrings in the legacy I left behind, and truly enjoyed every moment. I especially liked that it was a long one! Seven hours is quite long for an interactive fiction game, and the author should be commended for his efforts, as well as Choice of Games for publishing this.

Check out the gameplay video below to see how the game plays:
What is it?
Swordy is a top-down physic brawler made primarily for local multiplayer.  Players can pick up a variety of weapons and swing them or hack away to try and bring down their opponents.  It does have single player aspects such as the ability to play against bots and single-player 'missions' which are fun but the real bread and butter of the game lies in a bunch of friends smashing each other with hammers for laughs.
How does it play?
The game plays smoothly.  Controls are easy to understand but challenging to master.  There doesn't appear to be any keyboard control (at least, not that I could find) but the game seems to really suit a controller anyway, being clearly designed for twin stick control.
Who would enjoy it?
If you like to play casual games with a group of friends, I can see you having a great time with this.  If stuff like Ultimate Chicken Horse or Overcooked are your thing, then this will be right up your alley.
Pros:
+ Crisp, responsive controls.
+ Really nice design aesthetic
+ Good variety of weapons with different physics/feeling.
+ Dev team seems to be very active and involved in progressing the game.
Cons:
- UI is a bit clunky and unclear to navigate.
- No online multiplayer support (and I don't think this is something that will be implemented).
- The shader really impacts upon frame rate (I don't have a top end graphics card (AMD HD7970) and I could still get 55 fps or so but my framerate pretty much doubled when I turned off the shaders entirely).
Overall, if you like local multiplayer brawlers, this is well worth your time, IMHO.

NiGHTS Into Dreams remains one of the best games from the Sega Saturn. NiGHTS HD recreates the Sega Saturn classic with the addition of a theater mode and art gallery, plus the Christmas NiGHTS extra story.
The game ultimately boils down to speed runs. There are 7 stages in total and the aim is to rack up the highest score by chaining links, combos and performing acrobatic stunts, all the while collecting dream energy to unlock special dream energy and returning it to the checkpoint. The game can be a little tricky to figure out at first but once you learn the patterns, you will have fun flying through the levels at high speed. My only concern is the controls doesn't quite have the same finese that the original has, but I am using an Xbox360 Controller. I would like to try this game with Steam's own controller.
There is also the option to explore the worlds a little and admire their design, however if you take too long the game pushes you to complete the level. This isn't a bad thing as afterall you are in a dreamworld.
A game that was developed in 1996 still stands as having some of the most imaginateive landscapes and character designs. Each level is a representation of the characters emotions and the challenges they must overcome in real life, The levels are bright and colourful and you often spot something you never noticed the last time you played the level. After the wonderful dream levels are the darker boss nightmare stages which contrast the adventure levels. The boss levels just feel like a nightmare and give you the sence of dread.
The HD textures and character models are really good, and there is an option to play in Saturn mode, with the low poly models. Unfortunately the Saturn mode also reduces the screen to it's original 6:4 format.
While the game is excellent, and it has all the charm of it's original. I still find myself wanting to play the original. However, I still highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a quick game to pick up and play a few rounds after coming home from school or work. You are looking at maybe 5 hours worth of Gameplay if you want to get all the achievements,

I wish this game did a better job of advertising its difficulty level.  I thought I was buying a casual game, but that's not what I got.
Quest Run is a cute game that doesn't try to be anything grand, and it succeeds at what it does.  You have several different classes of adventurers with limited equipment slots and skills, some ability to maneuver them, and a couple of random events - and that's about it.  The art style is pleasing, and it's easy to pick up in a short time.
However, the game is punishing.  I was shocked when, in the middle of a tutorial, my entire party was slaughtered.  That was a taste of things to come: I soon found that trying to go beyond the two tutorial dungeons meant losing every single time - hardly a lot of fun, or what I expected.  You did gain some gold from each attempt, fail or succeed, but that's it - nothing else stayed with you.  There was no sense of levelling up your characters or equipment - in fact, you were assigned different characters in each dungeon, meaning that you didn't really get to know their strengths and weaknesses without replaying the raid.  A lot.
And you have to replay a lot: there are some upgrades you can buy, like pets with abilities or additional classes, but they cost thousands of gold pieces - and you get around 150 for finishing a quest.  If you need an upgrade to seize victory, then you're going to have to replay the same raid dozens of times to save up enough - and then hope that it was worth it, since the descriptions are vague at best.
I get the impression that QuestRun is a lot like FTL or Rogue Legacy, both roguelike games in which there is a steep learning curve, and you're not expected to survive to the end of the game until you've put dozens of hours into it.  There certainly is a skill to playing QuestRun, as you come to understand the strengths and weaknesses of each class and try out different strategies.  I just with the game held your hand a little more, or that you had the chance to play through a quest or two that wasn't a tutorial without having your♥♥♥♥♥handed to you by the game.  Otherwise, you end up feeling like the developer is laughing at your feeble efforts, and that's hard to enjoy.
In the end, QuestRun is a good game, but not a game I can enjoy.  I wanted something that would be fun from the beginning, and instead I got a game that requires a lot of time and effort.  A lot of people will enjoy that, but I have other games I play when I want that.  I don't feel ripped off, but I wish I'd read the forums before buying.

Fun game, alot of content. Very optimized, even low end pc's should be able to play it. It's pay to skip, but theres not much need to, the grind is pretty fair. Platinum can be traded between players by trading mods and other items, and can be bought at a discount(25%,50%,75%) with coupons that drop from daily login bonus. You farm resources from enemies and containers during missions and use that to build stuff. All warframes and weapons can be built, though some weapons are event exclusive or are earned another way.
There are currently 30+ warframes along with 100's of weapons to obtain. Dozens of mods for each category (warframe, primary, secondary, melee, companion) exist which allow you to customize your gear however you like. Each warframe has 4 abilities and different attributes(health, shield, armor) to fit just about any playstyle. Weapons come in many forms rifles, bows, shotguns, throwing knives, beam cannons, swords, whips, hammers and many others. Compainions include sentinals/kubrows/kavats(robot/dog/cat) which help fight enemies and assist with various skills.
Art and sound is overall high quality. While the game is quite playable it is still being worked on, new features are frequently added and patches are common. Digital Extremes interacts with the community often and engages in open disscussion via thier Devstreams on twitch. Community on the whole is friendly, clans can be joined to talk and trade with other players.

Game has a major nostalgic hold on me. Played this game waaaaay back when I was younger on the dreamcast, cept I never 'played' it, I always freeskated in the tutorial.
That was a regret I always held, not seeing this game through. Thanks to the rerelease in HD, I was able to have this flashback back in time, and I saw it through to the end.
The game is very good in terms of style, looks, soundtrack, and challenging challenges. It is, however, still an old game. Keep that in mind if you plan on buying it. The creators of video games back then arn't as advanced as they are nowadays. There are things that don't work right, AI that is hard to beat, and annoying moments where you wanted to do one thing but the game did another.
Game shouldn't be judged on that, however. If you never played this game and expect it to be a fantastic game with no flaws  then you really don't know how video games work. That's like playing the classic Super Mario on the NES and saying 'this game needs a massive overhaul.'
Another recommendation of mine is to play this game with a controller. It is compatible with controllers and is very fun with one, otherwise you need to discover a way for you to play with keyboard / mouse with ease.
This game, however, is a fantastic example on where video games were turning and how much pop-culture / hip-hop influenced the world. We can look at this game and understand how times were back in the day. Take a trip back to memory lane with Jet Set Radio (and hope to god they release Jet Set Radio: Future).

It's a "SimHeros" type of game in the prespective of a city manager. imagine, Farmville with a much faster pace and you manage the heroic part of a kingdom instead of farming tomatoes and eggplants.
You are the leader of a brand new kingdom, your objective is becoming the most glorious and recognised kingdom of the land (you compete with other AI kingdoms).
In order to progress you need to complete quests (loads and loads...), take care of you towns and manage you "microkingdom".
The questing is basically assigning a hero or group of heroes to a specific quest, considering the particular equipment and stats combination to get the best result possible. Quests and your heroes quest performance are central to the game. It's how you gain fame a level up your kingdom, allowing more buildings, more heroes, more buildings....
In your kingdom, well, Townville... Build building, make money, buld more buildings, add abilities and great stuff, build more buildings....
Everything is very fast paced, and it gets faster with each kingdom leveling up... You easily lose track of time playing this puppie.... Very simple... very addictive.
Not a masterpiece, but it's worth your money, specially if you are someone that played #something#ville, #something#clickers, and likes to manage eficiently... cof cof... i'm very very tidy and efficient... You should listen to me. :P

Tapocalypse a clicker game. Period. It's tagged on Steam as "Racing Indie RPG Simulation Clicker" but at the end it is should simply say Clicker.
Gameplay:
Set in a post-apocalyptic game you play as a someone on a rugged vehicle who kills enemies spawning continously from the left, via clicking.
That is all there is to it. There are a million levels and upgrades but game boils down to just clicking.
Graphics:
Graphics look good, it's a game made in Unity. The design and game aesthetics are great.
Music/Sound Design:
Music is good but repetitive and the sound effects are well made.
Pros:
-It looks good.
-Lots of upgrades.
-Endless level ups.
Neutral:
-It's a clicker...
Cons:
-No matter how many upgrades and level ups there are, the entire game just boils down to clicking.
Conclusion:
If you like these sort of games, go for it. Knowing that the game is all about clicking, and possibly destroying your mouse's microswitch in the process :P, you can make an informed choice.
As far as clickers go, it's a good one. It looks good, it sounds good, it has that endless gameplay setup.

2. I'm not sure if this works from the beginning or if it's linked to some prestige tokens i already spent... however:
get 270 fuel
buy a bot as support
go to main menu
instantly start the game again
grab the bonus shown on the left side
enjoy your ~40k+ fuel
repeat as often as you like and maybe even soft reset while still in area 2
bonus even gets larger as you get more support units and advance further in the game

I never played Jet Set Radio back in the day, but I saw this for 99c on humble bundle (god bless them) so I thought I'd give it a go. 40+ hours later I can confirm it was that deal of the century.
Now I admit this game has it's fair share of flaws, controlling the skater feels clunky at first, the difficulty curve is a little uneven, and the camera will drive you mad (before you start I recommend heading into the options and turning 'center camera' off). But damn it was all worth it. Even after getting all the achievements and playing the whole game through 5 times(!) I still wanted to come back for more.
Like many classic Sega games such as Nights and super monkey ball, JSR is very much an arcade experience. The joy is in chasing high scores, mastering the levels and finding sweet lines (ala tony hawks) to rack up huge combos. I found the game most fun after I'd completed the (occasionally infuriating) story mode and was free to explore the levels without fear of being flamethrowered, or shot by helicopters.
I've seen Jet Set Radio get a lot of flack (especially from those without the rosy tinted goggles of nostalgia) but I would say the good points definitely outweigh the bad. For €4 can you really go that far wrong?

In Tin Star, you play a US Marshal, presumably occupied with Honor, Law, and Order (there are stats for each category).  My primary complaint about the game is that it offers too much individual freedom, to the point of departing from its premise.  What kind of Marshal blows up dams, robs wagons and shoots people under no provocation?  While many scenarios have diplomatic solutions, violence isn’t only a last resort.  In other words, I think the story might have been more convincing if the player had other careers to choose from, as opposed to being made a Marshal by default.
That being said, any fan of RPG’s should welcome Tin Star.  It’s constructed like a massive Western D&D campaign and is both one of the longest and most interactive titles by Choice of Games.  The challenges it offers are numerous and inventive, avoiding the grindy repetition typical of the RPG genre.

Gemini Rue is a point-and-click adventure game with a noire-ish science fiction theme (kind of like Blade Runner). This game was developed with Adventure Game Studio, so the graphics are extremely low resolution by any standard (320 x 200). In spite of this very low standard of graphics, the game plays very well. The point-and-click mechanics all work very well, you can interact with the environment, use inventory items, climb boxes and ladders, and engage in dialogs with characters. The main appeal of Gemini Rue is the sci-fi story. It is a very ambitious and dramatic story told without a hint of sarcasm. There are times when the story really pulls you in, which is the sign of a good story.
There are also times were the story falls flat, where you can tell that the writer is a very ambitious college student (Josh Nuernburger). For instance, Boryokudan means "violent gang" in Japanese, and is the official, boring name that Japanese police have given the Yakuza so they sound less romantic. It seems Mr. Nuernberger decided Japanese was cool and typed "mafia" into an online translator. The way this word is pronounced by the voice actors is also bad. "Boryokudan" is very difficult for an English speaker to say correctly, and the voice actors have merely pronounced the word as it is spelled, with no attempt at approximating the Japanese pronunciation.
The voice acting for the main characters is very good. Azriel (the main character) and the Director are excellent. For some of the lesser characters (the street vendor in particular) it seems that they just grabbed somebody off the street to read the lines.
There is some challenge to this game in terms of figuring out what is going on and what is the logical next action to take, so it is engaging without being too difficult. There are a few puzzles in the game but none that I got stuck on. There were two instances where I got stuck and consulted a walkthrough, but this won't be necessary for most people (I tend to get impatient). There are a few action sequences involving shooting which are very easy.
Overall I would say this is an excellent game for people who like point-and-click adventures and sci-fi stories. While very enjoyable, tt is not a perfect game and the graphics and production can seem a little amateurish at times.

Mouse and keyboard now work, it feels like a great use of the mouse... though controllers will always feel better, there is just one more reliable player to play the game at your parties... single player experience is "there" but not satisfying/fun enough to purchase the game for a SP experience. *Review made a few days after EA release*
Swordy is not for every PC, make no mistake, Swordy is a niche game requiring Multiple controllers (with the recent and solid addition of Keyboard and mouse) , Friends, and a willingness to wait until those meetups to play the game... (and it only really starts getting fun with a third (or more) person(s) too)...
To those having a Party with a few friends around, Must grab.
To those looking for a single player experience, Don't get it yet, Wait a few months and see how the single player modes progress and then re-evaluate
Swordy is a Unique "Arena Party Game" In the vein of "Starwhal" or "Duck Game" or "SpeedRunners". They are great, fun, and silly... though there's a few drawbacks out there.
Most of these Arena party games are platformers... and too many people have WAAAY different skill levels in platformers to make them fun or fair.
This game is a lot more like starwhal "new" control scheme, a game where most people are unfamiliar with the controls, starting everyone off on a level playing field.
What this game has going for it is a really strong sense of "Honourable combat", "Casual rulemaking" and "Improvisation mid combat"
"Looking at each other across the arena, blood has been spilled, but both your weapons are aflame... the rain starts... everything else seems to fade into the background, Slowly spinning up the hammer, charging forwards, both you and them start screaming..."
Moments like that seem to flow and occur naturally, Blows and weapon exchanges seem just right, your opponents rarely outskill you to the point of futility, and when amazing dagger throws do happen, there's nothing but awe across the couch. It feels like one of the few local multiplayer games where battlecries feel appropriate and easy to do. The game is really good at encouraging "epic memorable moments", everything feels fair (even when it's unfair).
The game is also nice in offering casual rulemaking. You have an immediately apparent unspoken social contract for politeness, a weapon selection as required, not needing to go into a "Mutators screen" to disallow certain items... as most friends are amiable to not allow swords, or to only go for punches, or overhead attacks... it's just really nice and refreshing not having to go back out to a menu to get that stuff done.
It's also really nice to see a bit of panic mode support, where your thrown weapon misses the target, and now you're running away from a psycho with a flaming spear, grabbing and tossing everything in your path to try escape... until either you manage to pick up another dagger and fling it at him... hopefully with a little more luck this time... or you run into a wall and get skewered...
Really, this is just an essential party game that doesn't lose it's lustre quickly, Get it if you're sick of platformers as your only party game options for sure. Get it if you're the type that can convince their friends to bring two controllers over.

One of the central aspects to any Elder Scrolls title is being able to play how you like and go where you want. There is no set linear path. The world is yours to explore freely however you wish and Oblivion is no different in that regard.
Unlike other RPGs which reward experience for defeating enemies, the leveling mechanics for Oblivion are based solely on the skills you use and how often you use them.
Use a Sword often and your Blade skill will increase. Using a Bow will effect your Marksman skill. Lots of combat spells like Fire or Ice will increase your Destruction Magic ability. Every 10 of your major skills increased will result in a level gain.
GOTY Deluxe includes Shivering Isles expansion and 9 DLC packs Knights of the Nine, Mehrunes' Razor, Horse Armor, Thieves Den, Fighters Stronghold, Vile Lair, The Orrerry, Spell Tomes, and Wizard's Tower.
A excellent game I highly recommend that will provide hundreds of hours of gameplay from official and and fan made mod content.

First off I’ve only solo played so far by myself on my own private server, which I prefer since mostly just want to relax and play. But I think It’s actually a great way to start off, since you don’t have to be afraid to make mistakes, cuz you can always fix it with admin or server control.  It’s a Great way to learn how the game works.
Now the graphics aren't bad, the character models look great, the game does have full nudity for both genders if you so choose to use it, which makes it feel more authentic and real I think. Although some more hairs, face part options and tattoos would be nice in the future.
The combat itself doesn’t have enough flair to make it really fun yet, having a few ability’s on your tool bar to use, like a quick 3 jab hit or heavy swing would be a welcoming addition.  Although i think no direct healing in the game is the worse since it seems extremely vital.  Health only slowly regenerates on its own, not enough to save your life. Considering I’m always fighting mobs of like 5 or 6 on my own.  Even if I survive it, the next wildlife that crosses my path will likely kill me, if not another mob of 3 to 6 guys.
The building can be somewhat enjoyable though, I really like being able to build from anywhere, it has like a fallout 4 building design but it’s a little easier and doesn’t have a boundary perimeter. As long as you have the resources you can build anywhere.  Which can be kind of funny and a bit op because if you’re really fast and clever you could just build something to walk up then dissemble the stairs, leaving any melee npc at your mercy with ranged attacks, Might differ with multi online play though.
The leveling up seems weak,  at max lvl 50 i should be able to like 3 shot or hit any weaker human who is barely clothed or geared regardless of my gear. Even with steel gear which is near end game gear. It still takes 3 or 4 hits to kill them.  It just doesn’t really make a huge impact to your power like it should especially consider you dont have potions or healing spells. only seems to make a big diiference if every single point is invested in melee or range but that just seems stupid. They either need to raise the lvl cap by a lot or change the damage values. Endurance and stamina are like the only ones that seem to make a significate difference.
Above all a purpose would be nice like a goal or some questlines, besides destroying other ppls and their buildings.  I mean why even make a game pvp and also pve when the pvp seems like the only way the game can be played?
Even though most of this sounds unappealing The game does have a lot of potential, it’s still only early Access so keep that in mind they do have a ton of work to do, some of the things I have mentioned they do plan to fix.  So right now this game is more like an investment. Buying this game right now will ensure its success in the future. Games do take a lot of money to make, Got to pay a lot of people. So the more people that buy this right now will help speed up the games progress.

Like many gamers with at least 10+years experience under their belt, there are just some games that you love because it has everything you want in it, whether it's the story, the gameplay or any other combination of things. One of those games for me was Dungeon Keeper 2. When I found out that Bullfrog Productions had been closed (and with it the development of Dungeon Keeper 3 stopped) I was a bit heartbroken because not only I wouldn't get to play another half-way decent dungeon sim, I also wouldn't get to see Horny the Horned Reaper in action again.
Fast forward about 15 years and I discovered this game. When I found out that this game is not only similar to Dungeon Keeper 2, but also it's successor-of-sorts, I had to take a moment and remind myself that this was not a dream.
It meets my expectations and then some. They even got the same voice actor from DK2 to reprise his role as guide to the player. If that's not commitment from the devs, I don't know what is. If you loved the Dungeon Keeper series then get your hands on this game.
P.S. This is my nomination for The “I Thought This Game Was Cool Before It Won An Award” Award because as soon as I had this game, I had to tell a few people I knew that had played DK2 and let them know that War For The Overworld was the game we were waiting for(I won't get to see everyone's favorite Horned Reaper again but I'll live).

There are a few games that I was sad to never have played in my childhood; there are some Pokemon games, some Zelda games, a few Final Fantasy games, but among that list is Jet Set Radio.  Seeing it for a really low price on the HumbleBundle website, I shrugged and bought it on a whim.  I am proud to say that this game has won me over.
The plot is pretty straightforward.  You're part of an inline skating gang that is trying to win the city of Tokyo-to via tagging.  You have to deal with rival gangs and police.  Sounds pretty simplistic and boring, but I think it's far from that.
The soundtrack is awesome and won me over the minute the first song came on.  The environments, for a game that was first released in 2000, look really nice.  The gameplay itself is really fun, jumping around the environments and evading your enemies whilst trying to completely cover the area in colour, and I also took a liking to the characters almost immediately.
The story is a bit lacking, but to be fair it's really not something that you focus on compared to the ever-so-enjoyable gameplay.  So what are you waiting for?  Get the damn game!!

Definitely scratches that itch that the long absence of a new Dungeon Keeper title has left fans of the series with. Which it should, as its's pretty much a straight clone of Dungeon Keeper 2 with names and designs changed around.
But this isn't at all a bad thing, it plays just as well as the original and there are some welcome original additions (like the ability to replace mined blocks) and new creatures (such as vampires, which need to regularly feed on blood) and new rooms and traps.
On the negative side, the game is rather short (16 hours for me) and currently has a sudden and unsatisfying ending. I feel there's also too many timed missions. This impacts the simulator side of the game, as you don't get to spend much time setting up and running your dungeon. It's also surprisingly prone to long load times and gets rather laggy despite the top end hardware of my system.
In short, if you're a fan of the Dungeon Keeper series, do yourself a favor and pick up Ward for the Overworld. It's not perfect, but it's the next best thing to a Dungeon Keeper sequel made by the original team.

All heroes in you team have stats - health, physical/magical attack, attack speed, physical/magical defend, luck, charisma and etc. Also all of them have special skills - heal, fireball, icewall, stun, etc.
The game starts and waves of foes become to attack you team. The power of you attack depends on your stats - better them - more damage you do,better defense - less damage make your foes. And it's all.
All game is built on a simple mechanics, but it works perfect. It's really interesting to find strategy vs your foes.
This game is realy HARD. Sometimes it seemed that there is no way to win in a mission, and you have to start many-many times to win the scenario.
If you - are the old school games and you like tactics and rpg - you like it.
Strongly recommended.

text:
Coming from massive experience with Fallout 3 and NV to this is a shock. DAMN, some of it is beautiful, the difference between a game that's trying to ward off an apocalypse and one that's trying to deal with its consequences.
As with all Elder Scrolls games, it's a crime to play this in a linear fashion. Get into the main plot line and then park that story and joy-ride on some others. You'll have the most fun on the most obscure sidepaths.
Compared with Skyrim, it is of course technically inferior, though some of the "improvements" in Skyrim should have been reconsidered ("more natural conversations," for instance, doesn't work out at all well when you have a couple of people. or a companion, obsessed with standing right in front of you and blocking your view of who you are talking with -- I'm looking at you, Serana). But fanboy comparisons in favor of one or the other are usually idiotic. Cyrodiil and Skyrim are different places and different societies. Some imbeciles complain that Oblivion is "too beautiful" or Skyrim "not beautiful enough," or that the populations of either or both don't behave like the Dark Elves of Morrowind. Well, what the hell did you expect?
There's a difference in structure between Oblivion and Skyrim that's seldom noticed but quite critical. Oblivion is an epic; Skyrim is not. An epic needs a hero and a villain who stand out and engage you, and a vital question to settle one way or the other -- such as the fate of the world. In Oblivion you have the hero in Martin Septim, an ordinary person who has to grow into an extraordinary role pretty damned quickly, and Mehrunes Dagon, one of the most interesting of the Daedric Princes, even though he's wicked from top to toe. (Quite a bit more nuanced than the unfortunate choice of Molag Bal to play the villain role in Elder Scrolls Online -- Molag Bal is just a thug.) You, as the player, have an easily understandable role -- in terms of the main quest, you are the one who makes things happen for Martin, his go-to guy (or girl) for the things he can't do himself. And the final valedictory by Martin celebrates what you have accomplished together, while reminding you that there will be more challenges in the future: "The amulet is shattered. Dagon is defeated. With the dragon's blood and the Amulet of Kings, we have sealed the gates of Oblivion -- forever.....The Third Age is ended, and a new age dawns. When the next Elder Scroll is written, you shall be its scribe. The shape of the future, the fate of the Empire -- these things now belong to you." It evokes the words of Martin's father, the old Emperor, at the very beginning, as if the game were about to start again. As, indeed, it would in real life. But that doesn't mean you can't be proud of what you just accomplished.
But in Skyrim, things are a lot more ambiguous. You aren't the sidekick of the true Emperor. You're the schmuck who's been slapped with the Dragonborn blessing/curse, with neither warning nor instructions, as if you'd been standing on the side of the road and been hit by a seagull turd. The people you meet with and work with run from the ordinary to the spectacularly unimpressive -- not a heroic figure among them. They whine and mutter, caught in the web of a decaying age. At one point, Jarl Balgruf's steward is trying to sell him on some big project. The Jarl is not impressed, and he finally ends up shouting, "Where am I to get the money? I can't even afford to repair the city walls!" And he can't. They're sloppily patched with sharpened logs. Ulfric is an "I'm in love with me" jerk, the Stormcloaks are bigots, and the Imperial commander, General Tullius, would all too obviously like to be ANYWHERE but Skyrim. Both the Greybeards and the Blades are.... well not to put too fine a point on it.... STUPID STUBBORN LOSERS. (Was that subtle enough?) And Alduin.... this nonentity is going to destroy the world? How? A hissy fit? A storm of poutrage? While Dagon was a Dark Prince, Alduin is a pissy little pug dog who's begging to be drop-kicked out the nearest window. It doesn't help that the final battle usually lasts about two minutes. Personally, I think Alduin must have been weakened in Sovngarde by repeatedly throwing up at the ghastly Wardor Street English everyone is forced to utter, like Grade 6 students trying to sound "authentic" for a medieval pageant. But so what, at least you've won, right? Not so fast. Paarthurnax, the only one of your "seniors" that it isn't a positive agony to deal with, hints darkly that perhaps Alduin will be recycled after all....The "victory scene" up on the Throat of the World is the gloomiest, grimmest Triumph ever seen. You almost think they're going to be passing out cyanide capsules at the end. And then what?...Oh, nothing. The dragons don't even stop attacking, despite the hint they might have taken from Alduin's end. In other words, apart from terminating MAYBE the terminally unbelievable "threat" from Alduin, you end the game having accomplished zip-all. Not that I mind. The tangles are credible and fascinating, and the drastic lack of noble words and behavior is all too realistic. But an epic it is not. More like a watered down dystopian vision, you load 16 tons and what do you get? Nothing, and you still owe your soul to the company store.
One detail that is better in Oblivion than in Skyrim is the appearance of the people. Yes, the Skyrim models are technically more advanced, and the textures are far clearer, but hot daamme are they ugly! Skyrim is the only game I know of that has UGLY elves, but I guess it doesn't matter since everyone in Skyrim looks as if they had had a truck parked on their faces. Maybe it's frostbite. And there's not a single bookstore in vanilla Skyrim, and only one real clothing store, where the staff go out of their way to insult you and the selection is vile. Oblivion has clothing stores, bookstores, and jewellery stores even before the modders go to work on it. Especially with a female character, you'll forgive Oblivion's blurry renditions easily once you see the Skyrim house of horrors.
There's a little bit of quirkiness in Oblivion, too, as there was in Morrowind, which hardly appears in Skyrim, where almost everyone looks as if they were on intravenous Valium. My favorite is the Dark Elf lady who asks you, "Do you happen to know what the penalty for necrophilia is in Cyrodiil? Assume that it's not a first offense...." and is delighted to find out it's only a 500 gold fine, "far cheaper than in Morrowind." You can spend days thinking about the implications of that.....
Plus, Oblivion has by far the best add-on content in the ES series, "The Shivering Isles." Not describable -- just go play it. It actually has an emotionally engaging main story line for once, about a very nasty trick that some of the Daedric Lords played on one of their own whom they thought was getting too big for his boots. And notice that at some angles, Sheogorath, the Lord of Insanity, looks very much like a certain former American president.....

If you're planning to buy this game now, you need a LOT of patience and commitment. It's very difficult to get into and master as of now due to the toxic community that has developed recently.
I've played this game for bit and I enjoyed it thoroughly for a good few years! My most enjoyable years were roughly 2013 until I decided to stop playing.
I see a lot of you complain about the exploits such as the reverse overheads and yes, it was annoying but we ALL had to go through with the high levels and deal with their crap, being tossed around like a newb. But, the community WAS good at one point and willing to teach you these exploits as well as how to counter them. Everyone was so willing to help you develop and hone your skills in the past. That was what made the game LEGENDARY. You could master everything in roughly 200 hours of gameplay with a teacher. Nowadays, you just gotta learn everything yourself. I'll get more into that in a bit.
I didn't mind the unrealistic exploits as everything is counterable. It really only provided more depth into the game because let's admit it, the combat would be too easy if these exploits were completely fixed. Speaking of fixed, Deadliest Warrior balanced those exploits out by making them do less damage. So it is an improved version catered to those who just want to get into the action without getting demolished.
But back to what I was talking about...the community now. I've decided to hop on around multiple servers and of course, I'm getting kicked from servers for being a higher level. That's always been an issue but not a giant one. But here's the kicker. The amount of trash talking has sky rocketed. I was called trash for being killed as the last person in Last Team Standing. Keep in mind, this was from a renouned clan in Chivalry as well and not some random person.
I left the server and hopped onto another clan duel server to witness a newer player trying to learn from a clan but they were just messing around with him and hazing rather than teaching any kind of fundamentals. This is why you would have to teach yourself as very few people are willing to help you learn and practice, thus taking the game longer to master. You could only really join a clan which would definitely improve your skill as they host practices but only if you are at a certain skill they desire. That is difficult to accomplish nowadays.
I'm sure there are still some helpful clans out there but your numbers have been reduced significantly. Less and less newer players are staying to play as no one really wants to put the effort to show them the ropes. Nearly half the servers on Chivalry are empty on a daily basis unfortunately until a sale hits but that is short lived and only the dedicated high leveled players stay.
All in all, the great days of Chivalry are long gone. All is left is a toxic community with very few helpful people left. It's quite depressing.
I wouldn't pay more than 5 dollars for this game. Just wait for a sale.

Hey everyone and this is my review about the game!
This is an automated turn based game.
There is an achievement list on there.
There is a shop to buy new stuff.
No options.
You will get 3 randomized heroes which you are able to re-roll for a small fee. Each hero has a different effect, special attack and stats. Some are tanky, some are powerful and all of them has an advantage and a disadvantage. Heroes are only able to attack their enemy if they are standing infront of them. Killing an enemy will grant them 1 xp ball. Having 3 of them will make them level up. The special bar will be slightly filled by each hit on an enemy and you are able to activate it once it is full. Sadly the game is really unbalanced as it is totally luck dependant and on top of that totally automated. The only thing what you have to do is rotate heroes position, use the special bar and equip them with better items. The battles are "Speed" turn based, so the higher the speed faster you are able to attack again. There are random events that can TOTALLY ruin your run. Like for in example, You are able to choose between "party member is instant death, or all items has been stolen". The negative events are showing up more often than positive ones. Monsters are getting powerful quickly.
Unbalanced.
Not enjoyable.
No progression feelings at all.
Ingame tutorial.
Grindfest and luck based.
Randomized hero re-roll.
Poor stats upgrade per level. (like +1)
Able to speed up.
Too many bad events or bad scenarios to ruin your run.
MEH, don't buy.

Yet another EPIC game from bioware, and the second installment of the Mass Effect Series, just as epic, if not moreso, as the first.
Choices still matter,and you see some of your choices from the first game making big and little waves in your story; actions matter, who lives, who dies, who do you save....
I only have 33.4 hours on steam with this game, but over 100 on Origin (more DLC available on origin).
This game along with the first are beyond amazing, this second installment is much darker than the first game.  The Reapers are back, only this time they're using the mysterious Collectors instead of the Geth, whole human colonies are vanishing without a trace, no signs left behind, no struggle, nothing.  Its up to you, to find out why/how and put a stop to it.
You have new companions, with returning faces, and a whole other side of the universe to explore and tame.
I recommend this game whole heartedly, the graphics hold up to the test of time, the decisions still matter, and it still hits you right in the feels, and keeps on delivering with an epic stoy.

First off I’ve only solo played so far by myself on my own private server, which I prefer since mostly just want to relax and play. But I think It’s actually a great way to start off, since you don’t have to be afraid to make mistakes, cuz you can always fix it with admin or server control.  It’s a Great way to learn how the game works.
Now the graphics aren't bad, the character models look great, the game does have full nudity for both genders if you so choose to use it, which makes it feel more authentic and real I think. Although some more hairs, face part options and tattoos would be nice in the future.
The combat itself doesn’t have enough flair to make it really fun yet, having a few ability’s on your tool bar to use, like a quick 3 jab hit or heavy swing would be a welcoming addition.  Although i think no direct healing in the game is the worse since it seems extremely vital.  Health only slowly regenerates on its own, not enough to save your life. Considering I’m always fighting mobs of like 5 or 6 on my own.  Even if I survive it, the next wildlife that crosses my path will likely kill me, if not another mob of 3 to 6 guys.
The building can be somewhat enjoyable though, I really like being able to build from anywhere, it has like a fallout 4 building design but it’s a little easier and doesn’t have a boundary perimeter. As long as you have the resources you can build anywhere.  Which can be kind of funny and a bit op because if you’re really fast and clever you could just build something to walk up then dissemble the stairs, leaving any melee npc at your mercy with ranged attacks, Might differ with multi online play though.
The leveling up seems weak,  at max lvl 50 i should be able to like 3 shot or hit any weaker human who is barely clothed or geared regardless of my gear. Even with steel gear which is near end game gear. It still takes 3 or 4 hits to kill them.  It just doesn’t really make a huge impact to your power like it should especially consider you dont have potions or healing spells. only seems to make a big diiference if every single point is invested in melee or range but that just seems stupid. They either need to raise the lvl cap by a lot or change the damage values. Endurance and stamina are like the only ones that seem to make a significate difference.
Above all a purpose would be nice like a goal or some questlines, besides destroying other ppls and their buildings.  I mean why even make a game pvp and also pve when the pvp seems like the only way the game can be played?
Even though most of this sounds unappealing The game does have a lot of potential, it’s still only early Access so keep that in mind they do have a ton of work to do, some of the things I have mentioned they do plan to fix.  So right now this game is more like an investment. Buying this game right now will ensure its success in the future. Games do take a lot of money to make, Got to pay a lot of people. So the more people that buy this right now will help speed up the games progress.

Brief summary of beta version of RPG Tycoon- Game is very buggy as warned, looks very promising but needs to take some pages from successful GameDev Tycoon.
Elongated breakdown-
Opened up my Store on steam to see this little Number pop up! Well hello little number maybe a 1 or even a lil .5. Nonetheless this game was there and as I really have enjoyed playing GameDevTycoon. I think this game can really learn a few things from Gamedev...
Graphics- The graphics are good and very reminiscent of old school Runescape. Which plays in very well into the game.
Sliders- The sliders don't make much sense and is very vague.. Also are very cumbersome and need some better sound effects the default Window sound is very unappealing.
Knowledge in Game- When you begin the game you are very overwhelmed and yet underwhelmed. You get some basic knowledge and are confused at the same time. You have no idea about what is working within the quests (like within the sliders and what works with what also point allocation).
Point allocation- The game has a bug where you can adjust the top portion of the allocation system by minusing them and have it return next quest with the points still remaining where you added them last time.
Money- I had no idea you lost the game when you ran out of money and so I ended the game within 2 mins by trying to build my city in more and adding roads.. To only have the game be all like you suck GG.
Visitors-Their bubbles of text get stuck behind buildings and cannot be read.
Quests and making money- NOOO Clue how to make good money, felt like I’m just waiting for my quests tooooo sllllooowwwwllllyyyy produce the little change each time.. Perhaps needs to be upped a bit? or I'm just a bit inpatient, who knows probably the second. The quests also need to be clearer and more feedback is needed and perhaps a memory system again similar to GameDev...
UI- is very clear and clean but needs some better animations and sound effects. Hopefully they will add in better tutorials and make the game easier to jump in.
Questing- Please make the UI more fun and clear when your hero is on a quest. You get no idea why points are getting added into the certain places.
As I said before game looks great, shows a lot of promise and I can't wait for it to be finished to really log in some hours. I hope they change the music to something a lil catchier, add in some better sound effects, update the UI a bit more, and clean up the game all around to be honest. Will play more, look forward to the full release.
Thanks for reading my rant. (PS: I’ve only spent a few times on this game so read my review with that in mind)

A very, -very- unenthusiastic recommendation. In theory, WFTO has all the right pieces to be a Dungeon Keeper successor, but it's lacking.... something. It's difficult to put my finger on it, but after going through the campaign I was less than impressed. It's missing that bit of charm that DK had for itself. Maybe it's because the campaign feels like it's just a long tutorial for each of the rooms and traps and ends suddenly without letting you enjoy your fully-unlocked tech tree.
That's not to say the game isn't good, though. It does very interesting things with rooms that DK 1 and 2 didn't, such as giving the "props" in rooms an efficiency bonus for being near fortified walls. It's a mixed bag, though; rooms larger than 5x5 will have props stuck in the middle unable to get a bonus, so it's almost worthless building anything but 5x? rooms, but sometimes you have to simply to get the damn narrator to shut up about how the crypt isn't big enough for all the corpses.
The game also seems intent on getting you to advance. Dungeon Keeper almost never rushed you. You could stay safe inside your walls until the lack of gold forced you out. WFTO, however? I think even the tutorial rushes you. Not even just for the achievement involved with finishing it quickly; it's do or die ASAP. And that rushed feeling follows you through the whole game. One of the final missions barely gives you enough time to get your workers digging out a single room before the enemy breaks into your space, and it's a constant, annoying, boring fight from that point on, from multiple directions, with no rest involved and nothing but luck to see you through. My last two attempts at that level followed the same tactics, the same speed, the same room layout planning at the very start. Three hours after the first one started, a single mistake put me in an unrecoverable death spiral that really shouldn't have been unrecoverable, and the attempt after that was a cheap and easy win for me in less than 15 minutes. Pure luck involved, nothing to do with choices or careful planning.
TL;DR: it'll satisfy your appetite for a modern Dungeon Keeper game, but like chinese take-out you'll be hungry again after an hour.

There are a few games that I was sad to never have played in my childhood; there are some Pokemon games, some Zelda games, a few Final Fantasy games, but among that list is Jet Set Radio.  Seeing it for a really low price on the HumbleBundle website, I shrugged and bought it on a whim.  I am proud to say that this game has won me over.
The plot is pretty straightforward.  You're part of an inline skating gang that is trying to win the city of Tokyo-to via tagging.  You have to deal with rival gangs and police.  Sounds pretty simplistic and boring, but I think it's far from that.
The soundtrack is awesome and won me over the minute the first song came on.  The environments, for a game that was first released in 2000, look really nice.  The gameplay itself is really fun, jumping around the environments and evading your enemies whilst trying to completely cover the area in colour, and I also took a liking to the characters almost immediately.
The story is a bit lacking, but to be fair it's really not something that you focus on compared to the ever-so-enjoyable gameplay.  So what are you waiting for?  Get the damn game!!

Before I say anything else, you should know that the game is in early access and needless to say, is VERY buggy and sometimes quite monotonous or boring. With that said, the game has the potential to become a great game in time. I can certainly see this game becoming the next great PC game like DayZ or Game Dev Tycoon. Should you buy this game? Sure! Unlike most early access games, RPG Tycoon is a relatively cheap game, which is (Or if not, it will become) well worth the money.

If you can accept that, then this game is definitely worth it! It is very much like ARK, but with sooooo much more content (yes, even if it is still EA). So, there ARE definitely some kinks that need working out, but people who understand that this game is NOT a completed game, are going to enjoy the gaming experience, and those who don't have patience for crashes, bugs, and server wipes should look back at the game in a couple months and see where its at!!!

TL;DR: Didn't enjoy it to start, but the game has progressed to a point where i can say it satisfies my craving for a new Dungeon Keeper. Recommend it to people who enjoy dungeon management and what i consider to be a different form of RTS.
Full review:
War for the Overworld... one of those games i play on and off when i feel like playing Dungeon Keeper... it didn't interest me early on... part of it was because the game in the state it was in when i got it wasn't enjoyable to me... i despised how they changed the mechanics from original DK and DK2, such as not being able to pick up your creatures when they aren't on your tiles. i also disliked how snarky and annoying the mentor was... however, the mentor issue seems to have been mostly resolved, and I've grown used to not being able to pick up my creatures when they aren't on my tiles... another part of my issue with the game was that i kind of had a grudge on the people i can only assume are developing the game now... I joined their original website (which i believe was called Keeper Klan) when i was about the age between 9 and 12 (in other words, i was a whiny, annoying, selfish little brat). And due to how i acted back then, the devs kinda hated me and were rather mean to me because of it... I've since matured and have grown to look past this fact, and blame myself for how they were treating me. It made sense that they treated me the way they did, considering how i acted and treated them.
But i'm trailing... back on the subject of the game
I may not have enjoyed the game early on, but i really enjoy the game in it's current state, now that it has seen improvement and I've been able to grow into and learn the mechanics more. It's nice to finally have a game i can consider to be a good spiritual successor to the duo. My only complaint now is the lack of customization options in the editor. Even with those complaints, I've still used it and learned most of how it works. I also decided to try the campaigns and thoroughly enjoyed them both. I also enjoyed the little home realms that allow you to make the dungeon of your dreams... to an extent, of course...
All in all, i love the game in it's current state. it fills that void in my heart for a new version of one of my favorite games when i was young. i like the direction they're going, and i hope they continue on the same path they're on now... a path that a lot of game developers, especially big ones, tend to veer from... I can definitely say i recommend this game at the current time... Devs, if you're reading this, i apologize for my actions when i was younger, and i hope you continue to support this game for a long while and make it even better~ c:
Sincerely - Tirsiak (known by old members of Keeper Klan as Zomboy99)

Ah, Jet Set Radio.  One of my favorite games from my childhood - back then, it was a game like no other - and that still stands today.  The visuals have aged very well and the graphics look great in HD.  The soundtrack is also as amazing as ever (Naganuma is some kind of a genius), even though a few songs were cut.  The gameplay is fun and challenging - I don't remember it being this hard!  The main thing that could have been changed during the port is the controls.   It plays exactly like it did on the Dreamcast.  Keyboard movement is restricted to 8 directions (like the Dreamcast D-Pad) and an external analog stick isn't much better.  Getting used to movement with a Dualshock 3 was rough, especially with how difficult the game is naturally.  Steam Achievements is a nice bonus as well  Still totally recommend if you were a fan of the original Dreamcast release!  Hoping a JSRF port is in the future!

If you grew up with this game, this is a good conversion (though a controller is a must) and the HD graphics mode offers a nice, if subtle upgrade to the original graphics. However, like most of Sega's early 3D games (Virtua Fighter excluded), it was somewhat lacking in polish to begin with and as such hasn't stood the test of time well. I have a lot more respect for the team that did Journey of Dreams after revisiting this than I did before because, while that game failed spectacularly, the original NiGHTS didn't exactly give them a lot to work with. A lot of the reason why Journey of Dreams was bad is that NiGHTS itself, by modern standards, isn't very good.
I'm giving this a recommend, but that only applies if you're already familiar with the game and would like to play it again without dealing with old hardware. On that level, this succeeds abundantly, and I hope Sega will continue to do re-releases of their older games. But if you're not already a fan of NiGHTS, this is a skip. It's a product of a bygone era of gaming, and a company that was struggling to find its identity in a changing industry, and it shows. NiGHTS was clever and beautiful for its time, but now it mostly seems counterintuitive and dated.

Brief overview:
This game (if you couldn't tell from the video) is about building machines out of blocks and mechanical parts, then fighting/racing/showing them off to other people.
There is an astounding amount of creativity in this game. Before anyone asks....No... This is not a rip off of robocraft. robocraft has way too little creativity and too much competitive play to be anywhere near similar to this game, with the exception of using blocks. The biggest thing I like about this game when compared to robocraft is the ability to bind keys.....BIND KEYS!!! You can set little mechanical parts to a key and then assign the same mechanical part on another part of your creation another key. This opens up a world of opportunity, and while the game is difficult to get started with, it is easily worth it. It does take time to get used to building, but when you build that one awesome creation, the amount of satisfaction it brings is unlike any other game. Then, you can battle or show it off to people. It is incredible how addicting this game is.
Pros:
Not too highly competative for people who just want to create things and test them out for fun.
Good community thus far

assigning keys, setting angles for hinges and rotating parts along with setting lengths for pistons

just.....way too much fun and brings out the creativity in anyone willing to pick up the learning curve.

Not very populous servers.
In short, I recomend this game to anyone. It sparks the creativity in everyone's mind and all it takes is a small learning curve. I promise, if you have a creative or imaginitive mind, this game is worth your time and effort.

Should be noted, as others have pointed out so far, that this is not a game, but more of an interactive novel.
I'm only a few chapters in, but the writing so far has been top notch. Very descriptive, and captures the imagination on an emboldened tale. The choices given are also pretty interesting. It's not so much as an A or B choice, but a great deal more. Minor spoilers here, about two chapters in, so skip the reminder of this paragraph if you don't want to spoil it. You encounter a cowboy, and a gold panner engaged in a shootout. You first choose how you want to arrive at the scene, and then engage with both characters. You can go in guns blazing, shooting before asking questions, or you can lend an ear to the two men and find out whats really going on. I got a chuckle out of this scene when I had the option to approach the men and, "Tip your hat and say, afternoon gents". You then find out whats going on, and effectively play detective. Listen to both sides of the story, figure out who is in the wrong or right, and then have one of the two pay reperations for what went wrong. Afterwards you can ask one, or both of the men to accompany you on your travels. Both characters are well written, and in the short time I've been with them, I actually feel like I'm friends with them(rather lame I know, but bare with me.)
The game also has a stat system, which is really interesting. Different options you select can have different effects on you. For example, in one section of the story I opted to travel with a ranchhand. He was on the frontier for a while, and offered up a good bit of knowledge on the wilds, and surviving harsh enviroments. As a result, my stats increased for those respective areas. In one section, im given a few days to launder about, and I can practice various things. I can take to target practice, read up on a variety of subjects, go gamble, etc. The stats effect different options, much like mass effect. You can upgrade persuasion, honor, and other traits. It's an interesting concept, and it makes your choice actually feel weighted.
This game, or novel, is hard to put down, and if you love westerns, and reading in general, you'll greatly enjoy it. Give it ago, it only costs a big mac, beef jerky, case of cheap beer, etc.

Having been a fan of NiGHTS since its original release back on the Sega Saturn, I can tell you a LOT of love went into this port. In addition to the original game itself, included also is the rare and coveted demo disc Christmas NiGHTS, opening up unlockables and a varient of Spring Valley primarily centered around Christmas (though the theme sometimes changes depending on the holiday/date, such as April Fools, Halloween, summer, Valentines, etc). This alone makes this port worth it to the die-hard fan, but on top of this, you've given the option to switch between the original Sega Saturn graphics, or the graphics of the formally Japan-only PS2 remake.
For those of you unfamiliar with this title, you can choose between to play as either Claris or Elliot, two children whom by day struggle to overcome their fears, and by night aid NiGHTS in overthrowing the king of all Nightmare, Wizeman. As you fly through linear circular stages, you'll collect orbs and other goodies, destroying captures that hold Ideya - raw dream energy - that had been stolen from the two children. Its story is left intentionally vague to encourage the player's own imagination to interpret the events. There are also many goodies and easter eggs to be found hidden around, including the curious Nightopian AI (these being creatures that breed, grow, die and can even hybridize with enemies within the level). At the time of its original release this game offered groundbreaking techniques in graphics and gameplay style, giving it its own place in history and recognized by many as an unofficial secondary mascot to Sonic Team.
And now for the downside. Unfortunately, the game is incredibly short and can be 100%'d in only a few hours, though the extras help to provide some replay value. Also, while the controls, for the most part, are pretty tight there are areas where NiGHTS becomes difficult to control - particularly areas like the bobsled, mermaid and rail portions from their respective levels.
Still, despite those problems, for the price and what it comes with, I would consider it well worth it and highly recommend it to anyone interested in a timeless masterpiece and a piece of gaming history. If you're still unsure, I would say to consider waiting for a sale. Either way, NiGHTS into Dreams is well worth having in your collection.

I didn't mind the unrealistic exploits as everything is counterable. Nearly half the servers on Chivalry are empty on a daily basis unfortunately until a sale hits but that is short lived and only the dedicated high leveled players stay.

There is quite a lot wrong with this game, that simply makes it boring to play.
My largest issue with this game is how it plays. Combat plays automatically while you do the strats (position your party, equip items, use items and skills), and thats the extent of your control aside for a few more minor things. At first that doesn't sound so bad, you might need to do certain things a certain way due to abilities your enemies might have. But this game has dumbed down everything that could potentially be challenging outside of direct combat:
- Each character has a single skill. one. ONE!!!!!!! (I found that each actually has a team buff/debuff, but all of them weren't thought out very well, 2 classes even had the exact same one as well, which is a little bit silly).
- Your characters are selected for you. WHY? Whats worse you need to pay in-game currency for the ability to select your characters? I don't understand what purpose it serves. You could say that it is to ease the player into the game, but that is BS since the game throws a full party of 3 people and those people are randomly selected out of the ones you can use, that doesn't sound like easing in.
- Items stats are boring as f**k. Its a very simple add to damage, and any class can equip any weapon and shield and have it deal more damage than a weapon they would typically hold (I had a mage holding a sword that added 5 to damage. better than his staff).
- A inventory system that I wish never exsisted. When your party picks up an item (which isn't notified very well to the player) it is added to the rather small inventory space, items are queued from the top and once you fill your inventory and find another item, the oldest item in your inventory is removed. What if I wanted to keep a potion? How can I stratergise if you don't give me the means to do so? You can't even remove an item from your inventory to bump a potion back to the top in order to keep. Why can't I do that? Seriously? It just seems a little bit stupid that I have to get rid of a useful potion for a god-awful weapon.
Due to the lack of control the player has and the lack of information about how some of the game's simple game mechanics work during the tutorial, all combined with the simplicity of class and equipment stats and abilities... *sigh*

It's an alpha. Things are prone to break.  Beyond this, very developed for an alpha. Funcom wins the award for the most patches put out in a day, week, month, ever. Their devotion to making this game happen is very impressive.
Those that play Rust or Ark will take very quickly to this game. Easy to pick up. Rebinding some of the keys will help make the game a bit more intuitive in use.  Those insistent on playing this game with a game controller will find themselves getting thumped by those using mouse/keyboard.
While I think the survival sandbox genre is getting a bit crowded these days, I definitely see Conan carving out its own niche.  Conan Exiles makes several improvements on existing game systems we are familiar with.  Nothing I see would be considered ground breaking, more of an evolution of game systems that one would expect from late comers to this genre (not a bad thing.)
The attribute system is pretty straight forward and has a direct impact on game play.  There are parts of this system that have yet to be fully fleshed out.
The tiered crafting system is definitely superior to that of Rust's blueprint hunt.  Conan allows for loner style of play, but the path in crafting will certainly be different than players operating as a group.  I recommend playing with a friend or two; will allow you to specialize and level faster.
The critters in the game aren’t static and path better than those found in Rust.  You can actually sneak by them depending on the direction they are facing.  NPC’s are a mix of static and moving.  Combine the two and you are definitely looking at a larger and more diverse group of baddies than what is found in Rust.
Thralls.  Yes, I want my own army of minions.  The use of thralls can add blueprints, not normally learnable, reduce crafting time or materials needed.
Those that like to fortify up and watch the world pass on by will find it difficult as food and water is a constant issue.

This was my experience:
Play a few games but I don't really understand the game. Finally after an hour and a half of going throught the tutorials a second time I figure it out. Start up an empire in Iceland. I don't bother anyone. I marry a Danish girl and help out my father-in-law with a rebelion and a small war but I don't really cause any trubble. The king of Norge (Norway) keeps wanting to start wars though. One day I get a letter, he wants peace as long as I fly his flage. Seeing as my wife was sick and had died a month before and her father was now losing a war I did not have the gold to help him win I had no other choice but to submit and accepted Norge rule. Immediatly the King of Norge invites me to his grand feast. He treats me well and offers me protection and safety. Alpha as ♥♥♥♥ King of Norge fights the Scots who have been bothering me for years. I ask if my son can marry his beautiful daughter who will one day be the Queen of Norge, and without question or hesitation he sends his daughter to Iceland and congradulates me on entering the family. WIth this my son is happy and I can concentrait on my kingdom. Over the next few years I build up a great army and nearly 1000 gold in wealth. However, I am an old man. I fear the fate of my father, I fear that soon I will die. The King of Norge is not a young man either anymore. One day I get another letter. The King of Norge is plaining to invade Scotland. Seeing as my other son married Godwinson (The King of England)'s daughter I was prepared to invade Scotland and claim all of  England and thus most of northern Europe for the King of Norge. I constructed a fleet of ships, hired thousands of men from the country side and some extra mecenaries just in case, and set sail. This time I was prepared for battle, I knew what would come. It was minutes laters as I prepaired my assault that I watched a Scotish fleet came from the deep ocean and landed on my shores and slaughter my people. Half of Scotland fought me in Scotland while the other half banded together and invaded my homeland of Iceland.
And that folks is the story of how Crusader Kings II gives you a cookie, lets you eat it and enjoy it before slaping you across the face and wash your mouth out with soap and hot sause. And I'll be god damned if it wasn't the most fun I've ever had. I laughed and I cried. I was filled with joy and then crushed with defeat. I was a king...I was THE KING...and then I was nothing...

I would definatley recomend this MMO to anyone who is tired of the turn based, cooldown timer traditional mmo. This game is entirley realtime combat, freeroamed enviroment, beautifully rendered, and of course crafting and scavenging are realistic and common, making it easy to level up. Yet I'm not going to glamorize the game and leave out all the cons. Some cons of the game are as follows: If you are new to the game and plan on getting a motorcycle/atv/car and don't level up your dexterity+coordination, it will be far to late to do anything about it and takes insanely long to bring it up to 25-35. Also the crafting times are insane, such as: Motorcycle Control System: 4 hours, that's a bit insane don't ya think? Althought the flipside is you can buy those off auctions for a reasonable price. So overall I give it a 9/10! Defiantley would send to anyone.

NiGHTs into dreams is a port of the classic SEGA Saturn gem from 1996. The goal is simple and requires capturing stolen Ideya by collecting at least 20 blue orbs and destroing the capsules. The sooner you destroy the capsule, the more time you have to collect more points before the time runs out. Once you've collected all four Ideya, NiGHTs is warped into a boss battle. There are four stages for the two characters, Claris & Elliot. The fourth stage for each character, Twin Seeds is the same and in order to unlock it you need at least all C's on previous stages. The game is short, but sweet. However, it can be a real challenge to get all A's on the stages, which is required to unlock the Christmas NiGHTs. SEGA has given the game a nice HD improvement, thus boosting more colorful and vivid visuals than the Saturn version. You can play the game in two modes, HD & Saturn. The keyboard controls for this game can take some adjusting and I would reccomend getting a Xbox 360 controller since this game was really meant to be played with a controller. This is indeed a good port of a very good game, probably Sonic Team's only masterpiece. Truely a gem.

Whether or not you should get this game depends on what's more important to you: the trip or the destination. This is one of the two best interactive novels I've ever played (the other being Mecha Ace). the writing is solid, the characters are fun and endearing, and the choices have weight and consequence without feeling shoehorned in just to force you into having to make a weighty decision. Perhaps more importantly, a lot of choices are appropriately grey - it might be honorable to do something, but is it really best (for you or the community)? The only problem has been during a almost every violent encounter I died. There is usually very little hint as to which action is the best one (even if you'd think your character would know better, or could easily perform the feat). Luckily, if you die, you can just restart the encounter. It just costs you "Legend", which I guess is the games rating score. In spite of this, the game is just charming to play.
So why do I NOT recommend it? Because the ending doesn't make sense. This huge conspiracy is built up over the course of the game, only to lead to a sudden and unexpected confrontation (where you can cordially invite everyone and their parents [literally] as allies, even if you pist them off earlier in yoru adventure) with a learing plot hole. Namely, how does one family threaten the livelihood of America with a small band of outlaws? It's completely nonsensical, and when combined with the rushed ending, becomes disappointing.
I would only recommend this game if you are willing to enjoy the journey and don't care (much) about the ending. It's the longest interactive novel I've ever played/read... and the most disappointing.
