TL;DR - If you have extra money to throw at the game, go ahead and play the game. If not, I recommend you don't patron your accounts. Just enjoy the game as it is and don't get sucked into it.
Long Version -
I'm not a veteran player; been playing the game since circa April of 2016. I wasn't a social butterfly in the game; I liked crafting and keeping to myself, and that was about it.
I started the game just for ♥♥♥♥♥ and giggles, thinking i probably wouldnt stick around. But I loved the game. It was very dream-like and new with so much fun stuff to do and explore. I spent all my free time questing and trying to learn about the game.
Around the 2 month mark of me playing, I decided to purchase my first month of patron with my own money. It wasn't that much, I said to myself, and I can pay for future months of patron in the gold I make.
But after that first month of patron, it kind of went downhill. I wasn't aware of it for a long time.
As time went on, I stopped questing. Sure, I found other "fun" things to do. But most of the fun things I was doing was whatever made the most gold at the time. As the markets on NA and EU changed, I had to change my setup a couple times a year.
I finally got my EU alt at a gold-making rate that I could do whatever I wanted with my gold on NA, and because I didn't care much about end-game gears, I bought shiny stuff that I could enjoy the game with; boats, mouts, cars, that kind of stuff. That was fun for me. I loved getting new things. I orimarily became a merchant, running packs, to fund getting new stuff.
3.0 was a weird update; I was on the fence about it. I liked the new additions in areas and races, but I didn't like the new family/vocation daily quests. Even though they were extra gold, they were tedious to do on all my characters per day, so I stopped doing most of them.
The 3.5 update is where it got bad. All the changes to the trade system hurt me for the first few months.  I had to rethink my routes, what packs were more profitable, and plan ahead to make sure I could get in and out of the tiny trade centers efficiently.
I bought a merchant ship to help with large shipments. Sunk a good chunk of gold into it, but made it back within a couple days using that ship. A couple days ago, it was pirated off the Yny trade spot by greens. I'm not sore about that, as it was my fault when I knew, but chose to anyway because it would save me time over running my freighter twice. Live and learn, yeah?
When I told my friend, who doesn't play the game, about the incident, he said, 'Why don't you do something in the game that's fun? Why don't you do dungeon runs?" I told him I wouldn't do that because it wouldn't make much gold.
What he said next kind of struck me and made me realize what was going on. He said, "No, you shouldn't be doing something for how much gold it makes for you. You should be doing it because it's fun."
After that I realized almost everything in the game craft and trade-wise wasn't actually fun for me. I'm probably going to let my patron expire after this month, and stop playing altogether.

NiGHTS Into Dreams... was the flagship game of the Sega Saturn console.
You play as one of two children, Claris and Elliot, lost in dream worlds of their own as they fight against their fears and recover their inner selves. The two children encounter a dream entity called NiGHTS, captured for rebelling against his master -- the master of Nightmares -- Wizeman. By merging with NiGHTS, the children can explore their dreamscape, defeat Wizeman's minions, and finally confront the master himself.
Despite the premise, the game is light-hearted. The player controls the children through colorful and musical 3D worlds, complete with their own artificial life. Once you merge with NiGHTS, you begin a play through four courses that will take you around the level, collecting pickups to unlock each course successively. You control NiGHTS on a 2D plane that weaves around in 3D space, so you only have to worry about going forward, back, up, or down. Courses are also timed; letting the timer run out turns you back into a child, legging it back to the start, and scattering the pickups around you.
In order to progress to the boss of a level, you must finish four courses with a good enough average score to proceed. Score is improved with the pickups you bring with you, as well as how often you went through loops, or picked up items, in succession.
NiGHTS Into Dreams... is not a long game. However, it takes a while to truly master its scoring system. Until you gain the mastery of doing acrobatic loops through the skies, you'll be accompanied by dynamically changing music tracks, uplifting beats, and controls that are easy to pick up.
There is more to the game than I've written above -- the ability to hatch and help the artificial life grow, the addition of the Christmas NiGHTS limited edition content, updated graphics, and more. This HD re-release is a port of the uncommon PlayStation 2 version. While a timing bug has crept in, making the animations a bit too fast compared to some musical cues, this edition is still faithful to the original's gameplay and spirit. The music alone has sold me to this game many times over.

This is....One of those games. It never says a word, nor does it ever have anything in game to explain the story in full outside of what you see and play. It also only ever presents the play 7 stages in total making it a very 'short' single play experance.
Yet because of all of that, it is chances are one of the best games ever made in all time. It's got a MASS of hidden depth and secrets for the player to poke at and find, it offers a fast pace gaming style even Sonic would blush at, all while presenting a world so colorful and vivid that it would be sucessior couldn't even mimic. It's story is presented in such a way that, while no one ever says anything, you still understand what's going on, what these two kids are struggling with, and how NiGHT's is trying to help them with such before even they need the assistance of the kids in the end.
It's wimsyical, magical, and perhaps given just a bit more prase then it's fully worth. Yet I think if you really talk towards anyone who played this game in any fashion, more less played it yourself, you might too understand just what got birthed doing a time when gaming was in it's true 'golden age'.

Most of the time I feel like I hate cyberpunk. It's a genre that lends itself too well to existential angst and superficial anti-corporatism. The themes of human identity in the face of transhumanism and the threat of all subsuming, monolithic corporation feel overplayed to me. They've lost their appeal to me through sheer overuse.
Nonetheless, I can't help but appreciate the aesthetic and style of the genre. There is an inescapable appeal in hard boiled sour old badasses walking the worn wet streets of slums and ghettos orders of magnitude more technologically complex than contemporary society, feebly clinging to their humanity in the face of dilemma after dilemma. For me, Blade Runner captured this atmosphere and mood, and for that it is one of my favorite films. Gemini Rue has also nailed this feeling and ambience, and because of that I keep coming back to it years after my first playthrough. It's not a groundbreaking game, but it's a fantastic experience which is probably well worth your time.

Greetings, dungeon keep...err, I mean Underlord,
I had been playing Dungeon Keeper II for a couple of decades when I heard about this game by chance, back when it was still bare-bones early access.
At the time I bought it mainly to get some money to the devs in the hopes that they would actually produce a worthy sequel to the aforementioned Dungeon Keeper II and not just take me and the other early accessers money and run laughing into the hills. So I played the bare-bone version when I bought it, felt a bit ambivalant about it and then as the months passed I forgot completely that I even had it. Until now that is!
So, coming back to the game now that it is more fleshed out, has a couple of campaigns and is generally a lot stabler I must say that I'm really enjoying it. It still has its issues but I cant tell if thats my now somewhat decrepid computer or the game itself; Units occasionally just freezeing in place and not doing anything being the most common and annoying problem. Other than that, it looks good, feels good. The narrator is spot on. The art direction pretty interesting and yeah, I suppose over all it just feels like I'm playing Dungeon Keeper III.
Now this last part is both high praise and a bit of a negative critique in one; DKII set the gold standard for dungeon management sims so the fact that this delivers the same albeit somewhat updated experience is awesome. To an extent.
Yes there are more mechanics to enjoy such as in game research, alchemy and rituals but it still feels almost like a reskinned carbon copy of DKII. Almost. Although maybe that's what they were intentionally going for. I havent read the dev blogs or anythign but if that is the case, kudos to them. They really nailed it. It would have been nice to see a tad more ambition but ho hum... Still, this is by no means a damning indictment of the game, just an observation. I wanted a spiritual successor to DKII and I got one. I haven't tried any of the other Dungeon Sims that has been cropping up recently so I can't compare.
All in all, an enjoyable game to sate my inner dungeon architect. Because that's the most fun part right? Designing the actual dungeon and making it look all nice? Building up ingenious defences and watching the good guys crash and break against the bulwarks only to be dragged unconcious into the dark echoing interior to never see the light of day again, yeah?
Well, it is for me in any case; in game as well as in real life...

I may have said too much.
Dungeon? I know of no dungeons, officer...

***This review is written from a private server perspective. I have not played on the public servers, and probably never will. I don't know anything about the problems with the public servers. I also do not PVP***
Alright. To start his review off short and sweet. This game is good. Updates are regular, fixes come in pretty fast. That being said THIS IS STILL EARLY ACCESS. If you don't know what that means, go here. There will be bugs. If you can't handle crashes, server wipes, losing items, losing progress, then this game isn't for you. No early access game is.
It has bugs. Lots of them. The building is actually quite smooth and works very well. The graphics are also fairly nice, but the animations need work. NPC pathing and AI are pretty much alpha AI. They're on the docket. The company has said they are going to be upgrading them in the future. This can make pve combat somewhat... well I don't want to say boring because it's still scary, but less active and more hack and slash. There's not a lot of reason to use anything beyond a sword. Pike's have range, but the AI just closes the range and starts wacking at you, there's not really any pushback system. This kind of ai/combat restraints make it more of a spam attack game at the moment.
Building. Like I said before, it's very well done. I've yet to encounter a problem building a structure. I wish there was 90 degree triangles, but the triangle system they have can make some cool designs, even if they are a little tricky to get used to.
Gathering is pretty straight forward. You hit a node with a certain tool and you get resources. The amount of resources depends on the tier of the tool. On private servers you can increase or decrease the amount of resources people get. You can also do this with xp, mob health, mob dmg, minion health, minion dmg etc. That's one of the greatest selling points about this game. Private servers have a HUGE amount of power right from the slider menu.
The Thrall portion of the game is probably one of the things that interest me the most. It's also one of the buggiest right now. Thralls seem to disappear if left on regular ground. Or if they're floating a bit, or for some other reasons. But it's also one of the funnest. Running off to an enemy NPC camp to "tonk" someone is about as fun as it gets. Murder the camp, tonk the person you want to take with you, cook some gruel for them, and bam. After about an hour to three, depending on the rank, you have a new best friend! The placing of these thralls is like an item, and they'll react to incoming dangers or work your resources for you. Right now they're glitchy. And their Ai makes them more of a turret than actual NPC's in your village. But *hopefully* with later patches we get a solid AI, that lets you build a thriving town or settlement with npcs actually interacting with stuff.
The devs have also been very keen about involving the community. There's already been a variety of changes based on user opinion. That's the biggest reason to get in right now, if you like the direction this game is heading. If you don't really care about input, and just want to play the finished game, wait. I'm sure it will still be in early access this time next year, so wait and see where the games at then.
Pros: - Game runs fine on a private server. Still a little laggy at times though.
- Building is in working order. Can build some pretty cool stuff.
- Thrall system is cool if not buggy.
- Random NPC camps and monster make the came more PvE focused than most others. Good if you're playing coop.
- Base game ideas are very cool. Where they talk about taking the game also sounds very cool. You can watch their                  streams to gauge for yourself.
- Makes you feel very afraid at times. Survival aspect is spot on.
- Most of the difficulty and progress is in your admins hands.
- Full of neat Conan lore

Cons: - NPC AI is poor. Most things can be two-manned pretty easily. The mobs will just spam attack too. There's no variety. To be fixed in the future.
- Some people still have troubles joining servers. Maybe user error, may be game errors.
- The customization in game is limited. Only three armor sets and the moment, but there are some clothing sets from the different religions. More clothes/armor incoming in future updates.
- There's bugs. Not a lot of game breaking ones, but they can still get annoying.
- I read about a lot of pvp imbalances. Not surprising in early access. Or in pvp.
- I personally find some parts to be too easy. Waters plentiful, food can be grabbed from bushes. But again, the amount of food and water decay you have can be edited in the settings. Most mobs can't catch you as you sprint away, minus hyenas and spiders. I've been asking for varied animal attacks to help with this. Hopefully it comes true.
That's about it. Right now I'd give it a solid 8/10 for the price point. Will definitely continue to play, and maybe in a few months I'll update this review.

This is still one of - if not THE best - medieval conquest games I've ever played (I still own my original CD and manual!). Granted, it does show its age in the graphics and some parts of the interface, but the basic gameplay is solid. Everything is easily managed from the well-constructed sidebar menu, from population management and weapons production to army recruitment and diplomacy. While the combat engine suffers from some issues with unit pathfinding, the battle system is still quite engaging and fun, with success depending on correct use of terrain, tactics, and combined arms. Given that this Steam version includes the Siege Pack expansion with a tactical map editor and a slew of added campaign maps, at its current bargain price this classic game is an absolute steal. Definitely a must-have for nostalgic strategy fans.

Plenty of great levels
Unique "mobs"
A great leveling system.

For "Legit" Achievement hunters its a great game you'll obtain most of the achievement while playing. If you "beat" the game most likely you'll be able to obtain most of the achievements without having to spend too much time doing so.
Majority of my play time was just playing the game, I think I spend an additional 2 hours trying to obtain some of the achievements I didn't obtain before "beating/finishing" the last level or "hidden level". And on a last note the game didn't feel tedious, I'm not sure about the rest of you but some TD games feel tedious to me.

So I've finished the game and it really was an awesome game, but it has its flaws and there is a big drop in quality after the first two acts, but I still consider this an approvement over the divinity original sin, which was a wonderful game. So any fan of the previous title should really try this one. I'm sure there are plenty of review, which highlight the positive aspects of the game, I'm not really good at that, so I'll just let you know, that I've enjoyed the dialogues, the combat, the characters, the magic and the overall RPG elements.
Fair warning, the game has a lot of bugs still, personally I've encountered just one potentially game breaking bug, which had to be solved by running away while using unarmed civilians as distraction, if that haven't worked I would have to load a previous save, god bless their souls (not the godwoken, I've let them to die and never looked back). But the most annoying bugs concern the journal entries, which track your quest progression, they do not update correctly, which is really irritating, since the story and your choices should be really important part of this game and the journal should reflect that, but that is unfortunately not so at this moment. Hopefully this will be fixed in the future updates. Because it really takes away the joy of completing the quest, when the journal indicates afterwards, what a horrible person you are for not finishing it.
I have two more things, which I would like to mention. First thing are the elves, the terrible desing for the elves, I don't mind that much, that they have necks like girrafes or that they have wrinkled skin, what bothered me the most are the armor design. You take a plate armor, put it on human, lizard and undead with small changes, you put it on a dwarf with a little bigger change, but you put it on an elf and you get half naked person with something which looks like roots on the chest area and two oversized pauldrons on your shoulder. In the end they look terrible and you can't even hide it with armor, because the armor doesn't cover them. I guess it is a price you have to pay for their very usefull abilities. Second thing is splash effect, because the developers really wanted you to enjoy their system of elements everything has to have some splash effects, so the elemental play will be everywhere. It can get really tedious to controll the enviroment effects, in the end I preferred to use physical weapons over amazing source skills, so I wouldn't have to deal with splashing a bit of fire over poison and start a chain reaction, because there is always some oil and some other element elsewhere, god forbid you hit enemy with elemental skin, which makes them bleed element, causing another chain reaction.
Therefore I do recommend the game, but I would suggest you to wait for a bit before playing. I will certainly wait for them to fix the issues and then replay the game with different origin and more importantly with mods, so I can enjoy the game to the fullest.

I played the original Divinity when it released from early access. That game had some dark undertones, but overall felt pretty whimsical. Combat was very challenging, and I never beat it after getting stuck on the last boss. The main complaint I had was a lack of direction. There wasn't a clear overarching goal besides defeating the big bad, or path to getting there. There were often no hints on where to go next and I spent most of my time bumbling into fights way too hard for me and rerolled my characters often.
Divinity 2 vastly improves upon all of those aspects. Combat is still challenging, but rather than being overwhelmed by AI's mastery of combos and status effects immediately, you have a chance to resist them through the new armor mechanic. There are clear goals and some nudges in the right direction for where to head, but it still feels quite open and free. You can still blunder into areas you have no business being in, but quests and conversations will give you a good idea of where to go.
Divinity 2 also features, in my view, a huge tone shift towards dark and unsettling. The original showed some nasty things, but mostly as a gag effect. There is some really heavy♥♥♥♥♥♥going on in Rivellon now.
I love the game and would recommend it to anyone seeking a story rich, tactical turn based RPG.

Now that all of the good things are said, here are the bad things. The team might be spending on too much time polishing the game, mostly because it is in alpha so there isn't as much functionality as there could be. It looks cool and all, but right now they are just holding the game back from where it could be. It is like they are focused on making the game perfect as they are making it, instead of making it perfect when it is done. This will kill the game because a lot of the people playing it will just get board seeing the same things over and over, with them being modified to look better. They are just putting more work in than they have to, because say they add a feature, polish it, then it conflicts with an even better feature. With that said, it is a good game, and people should get it because they will, definetly, enjoy themselves. Whether it be a person who is in parkour, an arcade fighting game, or animals killing animals, it will be a game that will be enjoyed and loved.

TL:DR
I used to love this game, it was the "perfect MMO" to me for a time.
But then Trion went and ♥♥♥♥ed it up.
Long Version
For those of you that weren't around for the early days of the game here is a short history lesson. [Some of the details may be a little off because it has been several years]
In Beta/Alpha the game was great, had very stable servers and showed us all what the game SHOULD have been,tons of us spend the $200 (I think it was it’s been a few years now) just to play the Alpha for a time which was AMAZING, however there were still some major concerns that SHOULD have been addressed BEFORE release. For example, I remember myself and people in my guild wondering if we were going to actually be able to secure any decent amount of land for ourselves and the guild. So we studied the forum posts of all the major guild leaders and officers to figure out which servers the were going to go to at launch and we chose the one that they did not pick... Ollo.
Come launch day the release was an absolute travesty! Even though those of us who bought the most expensive package were supposed to get access to the game 3 days before anyone else the servers were damn near impossible to get into on early launch day because the que times were as high as 6 hours for some people in my guild, and not only that we come to find out that the major guilds that me and my guild mates were trying to avoid found that when they managed to get into their servers most of the land [that was easily accessible] was ALREADY CLAIMED BY HACKERS/SCRIPTERS within the first hour or 2 OF LAUNCH. So they all switched over to Ollo which prior to release was projected to be only a medium populated server and within hours of release was bursting at the seams with people trying to claim land.
A few days later after the land situation had calmed down and we all accepted that we were going to have to take what scraps we could get and that hackers and scripters were going to be the land barons of the game, there was newfound hope. Trion decided to double the number of servers, my guild looked at this as a 2nd chance to get the plot of land we wanted for ourselves as a guild and they moved over to one of the new servers. Me however, I had already achieved level 50 because I decided to no life and at least level while all of the other drama went down hoping trion would
-Limit the amount of land plots that an ACCOUNT can have claim to
-Do extensive bans of anyone suspected of scripting
-Make it to where an unfinished structure can only occupy a plot for a few hours unless it’s completed
But these things never happened, these 3 major SUGGESTIONS that the community had mentioned to Trion since ALPHA continued to fall on deaf ears.
So there I was….. stuck on a server with a random guild opposed to the one I had been with since Alpha, in possession of a few scraps of land spread all over the both continents, with a Gally I slaved to build, MAX level commerce profession (2nd or 3rd in NA I think), a nice set of gear (for the time), and a newfound interest for the music making system in the game…..and the cash shop controversy hit. I was one of the many that were outraged that Trion was more focused on making more money from us instead of fixing ANY of the major issues plaguing the game. But I continued to play the game because it was so good……..Then Auroria was released and it was the day 1 debacle all over again like Trion didn’t learn a goddamn thing from their mistakes after all this time. Again we got to log in on the release day of Auroria and see scripters and hackers had already claimed all of the castle nodes within hours of release. For me this was the end of Archeage.
But what’s really sad about this whole story is that, not only is it one of the earliest examples [for me] of how CORPORATE GREED can ruin an amazing game that I absolutely enjoyed and sunk hours upon hours into [Steam hour count is was off] plus several hundred dollars before it even released, we still see this same cycle repeated over and over and over with MMOs that have come out the past few years and it seems Archeage was the game that set me into the spiral of jumping from game to game every few weeks interrupted by going back to WoW to for a few weeks to remind myself it’s not half the game it used to be interrupted by going back to Eve for a few weeks to remind myself again that CCP are ♥♥♥♥ing idiots and half of the community are cancerous ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s just to repeat the cycle all over again.
So from the bottom of my heart, for all of the friends that this game made me lose contact with, all of the time and money I wasted, and more importantly for the loss of the dream that this game was.

If I could choose neutral for this review I would.  This game is around 21 years old and should firmly fall into the category of abandonware.  More addictive retro games are given free legally by content owners.  I bought the game hoping to rekindle memories of a fantastic game and if I were playing 21 years ago it may well get a 5 star review, with little else like this.  The trouble is, since then, Total War has been made and even the original Rome Total War stacks up 100 times better than this game (i.e. Rome Total War may give you 100+ hours of fun, but this game 1 before you get bored with how basic it is).  I thoroughly enjoy retro gaming but have come to realize retro gaming serves a purpose when there is no other game like it, it is a unique proposition.  So I can still play Railroad Tycoon for 100's of hours, or Capitalism Plus, no other business games have been made so well in so much detail.  Well made classics like the original Civilization still provide a challenge, as does Rome Total War which in my opinion is better than the latter Total Wars.  Bullfrog's Theme Park is still unique enough to offer something different to the Rollercoaster Tycoon series.  Sadly though, this game shows its age, the user interface feels dire compared to more modern games, the skirmishes are crazy, the gameplay fairly simple and not complex enough to satisy modern strategy gamers - more modern games offer more depth in gameplay, better graphics, UI and AI and satisfy the same urge.  But, if it wasn't for this game, we might not have had the same modern games that developed, or Stronghold (by the same developers), so this was very much a fore-runner of its generation.  Unless you really want to give it a go or absolutely love this game, I would avoid this in favour of more modern games.
My rating (as of 2017) 5/10 : 50%.  I give it a "Yes" because of its historical importance to modern wargaming and strategy.

Lords of the Realm II - a classic I still like to play after 20 years!
The game is a nice combination of turn-based economics and a pseudo-Warcraft styled RTS combat system.
The goal is to become the King of the realm by defeating the other nobles. There are two campaigns and a lot of maps for custom games available for playing. You can modify the difficulty in a lot of ways especially for the custom games, so you can decide if you want advanved farming or not, eating armies and how strong the opponents are!
The gameplay itself can be very addictive, prepare for long gaming sessions especially on the larger realms.
The graphics are ok for their age, it is decent VGA graphics sufficient enough for the gameplay.
The OST is really nice and adds some atmosphere to the game.
There is also some kind of humour, especially when listening to the troops or when some of the other nobles sending you a letter in rage. And if you beat the campaign you can listen to a funny song!(and if you are too lazy to play through the campaign look for it in the game folder ;-) )
Are there any issues with this game? Well, while it overall runs without problems sometimes strange glitches occur like enemy armies or merchants going over mountains or even the ocean. While I stumbled upon these problems in very rare cases they can happen sometimes. Also I recommend to disable any software that might interrupt the gameplay with notification windows as it is very prone to crash in this case! Fortunately it auto-saves after every turn, still this can be annoying.
Aside this the gameplay also is in some regards unbalanced from my experience. Especially the strenght of the troops. Archers are the cheapest unit to produce only needing wood, but they are the strongest with their high range and fire rate! While knights are despite their high costs not so strong and the other ones are mostly uninteresting. Ok, macemen can act as "cheap knights" with nearly the same speed and rather low costs to produce, sacrificing some armour.
The siege part is also a bit odd, you can build catapults but these won´t do any damage to troops, I guess for balancing issues, so they just destroy the walls of a castle.
Also the animation and movement of the siege weapon looks very odd.
In fact you don´t need them except for a battering ram for the two stronger castles to destroy the drawbridge after the moat has been shoveled up.
The enemy AI is sometimes not that smart, making some games rather easy to win.
Another strange thing I encountered is that none of my capturing programs can record this game - neither FRAPS or Bandicam or other ones did recognise it. Not a real disadvantage, but in case you might to record it for Youtube or other means take note of this.
Despite these little drawback the game is overall enjoyable to play and highly recommended for everyone who likes medieval strategy games.
If I could with for something then it would be the addition of the german translation and dubbing for this game. It is overall well done, rather near to the original and some voices sound even more funny.

Hotline Miami's fast paced twin stick shooting meets Transistor's timeslowing mechanics and ability upgrades. With a sprinkle of cyberpunk on top.
Gameplay 9.75/10:
I had a blast with this! The only issue was that it could get a little repetitive for me at times (timeslow dash, melee, timeslow dash, melee, etc.) but when the game does work, it's fantastic. There's a lot of weapon and playstyle variety.
Atmosphere 7/10:
The atmosphere during gameplay is wonderfully done. The visual style, sounds and story perfectly add up to a very tense, dark atmosphere. Almost disturbing at a few points. The reason I'm giving this a 7/10 is that some of the cutscenes don't do a very good job and virtually break the tension.
Story 7.5/10:
I personally liked the story and was very invested, although, it can be a tad confusing at points, especially near the end. The main themes are technology, humans and greed.
Visuals 8.5/10:
The visuals work great for the game and the color schemes add to the atmosphere. The lighting is very well done and the effects are spot on. Along with this, there is some good art for the game as well.
Content 6.5/10:
It takes around 6-9 hours to beat the main story without doing many side missions. There are three difficulty settings and a new game+ option. Doing a 100% run and then just doing the main story in new game+ would take around 15-20 hours. According to the developers, two new free DLCs will be released eventually.
Overall, I give Ruiner an 8.75/10

Ok, I come from a background of playing Pedal to the Metal and Haulin, respectfully. I've never played ETS or ETS2, so I can't compare this game to those. The following review is on ATS:
Fantastic game! I really enjoy it. It's really well done and is superb, even though it only has three states and two trucks. (more on that later).
Graphics: 8/10. My computer is pretty good. It can handle FSX fine, but for some reason, it struggles with this game. I had to turn down my settings in game and I have to live with jaggies, or else it becomes an unplayble slideshow. I refuse to upgrade to Windows 10 (currently running W7) just to improve the performance, as the aforementioned FSX may then have issues. However, that being said, the graphics are absolutely beautiful! The landscapes at dawn or dusk are truly a sight to behold! The trucks are extremely well done, both inside and out. Shadows moving across the dash, the interior views of the sleepers, etc. You can tell alot of time and effort were put into designing the trucks! One small thing I really like that wasn't doable in the games I mentioned, is the ability to turn on parking lights only without turning the headlights on. This is a cool feature as just like in real life I can illuminate the dash without the headlights needing to be on as well. Also, the rain effects are impressive! (If you want realism, since it rarely rains in the states included, you can turn this effect off.)
Gameplay: 10/10. Yes, gameplay is nearly perfect! In Pedal to the Metal and Haulin, the trucks all drove like high performance autos, I.e. 0-60 MPH in two seconds, even while pulling a fully loaded trailer. Here, the trucks are slow to get up to speed, and definitley feel heavy going up hills. Gives that bit of realism as I struggle to get up to 55 MPH while AI cars pass me. Only small gripe is the cops are really picky. Go five miles over the limit and you will get ticketed. However, you can turn cops off in settings and fly if you prefer.
Fun factor: 10/10. Whether you're a real life trucker, or one who never got the chance to be one but wonders what it'd be like to live life on the road with 18 wheels under you, this game is definitely for you. I find myself spending hours and hours driving around and delivering or dropping off loads. I usually bore of driving sim games after a few days; not so here. Every day after work I come home and start this game, and you can say farewell to me for hours, lol.
In summary: As mentioned above, only three states are available thus far. But you know what? I don't care! Each state is extremely well done, and since I live in Vegas, it's where I started my career. I can say it's pretty darn accurate, right down to the sculptures alongside the 95 freeway! Only gripe would be, freeway offramps and onramps do NOT have stop signs; they have traffic signals. But ok..
Driving from Vegas to Tucson, for example, feels like a long trip, just like in real life. No, it won't take 6 + hours real time, but it sure feels like it! So, three states are enough for me, so long as each additional state they create is just as well-detailed. The states included are more than enough to keep me busy. My first time driving over the Golden Gate Bridge was simply stunning! I almost wrecked trying to enjoy the scenery, lol.
The available upgrades to the trucks (levels) are impressive. Almost like they borrowed features from previous modders. I recommend starting with the Kenworth W900. I was able to upgrade it to include the studio sleeper, an abundance of lights, and a beautiful dashboard after just reaching Level 12.
I'm only using the included defaults, but for those interested in other trucks and aren't willing to wait for SCS, there are plenty of mods available on the internet.
has a nice selection. Also, for those who want a full USA map and again don't want to wait, the same site has one called the "coast to coast v 1.8 map" that's getting positive reviews. They also have one that includes Mexico and Canada, so if you wish to go across the borders, there you go.
In summary: I really enjoy this game. Almost every day I see something new. As an example, the other day I took a wrong turn and went behind an apartment complex. I actually saw a guy dancing in the back of the building, with a girl sitting there watching him! Little things like this really make the game world feel alive. Even little things like an obvious UPS van (although it's called something different in game) being unloaded by a guy in his brown uniform, pedestrians milling about on street corners, the blowing tumbleweeds across the desert road, etc. All are a huge step up from the previous games I played.
Pros: Great graphics, great gameplay, hours of fun, great rewards.
Cons: Poor performance on my better than average machine. Hoping that as more states are released, it doesn't kill my machine.
Limited trucks to drive and only 3 states, but that can be solved with mods as mentioned earlier.
Recommend? Highly!

I fully reccomend this game, with its great soundtrack, gameplay, and artstyle, allowing for a difficult, but rewarding journey.

Lords of the Realm II is a classic game that I spent countless hours playing upon the games initial release. In my opinion this is an improvement over LOTR. The graphics and interface are friendlier and the combat is much better.  On the flipside, the economy has been watered down, making it far less interesting and challenging than the original.
The overall objective of this game is to♥♥♥♥♥♥ pillage, and conquer the neutral as well as the enemy controlled counties of the map. Each map varies in the number of counties such as 4 or 6, for example. In order to meet the objective, one must build up an economy, raise troops, and go out and conquer the surrounding lands. All the while, the AI is doing the same.
As noted the economy is much easier to handle in this game. For example, agriculture has two options, grain and cows. However, there is also the buying and selling of iron, stone, and wood as well as varies weapons that the prudent seller/manufactuer may make money on.
On the upside the combat part of the game is much improved however, with the ability to position and move your troops much more fluidly, so you can try to outflank the enemy, or bottleneck the enemy in defensive terrain (ideally with melee troops defending a bridge while your archers and crossbows rain death on them).
Please note that you van also build a castle for your county-counties. They range from a motte and bailey to a full stone castle with defenses such as burning oil. Its always nice to have your castle seiged just to kill the enemy with arrows and burning oil.
I wholeheartly recommend this game to anyone who played it intially and to anyone who likes strategy games. The graphics aren't in anyway as fantastic as COH but the game is fun and will frustrate you (in a good way) and make you laugh in a sadistic way.

Dungeon Warfare is a classic Tower Defense game with 1 small differences. Instead of towers you have traps, a lot of traps, actually. The rules are simple, enemies are approaching, place traps to destroy them. Get gold by killing them and place new traps. Repeat until a level is finished. When you get lvl up and upgrade your traps or get new ones. When new level starts. As i said, it's classic.
There were the things I really liked. For example, its really pleasant to see how enemies die :D
Nice visual and sound effects. Also, there are a lot of enemies comes, they gather in group and then a group dies... its awesome feeling.
There is a lot of everything. There are ground traps, wall traps, hook trap, demon portal which summons units on the path, push trap and etc... so you have unlimited choice of ways to pass every level. You received the experience by passing levels and then you get gems which can be spent on upgrades of towers. It's sad, but they gives small bonuses like -1% cooldown time, but there are a lot of them. I know, some people like systems like this. Also, these upgrades unlocks new upgrade for traps. For example, if you will make 15 upgrade for Spike Trap, it will get 3 upgrades +1 damage /+1 damage and 2 upgrades fro choose, add burning effect on attack twice per activation.
There is interesting mechanic for setting difficulty. There are 12 tunes in the game, each rune add an feature to the game (enemies get extra health or you have got only 1 live and etc.). If you take rune to the battle, the game becomes harder, but you will receive increased reward, up to 7 times of basic. So, you can change the difficulty of the game whatever you want with such interesting mechanic.
There are also things which I could describe as boring. First of all, the bestiary of enemies is small. I have passed about 15 levels and have met only 7-8 different enemies. There comes an another flow, the design of waves of levels. They are... the same... A bunch of peasants with nobles comes at the first waves. Fast moving thieves com at the 2 or second wave. Then knights with moderate HP and armor appear. At the last wave a lot of Crusaders com, they have large amount of health and heavy armor. So, I after I realized it after ~12 mission, the game become pretty boring for me. Yeah, new traps, units, runes appear... I am an old TD fan, but it wasn't enough for me.
Also, this game lacks of strategy. There is no special strategy for different enemies. All traps are good against all enemies. So it's possible to pass the mission without any thinking. I don't think it's a good feature for a strategy game.
This game will be interesting for TD fans. People who like sandboxes and games with not strict goals and ways of their achievement will find this game satisfying. But this freedom brings a lack of diversity between missions. Anyway, the game is worth for a try. I recommend it

Fallen Earth, in my opinion, is one the best MMOs I've played; the community is very helpful when needed and the GMs keep the help section of the chat regulated and reduce spam as much as possible. There are a total of 55 player levels as of now, im only level 30 so I havent really seen everything, but from what I have experienced, a very enjoyable game.
For me, the one biggest problem is definitely the client-to-client synchronization. Players may look as if they are in a position, but really they may not be there. You may also see NPCs glide across the screen due to the synchronization being terrible, but it has improved a bit. In the beginning, you start off with an axe, two knives, and three pellet guns (one being an air rifle and the other two being pistols). After about two or three of the beginning missions, you are awarded a horse for basic transportation, but as you progress further into the game, you get other mounts/vehicles. The basic vehicles are: ATVs, Motorcycles, Dune Buggies, and Interceptor Speedsters (basic cars). Each vehicle has many different variations that you can craft.
The crafting system isnt too complex, but it can be very slow; vehicles can take up to a few days to fully craft from raw materials, but smaller items, such as ammunition, can take a few minutes. If crafting isnt your thing, then there is also an auction house in almost every city; here you can buy player-listed items for how ever much the player lists the item for.
If youre someone who absolutely has to have good graphics, then you may not be too fond of this game; the graphics are pretty bad, but that shouldnt really be too big of a deal if you dont mind it. There are also limits to free to play players however, but they can easily be negated by purchasing any single item from the game's market place. The only limitations i am aware of are a limit to how many chips you can have (currency), a character limit of only one character and no access to the Global chats, but there may be more. In my opinion, its definitely worth it to go 'freemium' by just buying a really cheap item from the store, or by purchasing the Survivalist Package that is offered by Steam. I believe that the limit to the amount of chips you can have if you are free to play is about 100,000 chips. This would be 10 red chips and each red chip is 10,000 chips. Chips go by: Yellow>Red>Blue>White. Blue is 100 white, Red is 100 Blue and Yellow is 100 Red.
There is a total of six different sectors in the game (The entire province is huge, roughly 83km by 83km, according to the Wiki) which all have different fast travel locations that you must first travel to via mount/vehicle. The game also encourages palyers to use roadways with vehicles as they provide a 'boost' and significantly increase your speed. There are also six major factions you can choose to be a part of once you reach Sector 2: The Techs, The Enforcers, Travelers, The Lighbearers, The Vistas, and The CHOTA. Each faction provides unique equipment that you cannot use unless you have a certain reputation with the appropriate faction.
All in all, a very enjoyable game that will last a while if you can dedicate yourself to playing.

You get a speed boost when you ride on the main roads, you can roleplay and go killing other players who are in PvP mode.  I recommend it to anyone who loves Fallout and is dying to play it online with people.

This game is really really good. I fell in love with it during the first five minutes of gameplay. It is surprising challenging but everything feels so responsive and realistic. You are an animal (mainly rabbit, but can be a cat, dog, wolf..maybe more?) who is trained in the martial arts. What I mean by that is, you jump and can do flips, wall run and wall climb, and the combat is amazing. It is really tough trying to get the hang of everything though. I've only played about an hour and I am repeatingly dying. AI is tough when you are new to the controls and same with the maps where there are no enemies, you just climb. You have a chance of taking fall damage if you fall high enough, and if you do a flip at the wrong time, you can snap your neck and die. It is very realistic and a very good game.
However... I think this is just limited down to my computer as it is not as powerful as most gamer computers...in fact... calling it a gaming computer is a bit of an over statement... the game constantly crashes on my computer. I open up the editor to add an object into my game and it crashes. I go to the menu to load up a new level and it crashes. The crashes are rather annoying, and they do put a dim on my experience.
But because I think the issue is limited down to just my computer being not as strong as I would like it to be, I would recommend this game. It is fun, and fast pasting. You have so many hot keys and so much freedom. I doubt I will tire of this game.
I know that the game is early access. But the developers need to put more keys on for the controller. Like the pause menu or slow motion hot key. Also, I enjoy playing on a controller more, but the default settings for the controller keys are rather annoying and it can't be changed. They did put options to rebind keys... only it is for keyboard only and not controller. Hoping to see a controller menu in the next update!
Overall, it was a very great game. I see bigger AAA companies pumping out sequels what seems like every other month and they are messy. (Battlefield 4 anyone?). This game which is still in the ALPHA, has put those AAA titled games to shame. Wait to go!

It's very hard for me to review this game and give it a straight thumbs up or thumbs down. It's not a bad game, it's just a badly made paid system in place, which is the only reason I'm forced to give ArcheAge a thumbs down.
ArcheAge was one of my first steps into the MMO genre, having never played an MMO before in my life. Upon first getting into it, I could barely run it on my old laptop (I've since upgraded and it runs perfectly smooth now), but it has always held a special place in my heart. That being said, I never got to the higher levels when I first started, and finally I have on my newer laptop.
The good in this game is that it's very beautiful, very open-world feeling. To top that, however, ArcheAge has an amazing character creation, one of the best I've seen yet. It easily outclasses Tera in this regard, and is a solid competetor with Black Desert Online. It's also one of the only free to play MMOs I've encountered that let you fully customize your class, your skill line, and let you reset whenever you want to. Which personally, having started in ArcheAge left me severely disappointed when other free to play MMOs I got into didn't have this feature.
As you level they introduce you to housing, farming, and all of your basic PvE MMO things. What they don't tell you, however, is that this is gated behind a subscription. In fact, most of the "basic" MMO functions in this game are gated behind their Patron subscription. You'd think the tutorial on these things would be reserved for those who had bought into it, or it at least be made clear that you will not have access to this if you level. But they don't. For a game that advertises itself as a Sandbox MMO this is severely disappointing. I understand why they don't inform the player that you have to buy into these perks (surprise them with having to buy it so it looks more appealing), but I feel like that isn't a thing you should be gating behind a paywall, and a subscription-based paywall at that.
Your sense of choice really stops at character creation, unless you buy-in. Your mount is selected for you based on your class, you can't do anything but grind levels unless you buy into their Patron subscription, and it leaves everything feeling just a little dull, where you can easily pick up another free to play MMO or even drop a small amount of money into a non-subscription based MMO.
Overall, I recommend this game only if you're willing to sink your money into a free to play game. A lot of people throw around the term pay to win, but I would more accurately label ArcheAge as "play to have fun after level 50 or so". People new to MMOs are better off looking elsewhere, or just playing casually if you must.

Absolutely the best contemporary point-and-click adventure game I've played in years - and I play a lot of adventure games. The characters, the story, the dystopian retro-cyberpunk setting and the clever, yet logical, puzzles all contribute to making this a beautiful adventure that deserves to be praised and regarded as a classic in the years to come.
The game also contains several easter eggs and secrets which, along with the branching dialogue paths in the story, the behind-the-scenes commentary, and the alternative solutions to puzzles, should contribute to its re-playability factor.
The only aspects that I find mar this otherwise flawless gem include the combat scenes (which feature quite heavily towards the end - yes, you can die), the inability to change the resolution from the in-game options menu (which led to some heavy pixellation on my 1920x1080 screen) and the lingering sense that your in-game decisions don't have a large effect on the conclusion of the story.

This is a great game, but I spent alot of time playing DK1 and DK2, and the way WrtO differs seems to be in its pace, more so in skirmish against AI, the thing I enjoyed about DK was the slower pace, once you got past the tutorial levels you would normally start on one huge map which you had to spend time gathering gold and leveling up your minions, where as this one kinda forces you to play fast and with limited space, so theres no extravagant massive rooms you can build since you really need to use the space you have effectively.
The units themselves are very nicely done, but once again it lacks the content DK had, so if you dont know, on DK you had to manage your minions, and by this I mean there wasnt just a single minion per room so for instance in DK if you got a Fly and a Spider, you would normally have to try and keep them in seperate lairs because if they bump into once other when they arent training or using rooms they would attack and try to kill one another, this presenting a challenge if you wanted to keep both but served as something you really needed to keep an eye on, whereas in WftO there is just one type of minion per room and a empire version, none of your minions conflict everyone gets along very nicely.
Now the "Vampire" unit I do like very much, having to keep a steady supply to keep them appeased and in return you get a very powerful unit, so here im going to refer to DK1 and you can proberly guess I mean the "Horned Reaper" which was the games icon, which the Vampire unit itself is a nod to, both units need 3 units sacrificed to get one in return, whereas the vampire just needs food to stay happy, the Horned Reaper, well he was undeniably the strongest unit in the game but came with the biggest price, if you held him for to long he got♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ if you slapped him he got♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ if he was bored he got♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and he would begin slaughtering your own minions for the damn well fun of it, and a level 10 version of him would wipe out most of your minons, which would make you either decide on building a seperate mini-dungeon and lock him in it til you was ready to fight or having to get rid.
Refering to the pervious point there was the "Temple" room, which you sacrificed units to make ones you needed or the Horned Reaper, but it served a second function, any creatures rebelling or Horned Reaper going on a rampage you could drop them on the outskirts of this room and they would pray and calm down over a period of time, now when they rebel in WftO you pretty much have to take them down, I could be wrong but at this present time I cant see anyway to calm them down, showered them with gold/food and they still wont revert from rebellion status.
All in all the thing about these games is feeling like the bad guy, and DK did that great, WftO goes down the same road but doesnt give me that "Evil" vibe, aslong as you have food and gold, all your minions will hold hands and slip to battle, but here I am just remembering how much I loved DK, this game gets frequent patches and updates so who knows, maybe it will end up that way, but it is a great game and the closest ive seen to being a "Dungeon Keeper" for a long time  and is definatly worth playing, more so if you loved the DK games.
TL;DR
WftO is a great game, I ♥♥♥♥♥ and moan about how much I miss "Dungeon Keeper".  :D

This game, as a concept, is great. The shooting is decent enough by modern standards, the vehicle gameplay is pretty solid, the base construction isn't too bad, but the one thing that lets this game down more than anything else is the player base. Everytime I try to come back, it is very difficult to find a server, and even when you do, there is no point in playing on it. The community in this game is by far the most toxic and unforgiving playerbase on the internet, worse than any other game I have ever played. If you make a mistake, they will flame you, if you disagree with how to play, they will flame you. It is impossible to actually enjoy this game, because it is so full of trolls, jerks, and just generally toxic players. The game never really changes, there are probably still bugs in it which have been around for years. I love this game, I really do, I miss being able to play it, but the community is so vile, it is not worth the time or effort.

Моя самая первая и самая любимая cellshading-овая игрушка.Одна из лучших игр на Dream'e.Яркая,пёстрая,живая и динамичная,с неповторимой атмосферой и игровым стилем.Сюжетик хоть и довольно банальный,но его подача достойна похвалы.Местный диджей так и сыпет харизмой.А эти вставки между уровнями,просто очень крутые...И всё под отличную музыку,идеально вписывающуюся в антураж этого мирка.Далеко не бомжовскую кстати,даже Rob Zombie есть :D.Геймплэй очень простой-катаемся и красим,попутно делая трюки и доставляя массу неприятностей местным властям.Чем техничней и безупречней вы проходите уровень-тем больше очков вам начислят,тем лучше будет оценен ваш скилл.Игра не даёт расслабиться,руки здесь постоянно заняты,вечно что-то крутишь и зажимаешь.Лучше всего играть с джоем,на клавиатуре проблематично красить,но выкрутиться всё же можно.После прохождения сюжета в игре есть чем заняться-половина персонажей как правило не открыта,да и "души графити" спрятаны в хитрожопых местах.
К сожалению,сейчас таких игр больше не делают.Есть небольшие возможности кастомизации-можно создать своё граффити,при желании можно и дальше пойти...
Игрушка цепляет,жаль сейчас таких больше не делают.Единственный существенный минус-это отсутствие мультплеера.Было бы забавно соревноваться в закрашивании,одновременно прикрывая пукан от чьего-нибудь squirt gun.В целом,довольно удачный HD-ремейк получился,не считая только многочисленные краши и отстутствие одной песни из оригинальной игры.

I'm torn between a positive review and a negative one on this one.
On one hand, it is a faithful continuation of the dungeon keeper style, on the other, it could really do with some more polish, and that’s 1 year after its initial release, and even then it needed a pretty decent amount of polish as well.
My biggest gripe with it is that there are a lot of stuff that only really shines with some attention to detail, a quality I feel Subterranean Games lacks in some areas; For instance, why are my minion just in the animation they were in when I picked them up? both DK1 and 2 had them visible hang from my hand, struggling even, yet here they just kind of get attached to the model of my hand, unchanging, it's small thing yes, but it lends a certain amount of credence to your role, as well as theme, with you being an extremely powerful being, being able to just pick up and do with the lower minions whatever you want.
On top of that the campaign seems way shorter than any of the DK games, I'm willing to chalk some of it up to being extremely familiar with the genre, but another factor is that a large amount of the missions you're on a timer, which is in stark contrast to DK2, if not DK1 where it more often than not let the cunning Keeper control the engagement, and you're either forced into a battle because of a lack of resources than anything else.
HOWEVER, this is just what it does wrong, what it does right is atmosphere, it's ideas, it expands upon Dungeon Keeper in a pleasing way, there are certainly room for improvement, and while I don't expect the Campaign to see much of it, the general gameplay is still being updated, and if you're an ancient dungeon keeper like me, you're sure to find some value in this game.
The progress and bug fixing is really fast. Known and popular bugs get patched within days and that's enough for me. One of the few games that I actually see potential.

I love driving my car aimlessly for hours in real life and sometimes I like to do just that in the video game world. I used to drive trucks for a company years ago and I miss it. This gives me a lot of that enjoyment without having to change careers in real life since it's a simulator. I'll admit, I pirated Euro-Truck Simulator long before this game came out as I had never experienced this type of simulator before and thought it may be boring. I was so impressed with how awesome Euro-Truck was, I bought a copy at the store and bought American Truck Sim shortly after via Steam.
I play all different types of games like RPGs and racing games to shooters and the occasional hockey game. If you have the attention span of a gnat or have to kill something every 3 seconds to be entertained then you might not appreciate the simulator genre of games and thus this one wont be for you, but if you love driving, exploring, realism and especially semi-trucks, then I would definately suggest buying this and/or Euro Truck Sim.
Pros:
--A wide variety of AI traffic is VERY important for immersion and this game has a fantastic array of vehicles puttering about around you.
--The graphics are great
--The game play is easy to figure out and to get used to.
--Very realistic but not so real that it's tedeous and annoying.
--One of the very few games I love to use the first person in-cabin view as the interior of the trucks are wonderfully replicated.
--Hiring other drivers allows you to make more money as it can be slow at the beginning but gives you something else to save your money for if you already have the truck you want which is awesome.
Cons:
--The ONLY...and I mean literally the ONE disapointing feeling I have towards this game is that there are not enough truck models to choose from like there were in Euro-Truck Sim. There are loads of manufacturers operating in North America and I suspect SCS has plans to realease more as time passes but I was expecting to have more than two or three base truck models to choose from when I first played the game so I had to resort to modding the game to have more options.
What I would like to see in future updates and expansions:
--I would LOOOOOVE to see many many more truck models and manufacturers both new and past models like CAT, Freightliner, Volvo, Mack, Western Star, International (I'd imagine licensing is a nightmare but the more choices, the better!)
--I would love it if they could continue adding to the already large array of cargos you can accent including maybe official "overzied" cargos some how.
--I would also like the devs to continue adding customization options as updates are produced like many more unique wheel options, different style lighting add-ons or even slammed suspension setups and many more variations of exhaust stack setups.
Anyway, EXCELLENT game, great work SCS!! Thanks for providing a much needed escape from the often brutal real world we all live in!

I want to like War for the Overworld. I do. I probably could grow to like it, if it would let me play it. But between constant crashes and a gameplay style choice that just dosesn't work well for me, I'm left frustrated and disappointed. Sometimes you just can't go back to the way things were.
WftO has all the pieces to be a great spiritual successor to Dungeon Keeper 2; one of my favorite games of all time. The voice acting is nostalgiariffic, and the UI tickles all the old neurons that have been left dormant since EA murdered the Dungeon Keeper franchise in its sleep, lo these many years ago. The dialogue is funny, the creatures are creative, the spells and traps make me feel just as evil and fiendish as their inspirations did in prior decades. That should be enough to put this game over the top, for me. But the devil's in the details.
I'm not a huge fan of the rushes in the campaign levels I've gotten to see, so far. This game seems to be a lot more about defending your half-built and shoddily repaired dungeon from increasingly dire and unavoidable enemy incursions than about actually building up your dungeon as you explore the level and probe the enemy's defenses. That might be good news for some fans, but it's not really what made DK2 fun for me, personally. There seems to be a lot less freedom in how you can tackle the campaign levels if you want to survive - which seems ironic, given the plethora of new options WftO gives to you. No matter what gadgets are at your disposal, you have to move fast, you have to focus on immediate survival over long-term planning, and you have to rush for whatever objective the stage gives you, over exploring. If that's how you already wanted to play, then great. But I miss the more methodical pace I remember from DK2.
But that's a minor complaint. I could get past it, and find a game I still enjoy, even with some caveats, if not for the fact that it crashes so much it's barely playable. I have restarted the fourth level four times, because the game simply refuses to remain functional long enough for me to beat it. I've had similar issues with other stages. Saving can be used to brute-force your way through a level while losing minimal amounts of progress over and over, but is that fun? If I have to restart, I want it to be because I lost, or because I want to try a new strategy, not because the game is so unstable I have to restart the game (or reboot my computer!) every 5 - 15 minutes.
Maybe I'm the only one with this problem. I can't imagine that after all this time, this degree of crashing is still a problem for eveyone who plays this game, or there's no way it'd have remotely positive reviews. But I can only speak from my own experience, and for me, the game is basically unplayable. I more than meet the recommended specs, for what it's worth.
I have waited so long (3+ years!) for WftO to become stable. But I honestly think it crashed less back in Early Access. I give up, for now. I'll let it simmer on the back burner of my library for another couple of years, I guess, and hope it's actually functional by the time I get back to it. In the meantime, I can't recommend it.

Wave Mechanics is an intriguing puzzle game. You have a board full of tiles, some of them are numbered. Numbered tiles send waves into the direction of your choice, with length corresponding to the numbers on the tiles. The wave inverts the color of the tiles it affects (including the original tile itself), then the number of the tile decreases by one. You need to eliminate all numbered tiles by decreasing their value to 0, and at the same time the board's tiles need to correspond to the color defined by the board.
The game starts out fun and easy, then the difficulty starts to increase. While all the puzzles can be solved by logic, you will need to consider more and more subsequent waves in order to ensure that a certain move is right. At some point, your brain is liable to run out of capacity - for me, it was the halfway point in stage 6 where more and more 4s started to creep into the puzzles. Actually, it was fun up to the end of level 5, and increasingly tedious afterwards.
Wave Mechanics generates its puzzles procedurally, which is very impressive on one hand as the generated puzzles are quite good, however, as the difficulty increases, I certainly miss the human touch to make some of the levels a bit more approachable. I had one nightmare level in stage 4, but then those didn't return until stage 6. I also doubt that many people find the game fun on or past stage 6 - I may be wrong, though.
Certainly recommended, but be on the lookout for the levels where you feel more like wasting time than having fun. You get the best experience out of the game if you stop there - maybe use the procedural generator to your advantage and generate a new level set and play the lower stages once again.

tl:dr -> Excellent game for FPS and RTS fans; huge amounts of teamwork and customisation; playing with friends makes it even better. And it's free, so what have you got to lose? Give it a try!
Personally, i love this game. The gameplay is unique amongst the FPS and RTS genres; nothing quite like it... And nothing has surpassed it in all these years...
Yes it's old, yes the community is small... But the game has something about it... Something that makes people keep coming back to it over all these years. That's why i'm nominating it for the Test of Time award.
The teamplay element is amazing, it's great to play alone (so much to explore), but even better with friends. Up to 5 of you can form a squad, and earn bonus points for working together...
The game has a lot of depth, huge amounts of customisation available; it's not cosmetics though, but real meaningful options that improve and change how your character plays and the vehicles you can build over the course of a game...
And it has Vehicles too... and now the RTS elements come into play here... you can research new technologies that allow for new weapons, armours, engines and entirely new vehicle chassis that you can get as the game progresses. And you can mix and match these to customise your vehicles to suit whatever tactical situation you need.
The progression isn't like more modern games with item unlocks and new skin rewards; but you can feel that sense of skill progression as you get better with time. It's easy to learn, but incredibly hard to master.
Oh yeah, and its asymmetric, not just red vs blue... Both teams play differently...
Also, its got 64 player servers... so massive 32v32 matches can happen... That's almost unheard of in modern games.
I unreservedly recommend this game to anyone who is a fan of FPS or RTS games. It deserves more players.

Wave Mechanics is a puzzle game made by independent developer Adam Tarnowski who thought of a new way to melt your brain for two euros.
If you've already checked the screenshots, you can see it's about grids, numbers and colors. But that's not a Minesweeper or Picross, it's something new! The gameplay revolves around swapping colors between the squares to get the required color scheme.
It's easy to learn but hard to master - after one third of the game the difficulty gets higher. Since you can't fully rely on your instinct (you'll be making mistakes pretty often), the developer implemented an undo button. That'll save you many times, keeping you in flow instead of making angry and frustrated.
There are totally 49 levels (procedurally generated) divided into 7 chapters - each chapter makes the game harder, with more specific requirement to the state of the grid. The graphic style is minimalistic and in combination with relaxing sounds and music this game is a great casual puzzler with a low price tag. If you are into puzzle games, you'll enjoy this for sure!

Fallen Earth, in my opinion, is one the best MMOs I've played; the community is very helpful when needed and the GMs keep the help section of the chat regulated and reduce spam as much as possible. There are a total of 55 player levels as of now, im only level 30 so I havent really seen everything, but from what I have experienced, a very enjoyable game.
For me, the one biggest problem is definitely the client-to-client synchronization. Players may look as if they are in a position, but really they may not be there. You may also see NPCs glide across the screen due to the synchronization being terrible, but it has improved a bit. In the beginning, you start off with an axe, two knives, and three pellet guns (one being an air rifle and the other two being pistols). After about two or three of the beginning missions, you are awarded a horse for basic transportation, but as you progress further into the game, you get other mounts/vehicles. The basic vehicles are: ATVs, Motorcycles, Dune Buggies, and Interceptor Speedsters (basic cars). Each vehicle has many different variations that you can craft.
The crafting system isnt too complex, but it can be very slow; vehicles can take up to a few days to fully craft from raw materials, but smaller items, such as ammunition, can take a few minutes. If crafting isnt your thing, then there is also an auction house in almost every city; here you can buy player-listed items for how ever much the player lists the item for.
If youre someone who absolutely has to have good graphics, then you may not be too fond of this game; the graphics are pretty bad, but that shouldnt really be too big of a deal if you dont mind it. There are also limits to free to play players however, but they can easily be negated by purchasing any single item from the game's market place. The only limitations i am aware of are a limit to how many chips you can have (currency), a character limit of only one character and no access to the Global chats, but there may be more. In my opinion, its definitely worth it to go 'freemium' by just buying a really cheap item from the store, or by purchasing the Survivalist Package that is offered by Steam. I believe that the limit to the amount of chips you can have if you are free to play is about 100,000 chips. This would be 10 red chips and each red chip is 10,000 chips. Chips go by: Yellow>Red>Blue>White. Blue is 100 white, Red is 100 Blue and Yellow is 100 Red.
There is a total of six different sectors in the game (The entire province is huge, roughly 83km by 83km, according to the Wiki) which all have different fast travel locations that you must first travel to via mount/vehicle. The game also encourages palyers to use roadways with vehicles as they provide a 'boost' and significantly increase your speed. There are also six major factions you can choose to be a part of once you reach Sector 2: The Techs, The Enforcers, Travelers, The Lighbearers, The Vistas, and The CHOTA. Each faction provides unique equipment that you cannot use unless you have a certain reputation with the appropriate faction.
All in all, a very enjoyable game that will last a while if you can dedicate yourself to playing.

Dungeon Warfare is a fantastic tower defense game that offers uniqueness in the genre and plenty of replay value. As of writing the review, I have unlocked all levels and have beaten the game. It took me approximately forty hours to do so. The value here is immense; going by the $1.00 per hour of gameplay rule, you can expect to get four times or more of your money's worth, considering you buy it for full price.
This game is somewhat reminiscent of Dungeon Keeper. Your goal is to prevent the good guys from reaching your dungeon portal, and you must use various traps at your disposal (along with rechargeable spells, of which there are many that you may unlock over the course of the game). Keeping true to the genre, strategy is key, for particular traps are more useful in some areas than others. Unlike many tower defense games, many traps are able to be placed on the ground rather than on "towers" or walls, such as spikes/slime/grinders, which varies things up quite a bit. Throughout the game, winning one level will unlock up to three more, and each level shows you its layout and what it unlocks upon completion before you even play it. There are over forty levels in the main game, some of which are required to progress, and some of which are optional and grant you gems (required to level up everything; they upgrade your traps, spells, and even how much gold/lives you start out with). Beating a level also unlocks the ability to replay it with runes, reminiscent of the Gemcraft series. Each rune offers a different challenge, such as additional enemy health/speed, and enabling a rune on a level and subsequently beating it offers you an XP multiplier, which helps you level up. Thus, if you ever get stuck on a level, there are multiple options at your disposal to allow you to earn XP to level with and try again.
I am past level 70, and there is no end in sight. Do not expect reachable level caps here. Even once all trap upgrade tiers are unlocked (they can upgrade to level four, granting additional benefits and abilities during the level) you can continue to upgrade them to cost less, trigger more often, etc. You could, technically, play this game forever, and keep upgrading your already powerful traps to become ridiculous.
Levels are varied and interesting, and even the environments change (from excavation/mining areas to tombs to ice levels). There is a level editor to create even more levels, as if the abundance here isn't already more of an offering than most games in the genre. The graphics are endearing and colorful, and the game does not shy away from pixelated gore, a DOS-era voice chiming in after a killstreak to comment, "Juicy!" The music here is fantastic. There is an Easter egg of sorts to be found by those of us who are fans of the tower defense genre in later levels, and there is a secret level to be found within the game. I encourage you to find it yourself; if you beat the game without finding it, the ending credits will tell you which level to go back to in order to search for it.
I haven't had this much fun with a tower defense game since Kingdom Rush Frontiers. I spent 40 hours in this game over the course of a week, and I didn't get bored. This will be a game I will revisit in the future, and I highly recommend it to tower defense and strategy fans. Upon beating it I immediately searched for more Valsar games to support, and was disappointed to find none. If the developer releases more games in the future, I will be supporting them for sure.

A simple WWII-themed sidescrolling shooter. There are 10 story levels, 3 of which include bosses at the end. Story is minimal and mediocre (somewhat meaningless cutscenes for the first few levels, a random extended cutscene of a plot twist, then more simple cutscenes that don't really develop the story), while controls, visuals and sound are decent. I think you play as a German soldier and there's this random sphere that does bad things that your leaders have taken. You then go on a quest to destroy the sphere.
It uses pretty simple AI that you can abuse. In levels with melee enemies, you just walk right to spawn them and then kite left to kill them. You can use the random exploding barrels to defeat groups at a time. At first I just pushed a barrel to the top/bottom of the screen then pushed it along to use at the next wave of enemies. When I got tired of that, the knife (melee AoE instakill for regular enemies) was a good choice to just end the level quickly. Later on, I found that rifles do well for clearing melee groups with their piercing shots of 'ultimate'-tier damage.
For ranged enemies, you have to avoid the fire and shoot back. Their bullets disappear after a certain distance and they don't follow you so you can just soak damage then retreat to regen to full hp. The stationary ones (like ones shooting from a vehicle) have a limited arc of fire and don't turn around so you can just heal next to them (or take your knife out for a melee finish). However, ranged enemies don't follow you so you can usually just run past them.
There are bosses at end of a few levels. You can tell because the finish circle (instead of ending the level) teleports you to an arena with a boss. The boss is a huge sack of hit points that you kite around in a circle to avoid its attacks.
When you complete a mission you get levels (experience) and money. Levels determine what great you can buy at the armory. There are 11 guns with ~10-11 skins for each gun. The skins are of varying prices but it doesn't change the damage class of the weapon (med/high/ultimate). The only thing it says changes sometimes is the magazine capacity.
Worth a look if you like simple sidescrollers with a WWII theme. It's alright but I feel there are better games out there. A better done and similar type of game (but not exactly the same) would be the Metal Slug series. There are a lot of well-made beat 'em/shoot 'em up games.
